# The Rising Dawn,

## that is:

### The Root or Mother

### Of

### Philosophy, Astrology, and Theology,

#### from a true foundation,

#### Or

# Description of Nature,

#### how all things have been

and came to be in the beginning:

how Nature and the Elements creatively came to be, also of both dualities, Evil and Good; from which all things have their origin, and how it now lives and works, and what it will become at the end of this time: also how God's Kingdom and the Kingdom of Hell are constituted, and how human beings work creatively in each.

All from a true foundation, set forth with diligence in elucidations of the Spirit in the Being of God.

J a c o b B ö h m e, in Görlitz, in the Year of Christ 1612. In the 37th Year of his Age, Tuesday in Pentecost. All newly revised, and with diligence compared and improved according to the Author's own Manuscript.

New Edition.

Berlin and Leipzig, 1780.
Christian Ulrich Ringmacher.

# Preface of the AUTHOR

## concerning this Book to the favorable Reader.

### Favorable Reader.

1. I compare the whole of Philosophy, Astrology, and Theology, together with their Mother, to a precious tree that grows in a beautiful cultivated garden.

2. Now the earth, wherein the tree stands, always gives the tree saps, from which the tree has its living quality: but the tree in itself grows from the sap of the earth, and becomes large, and spreads out with its boughs.

3. Now just as the earth with its power works on the tree, that the same might grow and increase, so the tree works always with its boughs with all its might, that it might always bring forth many good fruits.

4. But if the tree brings forth few fruits, thereto very small, meager, and worm-eaten, the fault is not in the tree's will, that the same should especially desire to bear evil fruits, because it is a precious tree of good quality; but the fault is, that often great blights, deposits, mildew, caterpillars and vermin fall upon it, for the quality in the depth, cast out from the stars, corrupts it, so that it brings forth few good fruits.

5. Now the tree has this nature in itself, that the larger and older the tree becomes, the sweeter fruits it bears: in its youth it bears few fruits, for the rough and wild nature of the soil, and the predominant fruitfulness in the tree, cause this: and though it already blossoms, yet fall

1. I compare the whole of philosophy, astrology, and theology <note>original: "Philosophiam, Astrologiam, und Theologiam"</note> together with their Mother <note>Likely referring to Nature or Divine Wisdom</note> to a precious tree that grows in a beautiful pleasure garden.

2. Now the earth, in which the tree stands, continually gives the tree sap, from which the tree derives its living quality <term>Qualität: in this author's system, this refers to a specific force, property, or "source-spirit" that defines the nature of a thing</term>: but the tree in itself grows from the sap of the earth, becomes large, and spreads itself out with its branches.

3. Now, just as the earth works with its power upon the tree so that it grows and increases, so the tree works constantly with its branches with all its might, that it might always bring forth many good fruits.

4. But if the tree brings forth little fruit, and moreover very small, maggoty, and worm-eaten, the fault is not in the tree's will—as if it intentionally desired to bear evil fruit, since it is a precious tree of good quality <term>Qualität: property or nature</term>; rather, the fault is that great cold, heat, mildew, caterpillars, and vermin often fall upon it, for the quality in the deep, cast down from the stars, corrupts it so that it brings forth little good fruit.

5. Now the tree has this nature in itself: that the larger and older the tree becomes, the sweeter the fruit it bears. In its youth it bears little fruit, for this is caused by the rough and wild nature of the soil and the excessive moisture in the tree; and even though it blossoms beautifully, they fall...

yet most of its apples fall off as they grow, unless it happens that it stands in very good soil.

6. Now the tree also has a good, sweet quality <term>Qualität: in this author's system, a specific force or "source-spirit" that defines a thing's nature</term> within it, but on the other hand also three others opposed to it: namely, bitter, sour, and harsh. Now, as the tree is, so also its fruits become, until the sun works upon them and makes them sweet, so that they receive a lovely taste; and its fruits must endure through rain, wind, and storms.

7. But when the tree becomes old, so that its branches wither and the sap can no longer rise up, then many green twigs grow out below around the trunk, and finally also upon the root, and they reveal the glory of the old tree—showing how it too was once a beautiful green twig and little tree, and has now grown quite old. For nature or the sap defends itself until the trunk becomes completely dry; then it is cut down and burned in the fire.

## Now observe what I have indicated with this parable:

8. The garden of this tree signifies the world; the field signifies nature; the trunk of the tree signifies the stars; the branches signify the elements <note>original: "Elementa"</note>; the fruits that grow on this tree signify human beings; the sap in the tree signifies the clear Godhead. Now humans have been made from nature, the stars, and the elements, but God the Creator rules in everything, just as the sap does in the entire tree.

9. Nature, however, has two qualities <term>Qualitäten: properties or source-forces</term> within it until the Judgment of God: one lovely, heavenly, and holy; and one fierce, hellish, and thirsty.

10. Now the good quality qualifies <term>qualificiret: to act or work according to its specific internal nature</term> and works always with all diligence so that it may bring forth good fruits; in this the Holy Spirit rules, and gives sap and life to it. The evil quality also wells up and drives with all diligence so that it always brings forth evil fruits; to this the Devil gives sap and hellish fire <note>original: "Loh," meaning a blazing flame</note>.

11. Now both of these are in the tree of nature, and human beings are made from the tree, and live in this world in this garden between both in great danger; and upon them falls now sunshine, now rain, wind, and snow.

### Of the Author.

12. ...Godhead, so the Holy Spirit wells up and works within <note>The original term "qualificiret" refers to the way different qualities or forces interact and manifest their nature within a person.</note> him; but if he lets his spirit sink into this world, into the lust of evil, then the devil and the hellish sap well up and rule within him.

13. Just as the apple on the tree becomes maggoty and worm-eaten when frost, heat, and mildew fall upon it, and it easily falls off and rots: so also is man, when he lets the devil with his poison rule within him.

14. Now, just as good and evil well up, rule, and exist in nature, so it is also in man: but man is God’s child, whom He made from the best core of nature, to rule in the good and to overcome the evil. Even though the evil clings to him, just as in nature the evil clings to the good, he can nevertheless overcome the evil; if he raises his spirit into God, the Holy Spirit wells up in him and helps him to be victorious.

15. Just as the good quality in nature is powerful enough to triumph over the evil, because it is and comes from God, and the Holy Spirit is the ruler within it: so also the wrathful quality <term>wrathful quality; original: "grimme Qualität," referring to the harsh, dark, or destructive force in Böhme's cosmology</term> is powerful enough to triumph in malicious souls, for the devil is a powerful ruler in wrathfulness, and is an eternal prince of the same.

16. But man has thrown himself into wrathfulness through the fall of Adam and Eve <note>original: "Hevå"</note>, so that evil clings to him; otherwise his wellspring and impulse would be in the good alone. But now it is in both, and is now as Saint Paul says: *Do you not know that to whom you present yourselves as slaves in obedience, you are that one’s slaves whom you obey, whether of sin leading to death, or of obedience leading to righteousness?* <note>original: Romans 6, verse 16</note>.

17. Because man has the impulse in both, he may reach for whichever he wants, for he lives in this world between both, and both qualities, evil and good, are in him; whichever one man surges <note>original: "wallet," suggesting a boiling or active movement</note> into, with that he is clothed, whether in holy or hellish power.

18. For Christ says: *My Father will give the Holy Spirit to those who ask Him for it,* <note>original: Luke 11, verse 13</note>. Also, God has commanded man to do good and forbidden the evil, and still daily allows preaching, calling, and crying out, to admonish man toward the good.

# Preface

By this, one clearly recognizes that GOD does not want evil, but rather wants His kingdom to come and His will to be done, as in heaven so also on earth.

19. Since man is poisoned by sin, so that the wrathful quality <term>wrathful quality; original: "grimme Qualität," referring to the harsh, dark, or destructive force in Böhme's cosmology</term> as well as the good rules within him, he is now half-dead. With great lack of understanding, he can no longer recognize GOD his Creator, nor nature and its workings <note>The word "Würkung" implies the active influence or "out-working" of natural forces.</note>. Therefore, Nature has applied its highest diligence from the beginning until today; to this end, GOD has given His Holy Spirit, so that she has always and in every way born and prepared wise, holy, and sensible men who have learned to recognize both nature and GOD their Creator. These have always been lights to the world through their writing and teaching. With them, GOD has prepared His church on earth for His eternal praise; in opposition, the devil has raged and stormed, spoiling many a noble branch through the wrathfulness in nature, of which he is prince and god.

20. Whenever Nature has prepared a learned, sensible man with beautiful gifts, the devil has applied his highest diligence to seduce him into fleshly lusts, into pride <note>original: "Hoffart," a traditional term for spiritual arrogance</note>, into the desire to be rich and to have power. Thereby the devil has ruled in him, and the wrathful quality has overcome the good. Out of his intellect, and out of his art and wisdom, heresies and errors have grown, which mocked the truth and caused great error on earth; thus he has been a good army commander for the devil.

21. For the evil quality in nature has struggled with the good from the beginning and still continues to do so, raising itself up and spoiling many a noble fruit in the mother’s womb. This can be clearly seen first with Cain and Abel, who came from one mother’s womb. Cain was a despiser of GOD and proud from the mother’s womb, whereas Abel was a humble, god-fearing man. One also sees this with the three sons of Noah, as well as with Abraham with Isaac and Ishmael, but especially with Isaac with Esau and Jacob, who pushed and struggled in the mother’s womb <note>original: "gestossen und gerungen"</note>, which is why GOD says: *Jacob I have loved, and Esau I have hated.* Genesis 25:23. This is nothing else than that

both qualities in nature have wrestled fiercely with one another.

22. For as GOD was stirring in nature at that same time, and wished to reveal Himself to the world through the pious **Abraham**, **Isaac**, and **Jacob**, and wished to prepare a church on earth for His glory and majesty, so also did wickedness and its prince **Lucifer** stir within nature. Because both evil and good were within man, both qualities could rule in him; therefore, an evil and a good man were born of one mother at the same time.

23. It is also clearly to be seen in the first world <note>The "first world" refers to the era before the Great Flood</note>, as well as in the second until the end of our time, how the heavenly and hellish kingdoms in nature have always wrestled with one another, and existed in great labor, like a woman in childbirth.

24. With **Adam** and **Eve**, it is most clearly seen; for there a tree grew in Paradise of both qualities, evil and good, where Adam and Eve were to be tested to see if they could persist in the good quality, in an angelic manner and form. <note>The original German "Englischer Art" refers to "angelic nature" (from *Engel*), not the English language or people.</note> Then the Creator forbade Adam and Eve to eat of the fruit, but the evil quality in nature wrestled with the good, and brought Adam and Eve into the desire to eat of both. Therefore, they soon received an animal-like nature and form, and ate of both evil and good, and had to multiply and live in an animal-like way, and many a noble branch born of them was corrupted.

24. <note>The original text repeats the number 24.</note> Afterward, one sees how GOD worked in nature when the holy fathers were born in the first world, such as **Abel**, **Seth**, **Enos**, **Cainan**, **Mahalaleel**, **Jared**, **Enoch**, **Methuselah**, **Lamech**, and the holy **Noah**: these proclaimed the name of the Lord to the world and preached repentance, for the Holy Spirit worked within them.

26. Conversely, the hellish god <note>A reference to Lucifer as the "god of this world" (2 Cor 4:4) or the personification of the wrathful quality.</note> also worked in nature and brought forth mockers and despisers, first of all **Cain** and his descendants: and it went with the first world as with a young tree, which grows, turns green, and blossoms beautifully, but brings forth little good fruit because of its wild nature. Thus, nature in the first world brought forth little good fruit, even though it blossomed beautifully in worldly art and luxury: for these things could not grasp the Holy Spirit, who worked in nature then just as He does now.

-># Preface<-

27. Therefore GOD said: it repents me that I have made man <note>original: "Genes. 6, 6." refers to Genesis 6:6</note> and stirred nature so that all flesh died that lived on dry land, down to the root and stem, which remained standing: and with this He fertilized and tended the wild tree, so that it should bear better fruits. But when it turned green again, it soon brought forth good and evil fruits again among the sons of Noah; there soon appeared mockers and despisers of God again, and hardly a single good branch grew in the tree that brought forth holy, good fruits; the other branches bore and brought forth the wild heathens.

28. But when God saw that man was thus dead in his knowledge <note>The author implies a loss of the spiritual "recognition" or "awareness" of the divine presence within nature.</note>, He moved nature once again and showed man how within it there were both evil and good, so that they might flee the evil and live in the good; and He let fire fall out of nature, and ignited Sodom and Gomorrah as a terrible example to the world.

29. But when man’s blindness gained the upper hand, and they would not let themselves be taught by God’s Spirit, He gave them laws and teachings on how they should conduct themselves, and confirmed these with wonders and signs, so that the knowledge of the true God might not be extinguished.

30. But even with this, the light would not come to light <note>The author uses "an Tag kommen" (to come to day), meaning to manifest or become visible.</note>, for the darkness and wrath in nature increased, and its prince <note>Referring to Lucifer or the personification of the "dark" quality of nature.</note> ruled powerfully.

31. But when the tree of nature reached its middle age <note>Böhme uses "Mittelalter" (middle age) here as a biological metaphor for the middle stage of the tree's growth, rather than the historical Medieval period.</note>, it then began to bear some mild, sweet fruits, to show that henceforth it would bear lovely fruits. For then the holy prophets were born from the sweet branch of the tree, who taught and preached of the light, which in the future would overcome the wrath in nature.

32. Also among the heathens a light arose within nature, so that they recognized nature and its workings, although this was only a light within wild nature, and not yet the holy light. For the wild nature was not yet overcome, and light and darkness wrestled with one another until the Sun rose, and forced this tree with its heat so that it bore lovely, sweet fruits.

33. That is, until the Prince of Light came from the heart of GOD, and became a man in nature, and wrestled in his human body, by the power of the divine light, within wild nature.

34. This same princely and royal branch grew up within nature and became a tree in nature; it spread its boughs from the East <note>original: "Orient"</note> to the West <note>original: "Occident"</note> and encompassed all of nature. It struggled and fought against the <term>fierce wrath<gloss>German: "Grimmigkeit." In Böhme's philosophy, this represents the harsh, bitter, and destructive quality in nature and the human soul that must be overcome by divine love.</gloss></term> that was in nature, and against its princes, until it triumphed as a King of nature. He took the Prince of Wrath captive in his own house, as noted in Psalm 68 <note>original: "Psalm 68." Likely referencing Psalm 68:18: "Thou hast ascended on high, thou hast led captivity captive."</note>.

35. When this occurred, many thousands of legions of precious, sweet little branches grew out of that royal tree which had grown in nature, and they all possessed the scent and taste of that precious tree. And even though rain, snow, hail, and tempests fell upon them, such that many a little branch was torn and struck down from the tree, other little branches always grew in their place. For the <term>fierce wrath</term> in nature and its prince stirred up great storms with hail, thunder, lightning, and rain, so that many magnificent little branches were indeed often torn from the sweet and good tree. But these same branches tasted so lovely, sweet, and full of joy that no tongue of man or angel can express it; for they held great power and virtue within them, serving for the healing of the wild <term>Gentiles<gloss>non-believers or those living in their "wild" natural state</gloss></term>. Whichever Gentile ate from the little branches of this tree was delivered from the wild nature into which he was born, and became a sweet branch in the precious tree; he flourished within the tree and bore precious fruit, just like the royal tree.

36. Therefore, many Gentiles ran to the precious tree where the precious branches lay—those which the Prince of Darkness had torn away with his stormy winds—and whichever Gentile caught the scent of these torn-off branches was healed from the wild <term>fierce wrath</term> that was born into him from his mother.

37. But when the Prince of Darkness saw that the Gentiles were scrambling for the branches and not for the tree itself, and saw his own great loss and damage, he ceased his storming from the East and the South <note>original: "Aufgang und Mittag," literally "Rising and Midday"</note> and placed a merchant under the tree. This merchant gathered up the little branches that had fallen from the precious tree.

38. And then, when the Gentiles came and asked for the good and powerful branches, the merchant offered the—

38. ...to sell the same fruit for money, so that he might take <term>usury<gloss>profiteering or excessive interest; here, exploiting spiritual gifts for financial gain</gloss></term> from the precious tree. For this is what the Prince of <term>Fierce Wrath<gloss>German: "Grimmigkeit." A central term in Böhme’s thought, referring to the harsh, bitter, and destructive quality of nature apart from God's light.</gloss></term> demanded of his merchant, because the tree had grown in his territory and was ruining his field.

39. Now when the <term>Gentiles<gloss>original: "Heyden." Those living in a natural, unredeemed state or non-believers.</gloss></term> saw that the fruits of the precious tree were for sale for money, they ran in crowds to the merchant and bought the fruit of the tree; they even came from distant islands to buy there, even from the ends of the earth.

40. When the merchant saw that his wares were so valuable and so well-pleasing, he devised a scheme to gather a great treasure for his lord. He sent out merchants into every land and had his wares offered for sale and highly praised. But he falsified the wares and sold other fruit as the good fruit—fruit that had not grown on the good tree—simply so that his lord's treasure might become great.

41. But the Gentiles and all the islands and peoples who dwelt on earth were all grown out of the wild tree, which was both good and evil. Therefore, they were half-blind and did not see the good tree—even though it stretched out its branches from the <note>original: "Aufgang" (Rising/East)</note> to the <note>original: "Niedergang" (Setting/West)</note>—otherwise, they would not have bought the false wares.

42. Because they did not know the precious tree, which nevertheless stretched its branches over them all, they all ran after the merchants and bought mixed, false wares for good ones, believing they served for their health. Yet, because they all hungered so fiercely for the good tree that hovered over them all, many of them were made healthy by the great longing and desire they bore toward the tree. For the scent of the tree, which hovered over them, made them healthy from their fierce wrath and wild birth, and not the merchant’s false wares; this lasted for a long time.

43. Now when the Prince in the Darkness—who is the source of fierce wrath, malice, and destruction—saw that people were becoming healthy from his poison and wild nature through the scent of the precious tree, he became angry and planted a

# Of the Author.

...wild tree toward the North <note>original: *Mitternacht* (midnight). Böhme uses compass points symbolically; North often represents the region of "grimness" or the source of cold, dark nature.</note>, which grew out of the <term>grimness (original: *Grimmigkeit*). In Böhme’s theology, this refers to the harsh, wrathful, or severe quality of nature that exists before it is tempered by God’s light and love.</term> of nature, and had it proclaimed: "This is the tree of life; whoever eats of it shall become healthy and live eternally." For in the place where the wild tree grew, it was a wild wasteland, and the peoples there had not recognized the true light from GOD from the beginning until that very time, nor even to this day. And the tree grew on Mount Hagar, in the house of Ishmael the mocker. <note>A biblical reference to Ishmael, son of Abraham and Hagar; in the 17th century, this was often used as an allegory for the Islamic world or those perceived as being outside the Christian covenant.</note>

44. 45. Because the people of this place had all grown out of wild nature, the tree grew over them all, and became so large that its branches reached even into the precious land, beneath the holy tree.

For they were far too faint and weak; they saw well enough that it was a wild, evil tree, but they were too exhausted and could not stop its growth. If they had not run after the merchants with the false wares and eaten of the false fruit, but had instead eaten of the precious tree, they would have become strong enough to offer resistance to the wild tree.

**65. That** the **people** at the **end** lusted so intensely for the **tree's root** is a **secret mystery** <note>original: "Geheimniß Mysterium"</note>, and has been hidden from the **clever and wise** until now. It will not rise up in the **heights**, but rather in the **depths** in great **simplicity**: just as the **noble tree** with its **core and heart** has always been hidden from the **world-wise**. Even though they thought they stood upon the **tree's root and peak**, it was nonetheless nothing more than a **bright mist** before their **eyes**.

**66. The noble tree**, however, has worked in **nature** with the highest diligence from the **beginning** until today, so that it might become manifest to all **nations, tongues, and languages**. Against this, the **devil** has raged and stormed in the **wild nature**, and defended himself like a **grim lion**. But the longer it took, the sweeter the fruits the **noble tree** brought forth, and it revealed itself more and more against all the raging and storming of the **devil** until the **end**, when it became light.

**67. Then** a **green branch** grew upon the **root** of the **noble tree**, and received the **root's sap and life**, and to it was given the **tree's spirit**, which explained the **noble tree** in its magnificent **strength and power**, as well as the **nature** in which it had grown.

**68. When** this happened, both **doors** opened in **nature**: the **knowledge** of both **qualities, evil and good** <note>Böhme’s "qualities" (Qualitäten) refer to the fundamental forces of the universe—the "dark" fire of wrath and the "light" fire of love</note>. And the **heavenly Jerusalem**, as well as the **kingdom of hell**, became manifest to all **people** on **earth**. And the **light** and the **voice** resounded into the **four winds**, and the **false merchant from the south** <note>original: "Mittage" (midday). This likely refers to the Roman Catholic Church or the corruption stemming from the southern reaches of Christendom</note> was completely exposed, and his own people hated him and uprooted him from the **earth**.

**69. When** this happened, the **wild tree toward the north** <note>original: "Mitternacht" (midnight). In Böhme's geography of the spirit, "north" often symbolizes the Protestant territories or the onset of a new spiritual era</note> also withered, and all **people** saw the **holy tree** even in distant **islands** with wonder. And the **prince in the darkness** was revealed, and his **secrets** were uncovered; and his **shame and mockery and ruin** were seen and recognized by the **people** on **earth**, for it had become light. But that lasted only a short **time**, and then the **people** abandoned the **light** and lived in the **lust of their flesh**.

# XXII
## Preface

...what GOD is, and how in the essence of GOD nature, stars, and elements are constituted, and from where all things have their origin, how heaven and earth are formed, as well as angels, humans, and devils, furthermore heaven and hell, and all that is created; also what both <term>qualities</term> <note>Böhme uses "quality" to mean a fundamental force or characteristic of being—specifically the tension between light/good and dark/wrath</note> in nature are, from the true foundation in the knowledge of the Spirit, in the impulse and surging of GOD.

85. 2. Through <term>Astrology</term> <note>original: *Astrologia*; for Böhme, this is not just horoscopes, but the study of the "astral" or celestial forces that operate within the human soul and the physical world</note> is treated the powers of nature, the stars, and the elements, how all creatures have come from them, and how they drive, govern, and work in everything, and how evil and good are worked through them in humans and animals: from which it arises that evil and good rule and exist in this world, and also how the kingdoms of hell and heaven exist within it.

86. It is not my intention to describe the course, position, or names of all the stars, or how they annually have their <term>conjunctions</term> or <term>oppositions</term> <note>original: *Gegenschein*</note> or <term>squares</term> and such things, or what they work every year and hour.

87. These things have been experienced through long passage of time by highly wise and clever, spirited people through diligent observation and attention, and deep thought and calculation. I have not studied or learned such things, and I leave them for the scholars to deal with; rather, my intention is to write according to the Spirit and the senses, and not according to outward observation.

88. 3. Through <term>Theology</term> <note>original: *Theologia*</note> is treated the kingdom of Christ, how it is constituted, how it is set against the kingdom of hell, and how it fights and struggles in nature with the kingdom of hell, and how humans through faith and the Spirit can overcome the kingdom of hell and triumph in divine power, and attain eternal salvation, and carry it away as a victory in the struggle. Also how humans, through the working of the hellish quality, throw themselves into ruin, and finally, how there will be an outcome for both.

89. The overarching title: **Day-Spring in the Rising** <note>original: *Morgenröte im Aufgang*; often Latinized as 'Aurora', this represents the first light of dawn breaking through the darkness of spiritual ignorance</note>, is a secret <note>original: *Mysterium*</note>, hidden from the clever and wise of this world, which they themselves will in short time—

<summary>Böhme outlines the three pillars of his work: Philosophy (the nature of God and creation), Astrology (the operation of cosmic forces in nature), and Theology (the spiritual struggle between the kingdoms of Christ and Hell). He emphasizes that his knowledge comes from spiritual revelation rather than academic study.</summary>

92. They did not ascend bodily into heaven and see everything with their eyes; rather, the Holy Spirit revealed itself within their spirit. Afterward, one sees in the second world <note>likely referring to the post-flood world or the era of the Law</note> also among the holy Patriarchs and Prophets, that they were all merely simple people, and many were only herdsmen.

93. Likewise, his apostles were all merely poor, despised fishermen and common folk. Indeed, Christ himself thanks his heavenly Father that He had hidden it from the clever and wise of this world and revealed it to the babes (Matthew 11).

95. Likewise, I can say nothing of myself, nor boast or write, except this: that I am a simple man, and moreover a poor sinner, and must pray every day: "Lord, forgive us our debts," and say with the Apostles: "O Lord, you have redeemed us through your blood." I have not ascended into heaven and seen all the works and creatures of **GOD**, but that same heaven is revealed in my spirit, so that I recognize the works and creatures of **GOD** in the spirit. Moreover, the will to do this is not my natural will, but it is the impulse of the Spirit; because of this, I have also had to suffer many a fall from the Devil.

# Interpretation of the Title Illustration
->concerning the<-
## AURORA. <note>original: "AURORAM." The Latin title for the "Day-Spring" or "Dawn," symbolizing the beginning of spiritual enlightenment.</note>

When a double dawn breaks at midnight, and two suns rise together, then a great and glorious day is at hand, and the Bridegroom is already approaching.

Six days are appointed for labor and tribulation, during which one may indeed catch their breath so that life and strength are preserved, but one must not rest until the evening of the sixth is over, nor rejoice until the seventh has begun.

And before such a day arrives, the <term>day’s works<note>original: "Tagewerke." This refers to the spiritual and physical actions performed by an individual during their lifetime.</note></term> of all six days—from the first to the last—are gathered and brought before the eyes of the Lord; He looks through everything everywhere with precision, noting what is corrupted, forgotten, or neglected, so that He may measure out to each person their reward according to their work; for on the seventh day, everything that was wrought in the six days must stand on display.

But so that no one might be rushed in their day’s work, the Lord measures out the short time of the earth with the <term>celestial compass<note>original: "Himmelscirkel." Likely referring to the divine measurement of time or the movement of the heavens.</note></term>, lets the sun stand still for a whole day, turns hours into years, and delays our short tribulation with His long-suffering patience, so that He may further us in all things toward perfect works and toward our joy on the Sabbath.

Therefore, He has the celebration announced early and calls out at this midnight: "Behold, the Bridegroom comes, go out to meet Him." Let everyone in their office prepare themselves with their works and keep ready: the servants on watch with their <term>increase<note>original: "Wucher." In this mystical context, it refers to the spiritual profit or "talents" gained through faithful service, rather than the modern negative sense of usury.</note></term>, and the virgins with trimmed lamps when the Lord and Bridegroom comes. Everything must be prepared and set in order, for whoever wishes to gather wood on the Sabbath day, or buy oil when the Bridegroom holds His wedding in the locked castle, shall be stoned and cast with mockery into the darkness, where there is wailing and <term>gnashing of teeth<note>original: "Zähnklappern." A traditional biblical depiction of the state of those excluded from the divine kingdom.</note></term>. To prevent this, He warns faithfully and says: "What I say to you, I say to all: Watch."

<summary>This page provides a mystical interpretation of the title illustration for the book "Aurora," using the metaphor of the Sabbath and the coming Bridegroom to emphasize the urgency of spiritual preparation. It warns that all human actions will be judged at the end of "six days" of labor before the eternal rest begins.</summary>
<keywords>Aurora, spiritual awakening, Sabbath, Bridegroom, divine judgment, celestial compass, vigilance</keywords>

## Chapter 1.

### On the Investigation of the Divine Being in Nature: Concerning Both Qualities.

->I.<-

1. Although flesh and blood cannot grasp the Divine Being <note>original: "göttliches Wesen." This refers to God's essential nature or substance, which Böhme argues is hidden from the physical senses.</note>, but rather the spirit does so when it is enlightened and ignited by God: yet, if one wishes to speak of God and what God is, one must diligently consider the powers in nature, as well as the entire creation of heaven and earth. This includes the stars and the elements, and the creatures that have come from them, as well as the holy angels, devils, and humans, and even heaven and hell.

2. In such contemplation, one finds two <term>qualities</term> <note>Boehme uses the word "quality" (Qualität) in a unique way to describe a fundamental property, power, or "source-spirit" that drives existence and gives a thing its character.</note>: a good one and an evil one. In this world, in all powers, in the stars and elements, as well as in all creatures, these two are intertwined in one another like a single thing; and no creature in the flesh exists in this natural life unless it possesses both qualities within itself.

3. Here one must now consider what the word <term>quality</term> means or is. A <term>quality</term> is the mobility, the welling up <note>original: "quallen." Böhme often links this word to both "Quelle" (a spring or source) and "Qual" (torment/tension), describing how forces surge and interact to create life.</note> or the driving of a thing, such as heat, which burns, consumes, and drives everything that comes into it that is not of its own property. Conversely, it enlightens and warms everything that is cold, wet, and dark, and makes the soft thing hard. However, it still contains two species <note>original: "Species," meaning types or manifestations.</note> within itself: namely, the Light and the Wrath <note>original: "Grimmigkeit." This refers to the fierce, harsh, or "dark" side of energy that exists before it is transformed into light.</note>, which are to be noted.

4. The Light, or the heart of the heat, is in itself a lovely, joyful sight, a power of life, an enlightenment and a vision of things that are far off. It is a piece or a spring of the heavenly Kingdom of Joy <note>original: "Freudenreich."</note>. It makes everything in this world living and mobile; all flesh, as well as trees, leaves, and grass, grows in this world through the power of the Light, and has its life therein, as in that which is Good.

->A<- 5. Con- <note>This catchword "Hin-" (translated as "Con-") refers to the first syllable of the first word on the following page, "Hingegen" (Conversely/On the other hand).</note>

<summary>This page introduces Böhme's fundamental concept that the Divine Being can be understood by observing the dual qualities of "good" and "evil" (or Light and Wrath) that exist within all natural things. He begins to define "quality" as a dynamic, driving force that animates the universe.</summary>

5. Conversely, it [the quality of heat] has <term>fierceness</term><note>original: "Grimmigkeit." Böhme uses this to describe the harsh, consuming, or "wrathful" energy in nature that exists alongside the gentle light.</note> within itself, so that it burns, consumes, and destroys. This same fierceness <term>wells up</term><note>original: "quellet." Böhme often links the word "quality" to the "welling" or "bubbling" of a spring (Quell), implying an active, flowing power.</note>, drives, and raises itself within the light, and makes the light mobile. They wrestle and struggle with one another in their twofold source as one single thing; indeed, it is one thing, but it has a twofold source.

6. Light exists in **God** without heat, but in Nature it does not; for in Nature all qualities are within one another as a single quality, according to the manner in which **God** is everything, and how everything originates and proceeds from Him. **God** is the Heart or the <term>wellspring</term> of Nature; from Him, all things arise.

7. Now, heat rules in all powers within Nature and warms everything, and is a source in all things; otherwise, if that were not so, the water would be far too cold, and the earth would freeze solid, and there would be no air.

8. Heat rules in all things—in trees, herbs, and grass—and makes the water mobile, so that through the water-source, herbs and grass grow out of the earth. Therefore, it is called a "quality," because it wells up in all things and raises everything up.

9. But the light within the heat gives power to all qualities, so that everything becomes lovely and full of bliss. Heat without light is of no use to the other qualities, but is instead a destruction of the Good, an evil source, for it destroys everything in the fierceness of the heat. Thus, the light within the heat is a living wellspring, into which the **Holy Spirit** enters, but not into the fierceness. Heat, however, makes the light mobile, so that it wells and drives—as one sees in winter, when the light of the sun is indeed upon the earth, but the rays of the sun's heat cannot reach the ground, and therefore no fruit grows.

### Of the Quality of Cold.

10. Cold is also a quality, just like heat. It <term>qualifies</term><note>original: "qualificirt." To Böhme, this means more than just a description; it refers to the active "working" or "operating" of a force within a creature.</note> in all creatures that have come from Nature, and in everything that moves within it—in humans, animals, birds, fish, worms, foliage, and grass. It is set in opposition to heat and operates within it as if they were one thing; however, it resists the fierceness of the heat and stills the heat.

11. But it [cold] also has two species within itself, which should be noted: namely, that it softens the heat and makes everything fine and lovely, and it is a quality of life in all creatures, for...

<summary>Böhme explains the symbiotic relationship between light and the "fierceness" of heat, noting that while God is pure light, nature requires the driving force of heat to function. He also introduces the quality of cold as a balancing force that tempers heat's destructive potential.</summary>

no creature can exist without the cold, for it is a welling, driving mobility in all things.

12. The second species is fierceness <term>Grimmigkeit: a central concept for Böhme, referring to the harsh, wrathful, or "dark" side of nature's forces which can be either destructive or the driving force of life</term>, for when it gains power, it suppresses everything and destroys everything just like heat; no life can exist in it if the heat does not resist it. The fierceness of the cold is a destruction of all life and a house of death, just as the fierceness of heat is.

## Of the Qualifying of Air and Water.
<note>original: *Qualificirung* — In Böhme's vocabulary, this refers to the way different fundamental properties (qualities) interact and manifest their specific characteristics in the natural world.</note>

13. **T**he air has its origin from heat and cold, for heat and cold drive powerfully from themselves and fill everything; from this comes a living and weaving movement. But when the cold softens the heat, then the quality of both becomes thin, and the bitter quality draws it together so that it becomes drop-like: the air, however, has its origin and greatest movement from heat, and the water from cold.

14. Now these two qualities struggle constantly with one another; heat consumes the water, and cold constrains the air. Now, however, air is a cause and spirit of all life and all movement in this world, whether it be in flesh or in everything that grows from the earth; thus everything has its life from the air, and nothing that moves in this world can exist without the air.

15. Water also wells up in all living and weaving things in this world; in the water consists the body of all things, and in the air the spirit, whether in flesh or in the plants from the earth: and both of these come from heat and cold, and they qualify <note>that is, they interact and function together</note> with one another as one thing.

16. But now, in both of these qualities, two special species are also to be noted: namely, the living and the deadly effect. Air is a living quality when it is gentle in a thing, and the Holy Spirit <note>original: *H. Geiſt*</note> rules in the gentleness of the air, and all creatures are joyful within it. But it also has the fierceness within itself, so that it kills and destroys through its cruel rising. Yet the qualifying takes its origin from the fierce rising, so that it wells and drives in all things, from which life has its origin and existence; therefore, both must be present in this life.

17. Water also has a fierce, deadly source in

## Of the Influences of the Other Qualities into the Three Elements: Fire, Air, and Water.

### Of the Bitter Quality.

19. The bitter quality is the heart in all life, just as in the air it draws the water together and also disperses it so that it becomes distinct <note>original: *scheidlich* — meaning separable or capable of being divided into distinct forms.</note>; so it is also in all creatures, as well as in the plants of the earth: for foliage and grass have their green color from the bitter quality. Now, if the bitter quality dwells gently in a creature, it is a heart or joy within it, for it separates all other evil influences and is a beginning or cause of joy or laughter.

20. For when it is moved, it makes a creature tremble and full of joy, and elevates the same with its whole body; for it is like a glimpse of the heavenly kingdom of joy, an elevation of the spirit, a spirit and power in all plants from the earth, a mother of life.

21. The <term>Holy Spirit</term> wells and drives mightily in this quality, for it is a part of the heavenly kingdom of joy, as I will prove hereafter. But it also has another <term>Species</term> <note>original: *Species* — Here used in the Latin sense of a "type," "aspect," or "manifestation" of a fundamental quality.</note> within itself, namely fierceness <note>original: *Grimmigkeit* — A central Böhmean term referring to the harsh, wrathful, or "dark" side of nature's forces.</note>, which is truly a house of death, a destruction of all good, a corruption and consumption of life in the flesh. For if it rises too much in a creature and ignites in the heat, it separates flesh and spirit, and the creature must die the death: for it wells up and ignites the element of fire, in which no flesh can endure in the great heat and bitterness. But if it ignites in the element of water and becomes welling therein, it brings the flesh into sickness and disease, and finally into death.

22. The sweet quality is the opposite of the bitter one, and is a gracious, lovely quality, a refreshment

->Of the Sour Quality.<-

23. The sour quality is set in opposition to the bitter and the sweet, and it tempers everything beautifully; it is a refreshment and quenching when the bitter and sweet qualities rise too high. it is a desire in the taste, a pleasure of life, a welling joy in all things, a desire, longing, and pleasure of the kingdom of joy, a quiet delight of the spirit—all this it tempers in all living and welling things. However, it also has within it a source of evil and destruction: if it rises too high or wells up too much in a thing so that it ignites, it gives birth to sadness and <term>melancholy</term> <note>one of the four humors, associated here with a spiritual "heaviness" or gloom</note>. In water, it produces a stench, becoming stagnant and foul <note>original: "rüricht und brüchicht," referring to the physical breakdown of stagnant water</note>, a forgetting of all good, a sadness of life, a house of death, a beginning of sorrow and an end of joys.

->Of the Harsh or Salty Quality.<-

It resists the rising of the bitter quality, as well as the sweet and sour, so that they do not ignite. It is a sharp quality, a pleasure of the taste, a source of life and joys. Conversely, it also contains fierceness and destruction: when it is ignited in the fire, it gives birth to a hard, tearing, stony nature, a fierce source, a destruction of life. # Chapter 2.
## Instruction on how one should contemplate the divine and natural essence.

1. All of this, as recounted above, is called **quality** for this reason: because everything in the depths above the earth, upon the earth, and within the earth <term>qualifies</term> <note>from the German "qualificiret"; in Böhme's vocabulary, this means to interact, influence, or operate together as a single system</note> with one another as a single thing. Yet, it possesses many kinds of power and effect, though there is only one mother from which all things come and well up. All creatures are made and have come from these qualities and live within them as in their mother. Likewise, the earth and stones have their origin there, and everything that grows out of the earth lives and wells up from the power of these qualities; no reasonable person can deny this.

2. This **twofold wellspring**, both evil and good in all things, stems entirely from the stars; for just as the creatures on earth exist in their quality, so too do the stars. For through a twofold wellspring, everything possesses its great mobility—running, racing, welling, driving, and growing.

3. For <term>gentleness</term> <note>original: "Sanftmuth"</note> in nature is a still rest, but <term>fierceness</term> <note>original: "Grimmigkeit"; the harsh, wrathful, or rigorous aspect of nature</note> in all powers makes everything mobile, running and racing, and moreover, procreating. For the driving qualities bring **desire** into all creatures, both for evil and for good, so that everything yearns for one another, mixes, increases, decreases, becomes beautiful, perishes, loves, and hates.

4. There is in all creatures in this world a good and an evil will and wellspring: in humans, beasts, birds, fish, worms, as well as in everything that exists—in gold, silver, tin, copper, iron, steel, wood, herbs, leaves, and grass—as well as in the earth, in stones, in the water, and in everything that one can investigate.

5. There is nothing in nature where both good and evil are not present; everything surges and lives in this **twofold drive**, whatever it may be—except for the holy angels and the fierce devils, for they are decided <note>meaning they are separated into their respective domains of pure good or pure evil</note>; and each lives, qualifies, and rules in his own quality.

<summary>Böhme explains that all of nature operates through a "twofold wellspring" of good and evil qualities derived from the stars, which drive all growth and movement. He asserts that everything in the material world is a mixture of these opposing forces, unlike the permanently separated realms of angels and demons.</summary>

## Chap. 2. Aurora: The Dawning of the Day.

The holy angels live and <term>qualify</term><note>In Böhme’s vocabulary, 'qualify' (qualificiren) means to interact with, take on the properties of, or operate within a specific force or 'quality' of nature.</note> in the light within the good quality, where the Holy Spirit rules: the devils live and rule in the fierce quality, in the quality of wrath and anger or ruin.

6. Both evil and good angels were made from the qualities of Nature, from which all things have come; it is only the manner of their qualifying that is unequal.

7. The holy angels live in the power of the gentleness of the light and the kingdom of joy; but the devils live in the power of the rising or elevating <term>source-torment</term><note>original: 'Quall'. A word invented by Böhme to combine 'Qual' (torment) and 'Quelle' (source/wellspring), suggesting a state where one's very existence is a welling source of pain.</note> of fierceness, terror, and darkness. They cannot grasp the light, for they cast themselves out of it through their own self-exaltation, as I shall write later concerning the Creation.

8. If you do not wish to believe that everything in this world originates from the stars, I will prove it to you—provided you are not a blockhead and possess a little reason—so mark what follows.

9. First, look at the Sun; it is the heart or the King of all stars, and it gives light to all stars from their rising to their setting. It illuminates everything and warms everything; all things live and grow in its power, and the joy of all creatures resides in its power.

10. If the Sun were taken away, everything would become entirely dark and cold. No fruit would grow, and neither human nor beast would be able to multiply, for the heat would be extinguished, and the seed in all things would become cold and frozen.

### Concerning the Sun’s Quality.

11. If you wish to be a philosopher and a student of nature, and to investigate God’s being in nature—how all this is constituted—then pray to God for His Holy Spirit, that He may enlighten you with the same.

12. For in your flesh and blood you cannot grasp such things; even if you read about them, it is only a vapor or darkness before your eyes. Only in the Holy Spirit, who is in God and also in all of Nature from which all things have come, can you search even into the whole body of God—which is Nature—as well as into the Holy Trinity. For the Holy Spirit goes out from the Holy Trinity and rules in the whole body of God; that is, in all of Nature.

# Aurora: The Dawning of the Day. Chap. 2.

13. Just as the spirit of a person rules within the whole body in all the veins and fills the entire human being, so also the Holy Spirit fills the whole of Nature and is the heart of Nature; it rules in the good qualities in all things. If you now have that same Spirit within you, so that it enlightens and fills your spirit, then you will understand what is written here following. But if not, it will happen to you as it did to the wise heathens, who lost themselves in the Creation and wanted to explore it out of their own reason. In their <note>original: 'tichten', meaning mental devising or poetic contemplation</note> thoughts they came right before God’s face, and yet could not see it, and were stone-blind in the knowledge of God. Just as the children of Israel in the wilderness could not look upon the face of Moses, so that he had to put a veil over his face when he stepped before the people. This was because they did not understand or know the true God and His will, even though He walked among them; therefore the veil was a sign and a prototype of their blindness and lack of understanding. Just as a piece of work cannot grasp its master, so little can a human being grasp and know God his Creator, unless the Holy Spirit enlightens him. This happens only to those who do not trust in themselves but place their hope and will in God alone, and walk in the Holy Spirit; these are one Spirit with God.

14. If one now wishes to rightly consider the sun and stars with their <term>corpus</term><note>Latin for 'body'</note>, effects, and qualities, one finds the divine being rightly within them, in that the powers of the stars are Nature.

15. If one considers the whole <term>curriculum</term><note>Latin for 'course' or 'circuit'</note> or the entire orbit of the stars, one soon finds that it is the mother of all things, or Nature, from which all things have come to be, and in which all things stand and live, and through which everything moves. All things are made from those same powers and remain in them eternally. And though they will be transformed at the end of this time, when the good and evil shall be separated, nevertheless angels and humans will exist eternally in God, in the power of Nature from which they took their first beginning.

16. But you must here lift up your mind into the spirit and consider how all of Nature with all the powers that are in Nature—as well as the width, depth, height, heaven, earth, and all that is in them, and even above the heaven—is the Body of God!

The entrails or intestines signify the working or "consumption" of the stars: everything that has been produced by their power, everything they have made, they consume again, and it remains within their power. Thus, the intestines are also the consumption of all that which the human pushes into them—everything that has grown from the power of the stars.

Joy also has just such a wellspring, and from this same substance as wrath. That is, when the gall ignites in the loving or sweet quality—in that which is dear to the human being—then the whole body trembles for joy: in which the Siderial spirits are also sometimes infected when the gall rises too much and ignites in the sweet quality.

And as Isaiah writes of him: *He is Wonderful, Counselor, Power, Hero, Eternal Father, Prince of Peace* (Isaiah 9:6).

40. The **bitter quality** is also in God, but not in the same manner as the gall in humans; rather, it is an everlasting power, a sublime, triumphing wellspring of joy.

# Chap. 2. Morning-Redness in the Rising.

41. And although it is written in Moses: (Exodus 20. Deuteronomy 4. verse 24.) *I am an angry, jealous God*: <note>original: "Ich bin ein zorniger, eiferiger GOtt"</note> yet it is not meant to imply that God becomes angry within himself, or that a fire of wrath arises within the Holy Trinity. No, that cannot be; for it is written: *upon those who hate me*—it is within those same creatures that the fire of wrath arises.

42. For if God were to become angry within himself, then all of nature would burn. This will indeed happen once on the Last Day within nature, but not in God; in God, the triumphing joy shall burn, just as it has never been otherwise from eternity, nor shall it ever be otherwise.

43. Now, however, the elevating, surging <note>The original German "quallende" is a technical term for Böhme, blending the meanings of *Quelle* (source/fountain) and *Qual* (quality/vibration/agony), describing the inner life-force of a thing</note>, triumphing joy in God makes the heavens triumphing and mobile, and the heavens make the stars and elements mobile, and the stars and elements make the creatures mobile.

44. Out of the powers of God the heavens came to be; out of the heavens the stars came to be; out of the stars the elements came to be; out of the elements the earth and the creatures came to be. Thus everything has its beginning—including the angels and devils, who were made before the creation of the heavens, the stars, and the earth, from the same power out of which the heavens, stars, and earth were made.

45. This is therefore a brief introduction or guide on how one should contemplate the divine and natural <term>Being</term> <note>German: *Wesen*; refers to the inner essence or "substance" of reality</note>. Henceforth I will now describe the true ground and depth of what God is, and how all things are constituted within the Being of God.

46. This has indeed remained partly hidden from the world until now, and man has not been able to grasp it with his reason. But because God wishes to reveal Himself in simplicity in these latter times, I let His impulse and will flow; I am but a tiny spark. Amen.

## The 3. Chapter.

### Concerning the highly blessed, triumphing, holy, holy, holy Trinity, GOD the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, one GOD.

1. Kind Reader, here I would have you faithfully warned that you should let go of your conceit <note>or intellectual pride</note> and not...

...lose yourself in pagan wisdom, nor be offended by the simplicity of the author, for the work is not of his reason, but the impulse of the Spirit. <note>Böhme, a shoemaker by trade, frequently reminds readers that he lacks formal academic training and that his insights come from direct divine revelation rather than "pagan" (classical/secular) philosophy.</note> See only that you have the Holy Spirit, who proceeds from God, within your spirit; He will lead you into all truth and reveal Himself to you. Then, in His light and power, you will clearly see even into the Holy Trinity, and understand what is written hereafter.

->Of God the Father.<-

2. When our Savior Jesus Christ taught his disciples to pray, he said: "When you wish to pray, say: Our Father, who art in heaven." (Matthew 6). This is not meant to be understood as if heaven could grasp or encompass the Father, for he is himself made from the divine power.

3. For Christ says: "My Father is greater than all." (John 10:29). And in the Prophet, God says: "Heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool" (Isaiah 66). Likewise, "What kind of house will you build for me? I encompass the heaven with a span <note>A 'span' is the distance from the tip of the thumb to the tip of the little finger.</note>, and the earth with a measure." <note>original: "Dreylinge" - refers to a small coin or a 'third-part' measure.</note> (Isaiah 40:12). Likewise, "In Jacob I will dwell, and Israel shall be my tent." (Psalm 135:4, Sirach 24:13).

4. But that Christ calls his Father a "Heavenly Father," he means that his Father's brilliance and power appear completely clear, bright, and pure in heaven. Beyond the circle or boundary <note>original: "Cirk oder Schluß"</note> that we see there with our eyes—which we call heaven—there appears the entire triumphing, Holy Trinity: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.

5. Furthermore, Christ hereby distinguishes his Heavenly Father from the "Father of Nature," which is the stars and the elements. These are our natural father, out of which we are made, and in whose impulse we live here in this world, and from whom we take our food and nourishment.

6. However, he is our Heavenly Father so that our soul may constantly yearn for him and desire him; indeed, it constantly thirsts and hungers for him. The body hungers and thirsts after the Father of Nature—which are the stars and elements—and that same father also feeds and gives it drink. But the soul thirsts and hungers after the heavenly, holy Father, and he feeds and gives it drink with his Holy Spirit and <term>Source-Spring of Joy</term>. <note>German: "Freudenquall." A characteristic Böhme term combining "Quelle" (source/spring) and "Qual" (quality/vibration/life-force), implying an active, bubbling wellspring of divine life.</note>

7. Now, however, we do not have two fathers, but only one—

He distinguishes between the "Heavenly Father" who nourishes the soul and the "Father of Nature" (stars and elements) who provides for the physical body.</summary>

### Concerning the Substance and Attribute of the Father.

8. When one now considers all of nature and its attribute, then one sees the Father: when one looks upon the heaven and the stars, one sees his eternal power and wisdom. Just as many stars as stand under the heaven—which are indeed innumerable and incomprehensible to human reason, and some even invisible—so manifold and of so many kinds is the power and wisdom of **GOD** the Father.

9. Each star in the heaven has a different power and <term>quality</term><note>Böhme uses the word "quality" to mean an active force or a "source-spring" of a specific characteristic, rather than just a passive trait.</note> than the other, which also creates so many differences in and among the creatures on Earth, throughout the entire creation. Now, however, all powers that are in nature originate from **GOD** the Father: such as light, heat, cold, air, water, and all the powers of the earth—bitter, sour, sweet, harsh, hard, soft, and that which cannot be recounted—all of this has its origin and exit from the Father.

10. But if one wishes to compare the Father to something, one must compare him to the round sphere of the heaven: yet you must not think that each power that is in the Father stands in a particular part or place in the Father, like the stars in the heaven; no, instead the Spirit shows that all powers in the Father are in one another, like a single power, of which one has an image in the Prophet Ezekiel, in the 1st chapter. He sees the Lord in the Spirit and as a symbolic vision like a wheel, where four wheels are within one another, and all four were like each other; and when they went, they went straight ahead, whichever way the wind went, there all four went ahead, and none needed to turn. So also is **GOD** the Father, for all powers in the Father are in one another like one power, and all powers exist in the Father in an unsearchable light and clarity.

11. You must not think that **GOD** stands and moves in the heaven and above the heaven perhaps like a power and quality that has no reason or knowledge in itself—like the sun, which runs around in its <term>circuit</term><note>original: "Cirk"</note> and pours out from itself heat and light, whether it brings harm or benefit to the earth and the creatures, which indeed happens when the...

12. He is, however, from eternity to eternity thus unchangeable; He has never changed in His being, nor will He change for all eternity. He has come from nothing and was born of nothing, but is Himself All in eternity; and everything that exists has come from His power, which goes out from Him. Nature and all <term>creatures</term><note>In Böhme’s vocabulary, "creature" refers to any created being, including humans, animals, and angels.</note> have come from His power, which has gone out from Him from eternity: no creature, nor even an angel in heaven, can search out His breadth, height, and depth; instead, the angels live in the Father’s power quite gently and full of joy, and always sing within the Father’s power.

### Concerning God the Son.

13. If one now wishes to see **GOD** the Son, one must again look upon natural things; otherwise, I cannot write of Him. The Spirit sees Him well, but one cannot speak or write of it, for the divine being consists in power, which does not allow itself to be written or spoken. We must therefore use parables for ourselves if we wish to speak of **GOD**, for in this world we live in <term>piece-work</term><note>original: "Stückwerk". A reference to 1 Corinthians 13:9, "For we know in part," suggesting that human understanding is currently fragmented and incomplete compared to the divine whole.</note>, and were made out of piece-work. I would therefore have the reader summoned to that other life; there I will speak with him more properly and clearly regarding this high <term>article</term><note>A formal point of doctrine or belief.</note>: in the meantime, let the dear reader look to the sense of the Spirit, and it will not fail; he will also receive a little taste of power from it, if only he hungers for it.

The Son sees, hears, tastes, feels, smells, and understands everything that the Father is; he lives in his power and is everything that is good, just as in the Father, but evil is not in him.

27. The three elements—Fire, Air, and Water—have a threefold movement or *qualification* <term>original: "qualificirung"; in Böhme’s thought, this refers to the active, vital interaction where qualities (like heat or light) influence and "qualify" one another to create life</term>, but only one *body* <note>original: "Corpus"</note>. 28. Just as the three elements—Fire, Air, and Water—proceed from the sun and stars, and are one *body* <note>original: "Corpus"</note> within each other, and create the living movement and the spirit of all creatures in this world: so too the Holy Spirit proceeds from the Father and the Son, and creates the living movement in all the powers of the Father. And just as the three elements surge in the *deep* <note>The "deep" (die Tiefe) is Böhme’s term for the boundless space of the universe which he views as filled with God’s presence</note> as an independent spirit, and create heat, cold, and clouds, and flow out of the power of all the stars—and all the powers of the sun and stars are in the three elements as if they were themselves the sun and stars, from which the life and spirit of all creatures then arises and consists: so the Holy Spirit proceeds from the Father and the Son, and surges within the whole Father, and is the life and spirit of all powers within the whole Father.

### On the Holy Trinity.

32. 33. The Father is the whole divine power, from which all creatures have come to be, and has always been from eternity; he has no beginning nor end. The Son is in the Father, the Father’s heart or light, and the Father begets the Son from eternity to eternity forevermore, and the Son’s power and splendor shines back in the entire Father, just like the sun in the whole world.

34. Now the Son is a different <term>Person|a distinct expression or 'subsistence' within the one divine essence</term> than the Father, but not outside of the Father, and also no other God than the Father; his power, luster, and omnipotence is in no way less than the whole Father.

### Concerning the Divine Quality.

4. That is a true glimpse of the divine quality, as the quality is in **GOD**; in **GOD**, everything is spirit.

In **GOD**, there is no beginning nor end; the angels, however, have a beginning and an end <note>In Böhme's thought, "end" implies a boundary or a finite, defined shape</note>, though not in a way that is measurable or comprehensible to us. For an angel can be large at one moment and small the next; their swift change is as fast as human thoughts. All qualities and powers are present in an angel, just as they are in the entire Godhead.

32. You must understand this correctly: they are made and shaped from the Salitter and Mercurio—that is, from the "rising" <note>the dawn or emergence of divine power</note>. Consider this comparison: the elements come forth from the sun and stars, and they create a living spirit in the <term>Salnitter</term> of the earth. The stars remain in their orbit, and yet the spirit receives the quality of those stars.

33. Now, the spirit is a distinct thing after its assembly <note>original: *Zusammenfügung*</note> and has a substance just like all the stars, yet the stars are and remain distinct, each one free for itself. Nevertheless, the quality of the stars rules within that spirit, but the spirit can and may raise or lower itself within its own qualities, or it may live within the influences of the stars as it chooses, for it is free; it has received the qualities it carries within itself as its own property.

34. And even if it originally received them from the stars, they are now its own—just as when a mother has the seed within her, because she possesses it and because it is a seed, it belongs to the...

38. In the same way, **GOD** may withdraw his divine power, which is outside the angels, when they rise up against him. But when that happens, a spirit must waste away and perish, just as when the air—which is also his mother—is withdrawn from a human, he must die; so also the angels cannot live without their mother.

# Chapter 5.
## Concerning the bodily Substance, Being, and Property of an Angel.

<gloss>n</gloss>
Here now is the question: What kind of body, form, or shape does an angel have, or how are they shaped?
Just as a human is created in **GOD'S** image and likeness, so also are the angels; for they are the brothers of humans, and in the resurrection humans will have no other form and image than the angels, as our King **Christ** himself testifies (Matthew 22:30 <note>In this verse, Jesus states that in the resurrection, people are "like the angels of God in heaven."</note>). Also, the angels here on earth have never revealed themselves to humans in any other form than in human form.

### Concerning the Qualification <note>Böhme uses "qualification" (German: *Qualificirung*) to describe the internal movement, character, and interaction of spiritual forces and properties within a being.</note> of an Angel.

19. Now the question is: what kind of qualification does an angel have?

->Answer.<-

The holy soul of man and the spirit of an angel are of one substance and essence; there is no difference in this, except only for the quality itself in its bodily governance. That which qualifies from the outside into man through the air has a corrupted, earthly quality; on the other hand, however, it also has a divine and heavenly quality, hidden from the creatures, but the holy soul understands this well, as the royal prophet David says: *The Lord rides upon the wings of the wind* <note>original: *der Herr fähret auf den Fittigen des Windes* (Psalm 104:3)</note>. In the angel, however, the divine quality qualifies, entirely holy, divine, and pure.

20. But a simple person might ask: what do you mean by "qualifying"? Or what is that? By this, I mean the power that enters into the body of the angel from the outside and goes out again, as in a comparison: when a man draws breath and lets it go from him again; for therein stands the life of the body and also of the spirit.

21. The quality from the outside kindles the spirit in the heart in the first fountain-spring, by which all powers in the entire body are stirred: then that same quality rises up in the bodily spirit—which is the natural spirit of the angel or man—into the head; there it has its **princely seat** <term>princely seat: German *fürstlicher Stul*, representing the center of consciousness, intellect, and authority in the brain</term> and governance, and has its councils there, according to which it directs itself and acts.

22. Just as the light goes out from the Son of God into the entire Father, into all powers, and influences all the powers of the Father, and in turn, all the powers of the Father influence the light of the Son of God, from which the Holy Spirit arises.

### Chapter 5. Morning-Redness in the Ascent.

Counsel also rises with all the powers of the <term>Body</term> <note>original: "Corpus"</note> in the spirit into the head. For just as from **God** the Father and Son all powers go forth into the Holy Spirit, and one stirs <note>Böhme uses "rüget," an archaic term meaning to set in motion, affect, or stimulate</note> the other, from which the sound or <term>Mercury</term> <note>original: "Marcurius," referring to the alchemical principle of movement, sound, and communication</note> arises, so that all powers resound and move: otherwise, if one did not stir the other, nothing would move, and this stirring makes the Holy Spirit mobile, so that He rises in all powers and stirs all the powers of the Father. Within this, the heavenly kingdom of joy or triumph arises, as well as sounding, ringing, birthing, blooming, and growing; all of this has its ascent from the fact that one power stirs another. For Christ says in the Gospel: I work, and my Father also works. (John 5, verse 17.) By this "stirring" or "working" He means that all power goes out from Him and gives birth to the Holy Spirit, and in the Holy Spirit all powers are already active <note>original: "räge," meaning stirred or in motion</note> from the proceeding of the Father. Therefore, the Holy Spirit wells up and rises from eternity to eternity, and in turn ignites all the powers of the Father and makes them active, so that they are always pregnant.

34 This has exactly the same form in angels and humans, for all powers in the <term>Body</term> rise up, and one stirs the other, otherwise the angel and human would feel nothing. But if even one limb is moved too much, it cries out to the whole body for help, and the whole body stirs itself, like a great riot, as if an enemy were present, and comes to the help of that same limb and delivers it from the pain. You can see this if you only knock a finger hard, bruise it, or wound it—or wherever it may be in a limb—the spirit soon runs from that place to the mother, the heart, and complains to the mother. And if the pain is even slightly great, the mother awakens all the members of the whole body, and everything must come to the aid of that limb.

35. Now note, in this way one power stirs the other without ceasing in the whole <term>Body</term>, and all powers rise into the head before the princely council, which approves the stirring of all powers. If one limb stirs itself too much and does harm to any princely councilor—as through the sense of sight, wanting to love that which is not fitting for it, as Lord <term>Lucifer</term> did, who saw the Son of **God** and loved the high light, and moved and stirred himself too much, intending to become equal to Him or even more beautiful and higher—the councilors abolish such stirrings.

## How an Angel and Human are God’s Likeness and Image.

## Of the Mouth.

10. The mouth signifies that you are an un-almighty <note>Meaning humans and angels are not self-sufficient sources of power, but must receive it from God.</note> son of your father, whether you be an angel or a human; for through the mouth you must draw your father’s power into yourself if you wish to live. 11. 12. 13. 16. For heaven has only one form: nothing grows there that is not good. Only Lord **Lucifer** has prepared this world in such a <note>corrupted</note> way. That is why Mother **Eve** was ashamed when she had eaten of that which was prepared by the evil quality; likewise, she was ashamed of her reproductive organs, which had been prepared for her through this bite of the apple.

17. Now, the angelic and heavenly fruit does not have such a <note>shameful or corrupt</note> substance; there are indeed and truly all kinds of fruits in heaven, and not just symbols. The angels take them with their hands and eat them, like we humans do, but they need no teeth for it, nor do they have any, for the fruit is of divine power.

18. Their <term>body<note>original: "Corpus"</note></term> is indeed their property, for **GOD** has given it to them as a possession; and whatever is given to someone as their own or as a property is theirs by natural right. ## Chapter 7.
### Concerning the territory, place, and dwelling, as well as the government <note>original: "Regiment"; refers to the ordered rule or dominion of spiritual beings</note> of the angels, how it stood in the beginning after the creation, and how it has thus become.

->1.<-

Here the Devil will defend himself like a snarling dog, for his shame will be uncovered here, and he will give the reader many a hard blow, and always cast it into doubt, suggesting it is not so. For nothing hurts him more than when one throws his former glory back at him—how he was once such a beautiful prince and king. When this is thrown at him, he rages and storms as if he wanted to assault the world.

2. Now, if a reader should come upon this chapter in whom the fire of the Holy Spirit might be somewhat weak, I truly fear the Devil will beset him and incite him to doubt whether it truly is as it is written, so that his kingdom might not stand so completely exposed, and his shame not be so entirely uncovered. If he can bring this to doubt in just one heart, he will not fail to use all his art, trouble, and labor; I see clearly beforehand that he has this in his mind.

3. Therefore, I wish to have warned the reader to read it with diligence, and to have patience until he comes to the creation and the <term>governments</term> <note>original: "Regimente"; the structured hierarchies of power and order in the universe</note> of this world; then he will find it proved brightly and clearly from nature.

->Now mark:<-

4. When **GOD** the Almighty resolved in His counsel that He would make angels or creatures out of Himself, He made them out of His eternal power and wisdom, according to the form and manner of the **Trinity** in His Godhead, and according to the qualities in His divine being.

5. First, He made three royal governments, according to the number of the Holy Trinity, and each kingdom had the order, power, and quality of the divine being.

6. Here, lift up your mind and spirit into the depths of the Godhead, for here a door is being opened.

## Chapter 8.

### Concerning the whole Body <note>original: "Corpus"</note> of an Angelic Kingdom; the Great Mystery.

The angelic kingdoms are formed throughout according to the divine essence, and have no other shape than the divine essence has in its Trinity <note>original: "Dreyheit"</note>. The only difference is this: that their bodies are creatures that have a beginning and an end, and that the kingdom in which they have their territory <note>original: "Revier," a term for a district or precinct</note> is not their physical property, which they possess by natural right <note>original: "Naturrecht"</note> as they possess their own bodies by natural right. Rather, the kingdom belongs to **GOD** the Father; He has made them out of His powers and may place them wherever He wishes. Otherwise, their body is made according to all and out of all the powers of the Father. And their power begets the light and knowledge within them, just as **GOD** begets His Son out of all His powers; and just as the Holy Spirit proceeds from all the powers of the Father and the Son, so also in an angel, their spirit proceeds from their heart, from their light, and from all their powers.

2. Now observe: just as an angel is constituted in his physical body with all members, so too is a whole kingdom constituted; it is together like one angel.
