Furthermore, it is the formation of all kinds of red colors in its own quality; in the sweet [quality] it forms all kinds of white and blue; in the harsh and sour [qualities] all kinds of green and dark and mixed colors with various shapes and scents.

28. The bitter quality is the first spirit from which life becomes active, from which mobility takes its origin; it is rightly called the *Heart* <note>original Latin: *Cor*</note>, for it is the trembling, stirring, elevating, penetrating spirit—the triumphing or joy, an elevating source of laughter. In the sweet quality, the bitter is gentled so that it becomes entirely lovely and joyful. But if it is elevated, moved, or ignited too much, then it ignites the sweet and harsh qualities and acts like a tearing, stinging, and burning poison—just as when a person has a tearing pestilential boil, from which they cry "ah!" and "woe!"

### Now mark the end of nature in this world.

48. Now, when the sweet *quality* thus flees from the bitter, sour, and harsh, the harsh and bitter hasten after it as their best treasure; and the sweet pushes so violently away from them, and struggles so intensely to break through the harsh *quality*, that it tears open the *Body* <note>original: "Corpus"</note> and escapes out from the *Body* out and above the earth, and hurries so hard until a long stalk grows.

49. Then the heat above the earth pushes upon the stalk, and the bitter *quality* is then ignited by the heat, and receives a jolt from the heat so that it is startled, and the harsh *quality* dries it out: there the harsh, sweet, and bitter, and the heat, contend with one another; and the harsh in its coldness always creates its dryness, and then the sweet gives way to the side, and the others hasten after it.

50. But when it sees that it is to be captured, that the bitter presses so hard upon it, and the heat from outside also presses upon it, it makes the bitter fervent and ignites it: then it makes a leap through the harsh *quality*, and rises again above itself; then a hard knot <note>a node or joint in a plant stalk</note> forms behind it at the place where the struggle was, and the knot gets a small hole.

51. But when the sweet *quality* leaps through the knot, it has so severely *influenced* <note>original: "inficiret"; literally "infected," but Böhme uses it to mean a spiritual or chemical permeation</note> the bitter that it is quite trembling, and as soon as it gets past the knot, it quickly expands on all sides, intending to flee the bitter: and in such expansion, its body remains hollow in the middle, and in that trembling leap through the knot it gains even more stalks or foliage, and is now joyful that it has escaped the war.

52. And now, when the heat from outside thus presses upon the stalk, the *qualities* in the stalk are ignited, and push through the stalk, and are *permeated* <note>original: "inficiret"</note> in the external light by the sun, and bring forth the colors in the stalk according to the nature of their *quality*.

# The Aurora at its Rising. Chapter 8.

53. Because the sweet water is within the stalk, the stalk retains its greenish color, according to the nature of the sweet *quality* <note>In Böhme’s system, "qualities" are the fundamental forces—sweet, bitter, sour, harsh—that make up all matter.</note>.

54. The qualities, together with the heat, carry out such activity within the stalk, and the stalk grows continuously, enduring one struggle after another. 55. Then the sweet quality allows itself to be captured. The bitter, sour, sweet, and harsh then rule together among one another. The sweet quality still expands a little, but it can no longer escape, for it is imprisoned.

56. Then, out of all the qualities within the <term>Body</term> <note>original: "Corpus"</note>, a head or bud grows, and a new body forms within that head. It is shaped <note>original: "figuriret"</note> just as the root was in the earth at first, except that it now takes on a different, more subtle form.

57. Then the sweet quality gently pushes outward, and small, subtle leaves grow in the head; these are of the nature of all the qualities. For the sweet water is now like a pregnant woman who has received the seed, and she pushes outward until she bursts the head open.

58. Then she also pushes forth through the little leaves, like a woman giving birth. But the little leaves or blossoms no longer have just her color and shape, but rather those of all the other qualities; for the sweet quality must now give birth to the children of the other qualities. And when the sweet mother has given birth to the beautiful green, blue, white, red, and yellow blossoms or children, she becomes quite weary and can no longer nourish these children. Nor can she keep them for long, because they are only her stepchildren, which are very delicate.

59. ### Aurora in the Dawning. Chapter 8.

75. That is, when you say **B a r**, the last letter R purrs <note>German: *kirret*. Now behold, when you say **B a r m**, the two qualities—the astringent and the bitter—form the word **B a r m** very slowly together; for it is a long, powerless syllable because of the weakness of those qualities. But when you say **Herz**, the spirit in the word **Heart** flashes out as quickly as lightning and gives the word its distinction and understanding. And when you say **Ig** <note>The suffix *-ig* in German turns the noun into an adjective, similar to "-ly" or "-y" in English.</note>, you catch the spirit in the midst of the other two qualities, so that it must remain within and form the word.

78. The divine power is just like this: the astringent and bitter qualities are the **Salitter** <term>Salitter|A term Böhme adapted from "saltpeter" to describe the "divine matter" or the fundamental substance of God's powers and the "soil" of heaven.</term> of the divine omnipotence; the sweet quality is the kernel of mercy, according to which the entire being, with all its powers, is called **God**. The heat is the kernel of the spirit, from which the light goes forth; it kindles itself in the midst of the sweet quality and is captured by the astringent and the bitter, as if in their midst. Therein is the **Son of God** born, and that is the true **Heart of God**.

79. And the flame or flash of the light, which shines instantly in all powers—just like the sun in the whole world—that is the Holy Spirit, who goes forth from the clarity of the **Son of God** and is the flash and the sharpness. For the Son is born in the midst of the other qualities and is captured with the other qualities.

86. Here, observe the circumstances of how this happens or can happen: An angel is formed out of all the powers together, as I have described at length. Now, when he raises himself up, he first rises in the harsh quality <term>herbe Qualität: the astringent or "tart" force that pulls things together into a form</term>; he gathers this quality together like a woman about to give birth and presses himself. Because of this, the harsh quality becomes so hard and sharp that it can no longer master the sweet water, and the water can no longer rise gently within the creature. Instead, it is captured by the harsh quality and dried up, transformed into a hard, sharp, and fierce coldness. For it becomes too thick from the harsh contraction and loses its bright luster and its oiliness <note>original: "Fettigkeit"; in Böhme’s thought, this "fatness" is the fuel or "oil" that allows the light of the spirit to burn</note>, in which the light-spirit rises. 87. 88. When the heat then kindles the sweet quality, intending to soften its own heat in the sweet water (from which it usually rises and shines throughout the whole body), it finds nothing but a hard, dry, and sweet source which contains no sap, having been entirely dried out by the harshness.

89. It then kindles the sweet source, intending to refresh itself; but there is no sap left. Instead, the sweet source now burns and glows like a hard, parched stone and can no longer ignite its light. The entire body now remains a valley of darkness <note>original: "Finsterthal"</note> containing nothing but a fierce, hard coldness in the harsh quality; a hard, glowing fire in the sweet quality (in which the fierce heat rises for all eternity); and a raging, storming, stinging, and burning in the bitter quality.

# Chapter 9. Aurora in the Dawning.

25. Thirdly, the astringent quality loves the heat, because the light is born within the heat, whereby the astringent quality is enlightened and warmed.

26. And the sweet quality also loves the astringent, (1.) because the astringent dries it so that it does not become thin like elemental water, and so its quality remains in power, and so that in the astringent quality the light, which is born within it, becomes shining and dry. In addition, the astringent quality is a cause of the heat which is born in the sweet water, in which the light rises, in which the sweet water stands in great clarity.

27. Secondly, the sweet quality also loves the bitter, because it is also a cause of the heat, and also because the bitter spirit triumphs and trembles in the sweet water, heat, and light, making the sweet quality mobile and living.

28. Thirdly, the sweet quality loves the heat exceedingly much, so much that I cannot compare it to anything. Take a comparison (though it is certainly far too meager) of two young people of noble temperament <term>complexion; a person's physical and mental constitution, believed in Böhme's time to be governed by the balance of the four humors</term>, when they heat each other in the fire of love. It is such a fire that, if they could take each other into their bodies or transform into one body, they would do so. But this earthly love is only cold water and not true fire; one can find no proper comparison in this half-dead world, except only the resurrection of the dead on the last day; that is a perfect comparison for all divine things that receive true love.

29. The sweet quality loves the heat so much because it gives birth to the bright spirit within it, which is the spirit of life; for life arises in the heat. Otherwise, if there were no heat, all would be a dark valley. As dear as life is, so dear to the sweet spirit is the heat, and the light within the heat.

30. And the bitter quality also loves all other <term>source-spirits; the seven foundational qualities or forces of nature and divinity in Böhme's cosmology</term>: first the sweet, for in the sweet water the bitter spirit is refreshed and quenches its great thirst there, and its bitterness is softened within it and gains its bright life there; and in the astringent <note>original: "herben"</note> it has its body, in which it triumphs and cools and softens itself, and in the heat it has its power and strength, wherein its joy resides.

31. And the heat quality <term>quality; here meaning a fundamental power or "source-spirit" (Quellgeist) that gives reality its character</term> also loves all the other qualities, and the love within it toward and in the others is so great that it cannot be compared, for it is born from them. The astringent <note>original: "herbe"; the contracting, tightening force</note> and bitter qualities are the father of heat, and the sweet source-water is its mother, who conceives, holds, and gives birth to it; for through the harsh driving of the astringent and bitter qualities, heat is produced, which arises within the sweet quality as if it were rising in wood.

32. If you will not believe this, then open your eyes and go to a tree; look at it and contemplate it. First, you see the whole tree. Take a knife and cut into it, and taste it as it is: you will first taste the **astringent quality**, which puckers your tongue <note>literally "pulls your tongue together"</note>; now, this same quality also holds and pulls together all the power of the tree. Afterward, you taste the **bitter quality**, which makes the tree mobile, so that it grows, turns green, and acquires its branches, leaves, and fruit. After that, you taste the **sweetness**, which is quite soft and yet sharp, for it receives its sharpness from the astringent and bitter qualities.

33. Now, these three qualities would be dark and dead if the heat were not within them. But as soon as spring comes, and the sun reaches and warms the earth with its rays, the spirit within the heat becomes alive in the tree. Then the spirits of the tree begin to turn green, grow, and bloom; for the spirit arises in the heat, and all the spirits rejoice and live within it, and there is a heartfelt love between them. The heat, however, is born within the sweet water through the power and drive of the astringent and bitter qualities, but they must use the sun's heat for ignition <note>literally "kindling"</note>, because the qualities in this world are half-dead and too powerless—of which King Lucifer is a cause, as you will find in the account of his fall and the creation of this world.

## Concerning the 6th Source-spirit in the Divine Power.

-> 1. <-

The 6th <term>source-spirit</term> <note>Böhme’s term for the seven fundamental forces or "qualities" that constitute the being of God and the cosmos.</note> in the divine power is the sound or tone, so that everything therein sounds and rings; from this follows the language and the distinction of all things, as well as the ringing and song of the holy angels. Within it also resides the forming of all colors and beauty, as well as the heavenly realm of joy.

Now you ask: what is the tone and sound, or how does this spirit take its source and origin?

-> Note: <-

2. All 7 spirits of God are born into one another; one always begets the other. None is the first, and also none is the last; for the last begets the first just as much as the first begets the second, third, fourth, up to the last.

3. But that one is called the first and another [the second], and so forth, is considered according to which is first in the formation and shaping of a creature. For they are all 7 equally eternal, and none has a beginning or end; and because the 7 qualities always beget one another, and none exists outside the others, it follows that there is one single, eternal, almighty God.

4. For if something is born out of or within the divine being, it is not formed through one spirit alone, but through all seven: and if a creature—which is like the whole being of God—corrupts, elevates, and ignites itself in one source-spirit, it ignites not just one spirit, but all seven.

5. Therefore, that same creature is an abomination before the whole of God and all His creatures, and must stand in eternal enmity and shame before God and all creatures.

This now stands in the <term>wellspring</term><note>Böhme uses *Quellbrunn* (wellspring or fountain) to describe the seven spirits of God as constantly flowing into and out of one another.</note> of the seven spirits of God and always helps to give birth to the other six spirits.

->Understand this rightly.<-

20. It gives birth to its father and mother just as its father and mother give birth to it; for after it is born corporeally, it always gives birth back to the fire with the astringent quality, and the fire gives birth to the light, and the light is the <term>flash</term><note>Original: *Blitz*. For Böhme, this is the sudden ignition of life and consciousness.</note>, which always gives birth back to the life in all the wellspring-spirits, from which the spirits have life, and each always gives birth to the other in turn.

21. Here, however, you should know that one spirit alone cannot give birth to another, nor can two of them do it; rather, the birth of a spirit resides in the working of all seven spirits. Six of them always give birth to the seventh, and if one were not there, the others would not be either.

22. That I sometimes name only two or three for the birth of a spirit, I do because of my own weakness; for I cannot bear all seven at once in their perfection within my corrupted brain. I see all seven well enough, but when I <term>speculate</term><note>Original: *speculire*. In this context, it means deep, prayerful meditation or spiritual vision rather than mere guessing.</note> upon them, the spirit rises up in the central wellspring where the spirit of life is born; it then rises above or sinks below, and cannot grasp all seven spirits of God in one thought or all at once, but only piece by piece.

23. Each spirit has its own source, even though it is born from the others. ### Chapter 10. Aurora in the Dawning. 95

64. But there is no help; their torment only grows the more they mourn it; the more the hellish grimness ignites, they must lie in hell like the bones of the dead, like scorched sheep in the fire. Their stench and abomination gnaw at them; they dare not lift their eyes for shame, for they see nothing in their territory but a strict judge, and above themselves and on all sides they see the eternal joy.

## Chapter 11.
### On the 7th Source-Spirit in the Divine Power.

->1.<-

The seventh Spirit of GOD in the divine power is the *Corpus* <note>Body</note>, which is born from the other six spirits. Within it, all heavenly figures exist, and within it, everything is built and formed, and within it, all beauty and joy arise. This is the true Spirit of Nature—indeed, Nature itself—in which comprehensibility stands, and in which all creatures are formed in heaven and on earth: yes, heaven itself is formed within it, and all naturalness in the whole of GOD stands in this spirit. If this spirit did not exist, there would be neither angel nor man, and GOD would be an unsearchable being, consisting only of unsearchable power.

2. Now the question is: what is this form? If you are a rational <term>Mercury-Spirit</term> <note>original: "Marcurius-Geist." In Böhme's thought, this refers to the spirit of movement, communication, and intellectual perception, often linked to the alchemical Mercury.</note> who penetrates through all seven spirits of GOD, and approves and beholds them as they are, then by the explanation of this seventh spirit, you will understand the working and the essence of the entire Godhead and grasp it in your mind.

3. But if you understand nothing of this spirit, then leave this book in peace, and judge neither the cold nor the heat within it.

<summary>Böhme concludes his harrowing description of the hellish state of the godless before introducing the Seventh Spirit, which he identifies as the substantial "Body" of God or Nature itself, through which all things become tangible and formed.</summary>

6. Behold, all seven Spirits of GOD are born simultaneously; none is the first, and none is the last. When one spirit is stirred, it stirs all the others, and so the birth stands in full power. Therefore, it has a beginning in man, but in GOD it has none; for that reason, I must write only in a creaturely way <note>Using metaphors and sequences that human minds can follow.</note>, otherwise, you would understand nothing.

7. Behold, without the flash, all seven Spirits would be a dark valley. 11. Now, this spirit exists in its color like the blue of the sky, for it is born out of all six spirits. 12. But because the seventh has no particular quality in itself, the flash cannot become brighter in the seventh; rather, it receives from the seventh the corporeal essence of all seven spirits. The flash stands in the middle between these seven spirits and is born of all seven.

13. And the seven spirits are the **Father of the Light**, and the **Light** is their **Son**, whom they thus bring forth from eternity to eternity. The Light always and eternally illuminates and makes the seven spirits alive and full of joy, for they all take their rising and life in the power of the Light. Conversely, they all give birth to the Light and are all at once the Father of the Light; yet the Light gives birth to no spirit, but makes them all alive and joyful, so that they always stand within the birth.

18. ### The Holy Gates.

19. But the light, which stands in the center of all seven spirits, and in which the life of all seven spirits stands—and through which all seven become triumphant and full of joy—in that light the heavenly kingdom of joy arises, so that all seven spirits give birth. It is the **Son** of all seven spirits, and the seven spirits are its **Father**, who give birth to the light; and the light gives birth to the life within them. The light is the **heart** of the seven spirits, and this light is the true **Son of God**, whom we Christians worship and honor as the second person in the Holy Trinity <note>original: "Dreyfaltigkeit"</note>.

What does the poor layman <note>Böhme frequently defends the "layman"—the uneducated common person—against the "high-learned" clergy who he felt obscured divine truth with complex dogma.</note> know of the tumult the priests make in their intoxication? He goes along in his simplicity and gives birth in anguish. <note>original: "ängstiglich." In Böhme's thought, "anguish" or "anxiety" is a technical term for the tension of the natural qualities before they break through into the light of the Spirit.</note>

41. So you say now: Did God then blind the Turks, Jews, and Heathens? No; rather, when God lit the light for them, they lived in the lust of their hearts and would not let the Spirit show them the way; thus the outer light was extinguished. However, it is not so completely extinguished that it could not be born within a human being, since man is of God and lives in God, whether it be in Love or in Wrath. <note>Böhme views "Wrath" and "Love" as the two primary poles of God's manifestation in nature.</note>

42. If a man yearns, should he not become pregnant in his yearning? And if he is pregnant, he can also give birth. But while the outer light shines for him, he does not recognize his Son <note>A reference to the "Christ within" or the birth of the divine spark in the soul.</note> whom he has born; but when the light rises on the Last Day, then he shall see Him.

43. Behold, I tell you a mystery: it is already the time for the Bridegroom to crown his Bride. Guess, Fritz, <note>original: "rath Friz." A colloquial, direct address to the reader, using "Fritz" as a generic name for a common man.</note> where does the crown lie? Toward midnight; <note>In Böhme’s symbolic geography, "Midnight" refers to the North, representing the "harsh" or "dark" quality where the light is most hidden but about to break through.</note> for in the midst of the harsh quality, the light becomes bright. But from whence comes the Bridegroom? From the center, where the heat generates the light; he travels toward midnight into the harsh quality, and there the light becomes bright. What then do those toward midday <note>The South.</note> do? They have fallen asleep in the heat; but a storm-gale will wake them, and among them many shall be terrified unto death.

44. What then do those from the evening <note>The West.</note> do? Their bitter quality wants to rub against the others; but when they taste the sweet water, their spirit becomes gentle. What then do those in the morning? <note>The East.</note> You have been a proud bride from the beginning; the crown has always been offered to you from the start, but you thought yourself too beautiful before, and so you live with the others.

## Aurora in the Dawning. Chapter 11.

57. But when the heat rises within, the green form is shaped into a semi-reddish one, just as when a carbuncle stone <note>A historic term for a deep red gemstone, like a garnet or ruby, believed to glow with its own internal light.</note> shines out from a green flash.

59. See, when now the <term>Mercury</term> <note>original: "Marcurius." 60. I speak here, however, with an **angelic tongue**; you must not understand it in an earthly way, like this world.

61. Regarding <term>Mercury</term>, it also has this form: you must not think that there is a hard pounding, sounding, or clanging, or a whistling in the Godhead, as if someone took a mighty trumpet and blew into it. Yet the holy angels do sing, ring out, trumpet, and sound loudly, for God made them out of Himself for that very purpose: that they should increase the heavenly joy.

62. 63. This, as told above, is now the beautiful and holy heaven that exists throughout the whole Godhead, which has neither beginning nor end, and which no creature can reach with its physical senses.

64. Yet you should know this: that in one place one quality soon shows itself more powerful than another; soon the other rises...

# The Aurora in its Rising. Chapter 2.

If he [the devil] strikes me, I must retreat, but the divine power helps me up; then he also receives his blow and often loses the battle.

68. But when he is overcome, the gate of heaven opens in my spirit; then the spirit sees the divine and heavenly essence—not outside the body, but in the wellspring of the heart the flash rises up into the senses of the brain, wherein the spirit <term>contemplates</term> <note>original: "speculiret." In Böhme’s time, this meant more than just thinking; it referred to a deep, mirror-like observation or a spiritual "looking into" the mysteries of God.</note>.

69. For man is made from all the powers of God, from all seven spirits of God, just as the angels are. However, because he is now corrupted, the divine birth does not always spring up in him, nor does it spring up in all people. And even if it does spring up in him, the high light does not shine in everyone immediately; and if it does shine, it is nonetheless incomprehensible to corrupted nature. For the Holy Spirit does not allow itself to be caught or held in sinful flesh; rather, it rises like a flash of lightning, just as fire comes from a stone when one strikes it.

70. But when the flash is caught in the wellspring of the heart, it rises through the seven <term>source-spirits</term> <note>original: "Quellgeistern." These are the seven fundamental qualities or "fountains" that Böhme believes constitute both God and the natural world.</note> into the brain, like a dawning morning; and therein lies the goal and the knowledge. For in that same light, one sees another, and feels another, and smells another, and tastes another, and hears another, and it is just as if the entire Godhead were rising up within.

71. Herein the spirit now looks even into the depth of the Godhead; for in God, near and far are one thing. And that same God, of whom I write in this book, is just as much in his Trinity within the <term>body</term> <note>original: "Corpus"</note> of holy souls as he is in heaven. From this I take my knowledge and from no other thing; I wish to know nothing else but that same God, and He also creates the certainty of my spirit, so that I constantly believe and trust in Him.

72. And even if an angel from heaven told it to me, I would still be unable to believe it, much less grasp it, for I would always doubt whether it were truly so. But because the Sun itself rises within my spirit, I am certain of it, and I see for myself the arrival and birth of the holy angels and of all things, both in heaven and in this world. For the holy soul is one spirit with God; even though it is a creature, it is nonetheless equal to the angels: also it sees

77. What might follow entirely under this or after this, I do not fully know, only that some future mysteries in the Depth are shown to me.

79. It happens in the soul just so: when it breaks through in its struggle, it beholds the Godhead like a <term>Flash</term>, but the <term>well-spring of sin</term> <note>original: 'Sündenquell'</note> soon covers it up again. For the old <term>Adam</term> <note>Referring to the fallen, earthly nature of humanity inherited from the biblical first man, which cannot yet fully dwell in the divine light</note> belongs to the earth, and not with this flesh into the Godhead.

80. I do not write this for my own praise, but so that the reader may know where my knowledge stands, so that he does not seek another in me than who I am. ->Note the depth.<-

3. There are seven spirits of God; all seven have moved themselves, and the light within them has also moved, and the Spirit that proceeds from the seven spirits of God has also moved.

4. Now the Creator wished, according to His Trinity, to create three hosts not far from one another, but rather adjacent to each other like a circle. Now observe: just as the spirits were in their surging or rising, so too were the creatures formed. In the center of each host, the "heart" of that host was incorporated <note>original: "corporiret," meaning given a body or substance</note> together; from this, an angelic king or grand prince was formed.

5. Just as the Son of God is born in the midst of the seven spirits of God and is the life and heart of those seven spirits, so also an angelic king was created in the center of his territory out of nature—or out of the natural heaven—from the power of all seven source-spirits <term>source-spirits: Böhme’s "Quellgeister," the seven primary forces or qualities (like sweetness, bitterness, heat) that drive all of existence</term>. He was now the heart within a host and held the quality, might, and strength of his entire host within himself, and he was the most beautiful among them.

6. Just as the Son of God is the heart, the life, and the strength of all seven spirits of God, so too is a king of the angels within his host.

7. Now, just as there are seven principal qualities in the divine power from which the heart of God is born, several mighty prince-angels were also created according to each primary quality in every host. I do not know their exact number, but they stand alongside the king as the leaders of the other angels.

8. Here you should know that the angels are not all of one quality, nor are they all equal to one another in power and might. While every angel has the power of all seven source-spirits within him, one specific quality is the strongest in each. He is glorified according to that specific quality. For as the *Salitter* was at each location at the time of creation, so the angel became; and according to the quality that is strongest within the angel, he is named and glorified.

9. Just as each of the meadow flowers receives its own color from its quality <term>quality: In Böhme's thought, a "quality" (Qualität) is a specific property or force of divine nature, such as heat, bitterness, or sweetness</term>, and is also named according to that quality, so it is with the holy angels: some are strongest in the harsh quality, and these are light brownish and closest to the cold.

10. Now, when the light of the Son of **GOD** shines upon them, they appear in their quality just like a bright, brown flash of lightning. Some are of the water quality, and these are bright, like the holy heaven; and when the light shines upon them, they look like a crystalline sea.

11. Some are strongest in the bitter quality; these are like a precious green stone <note>likely referring to an emerald</note> that looks like a flash of lightning, and when the light shines upon them, it appears like a reddish-green light, as if a carbuncle <term>carbuncle: A deep red gemstone, historically believed to glow with its own internal light</term> were shining from within it, or as if life itself had its origin there.

12. Some are of the heat quality, and these are the brightest of all, yellowish and reddish; and when the light shines upon them, they look like the lightning-flash of the Son of **GOD**. Some are strongest in the love quality; they are a vision of the heavenly kingdom of joy, entirely bright, and when the light shines upon them, they look like a light blue color—a lovely sight to behold.

13. Some are strongest in the quality of sound <note>original: "Thons" (Tone/Resonance). In Böhme’s system, the seventh quality is the "Sound" or "Tone" which gives distinct form and articulation to the others</note>; these are also bright, and when the light shines upon them, they look like a rising flash of lightning, as if something were about to raise itself up there.

14. Some are of the whole of nature, like a common intermingling; when the light shines upon them, they look like the holy heaven, which is formed out of all the spirits of **GOD**.

15. But the King is the heart of all qualities and has his domain in the center like a wellspring—just as the sun stands in the middle of the planets and is a king of the stars and a heart of nature in this world. An angelic king, or Cherubim <note>original: "Jerubin"</note>, is also that great.

16. And just as the other six planets are commanders alongside the sun and give their will to the sun so that it may rule and work within them, so all the angels give their will to the King; and the prince-angels sit in council with the King.

17. But you should know here that they all have a will of love toward one another; no one envies another for his form or beauty. For just as it is within the spirits of **GOD**, so it is among the angels.

No one thinks himself more beautiful than the other, but each has his joy in the other and rejoices in the other’s beautiful form and loveliness; from which their love for one another rises up, so that they lead one another by their hands and kiss one another in a friendly way.

40. If you now wish to know where their love, humility, and friendliness come from—which rise up in their hearts—then observe what follows.

41. Every angel is fashioned like the entire Godhead and is like a little God; for when God created the angels, he created them out of himself. Now, God is the same in one place as in another; everywhere there is the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.

42. In these three names and power stand the heaven and this world, and everything your heart can think of; and even if you were to close a tiny circle that you could hardly see into or discern, the entire divine power would still be within it. The Son of God is born within it, and the Holy Spirit goes forth from the Father and the Son within it. If it is not in love, then it is in wrath, as it is written: <note>original: "bey den Heiligen bist du heilig, und bey den Verkehrten bist du verkehrt"</note> "With the holy you are holy, and with the perverse you are perverse" (Psalm 18:26). These people awaken the wrath of God over themselves, which also stands in all the spirits of God in the place where it is awakened; conversely, where the love of God is awakened, it stands in the full birth of the entire Godhead of that place.

43. And in this there is no difference; the angels are created one like another, all out of the divine <term>Salitter</term> <note>A term coined by Böhme, likely derived from "salniter" (saltpeter), referring to the spiritual "soil" or fundamental crystalline substance of the heavenly realm.</note> of heavenly nature. This alone is the difference between them: that when God created them, each individual quality stood in the great movement in its highest birth or rising. From this it has come to pass that the angels are of many different qualities.

### Of the total heavenly bliss of all three kingdoms of the angels.

51. Here the Spirit shows that wherever any angel is created, that same place or <term>location</term> <note>original Latin: *Locus*</note> in the heavenly nature, in which and out of which he became a creature, is his own seat, which he possesses by <term>natural right</term> <note>original: *Naturrecht*</note> as long as he remains in God’s love. For it is the <term>location</term> that he had from eternity before he became a creature; for the <term>divine substance</term> <note>original: *Salitter*. 52. But you should not think that God is thereby bound, such that He may not drive him out of it if he should act differently than how God first created him. For as long as he remains in obedience and in love, the place is his by natural right; but when he rises up and ignites the place with the <term>fire of wrath</term> <note>original: *Zornfeuer*</note>, then he sets his Father's house on fire and becomes an opposition to the <term>location</term> from which he was made, making two things out of that which was one before his prideful rising.

53. Now when that happens, he keeps his corporeal natural right for himself, and the <term>location</term> keeps its own right for itself as well. But if the creature, which has a beginning, wants to set itself against the First—which was before the creature and has no beginning—and wants to destroy the <term>location</term> it did not make, wherein it was created as a creature in love, and wants to turn that same love into a <term>fire of wrath</term>, then Love rightfully spews out the fire of wrath along with the creature.

54. From this, the laws in this world also arise; for when the son sets himself against the father and strikes the father, he has lost his paternal inheritance, and the father may thrust him out of the house. But while he is in the father’s obedience, the father has no power to disinherit him.

# The Aurora, or Day-Spring. Chapter 12.

Heaven, as well as many other worldly laws written in the books of Moses, all take their beginning and origin from the divine nature in heaven, which I will then clearly prove in its place based on the true foundation in the Godhead.

->Now one might say:<-

### So then, an angel is tied to the very place in which he was created, so that he may not or cannot leave from there.

56. **N**o, just as the spirits of **GOD** do not allow themselves to be bound in their rising—so that they should not flow among one another—likewise, the angels are not bound entirely to their <term>location</term> <note>original Latin: *Loco*</note>.

57. For just as the spirits of **GOD** always rise into one another and have a play of love in their birth, yet each spirit retains its natural seat or its <term>location</term> <note>original Latin: *Locum*</note> in the birth of **GOD**, and it never happens that the heat turns into cold, or the cold into heat; rather, each retains its natural <term>location</term> and rises in the other, from which life has its origin.

58. So also the holy angels flow or wander among one another in all three kingdoms; thus one receives from the other—that is, from the other’s beautiful form, friendliness, and virtue—his highest joy, and yet each retains his natural seat or <term>location</term> <note>original Latin: *Locum*</note> in which he became a <term>creature</term> <note>original: *Creatur*; here meaning a created being</note> as his own property.

59. # Chap. 12. Aurora, or the Day-Spring in its Ascent.

## Concerning the Royal Primacy or Power of the Three Angelic Kings.

72. Just as the Godhead is threefold in its essence, in which the outgoing from the seven spirits of God manifests and brings forth threefold—as Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, one God, wherein the entire divine power consists, along with everything that exists—and yet the three persons in the Godhead are not a separable essence, but are within one another: So also in the same manner, when God moved and created the angels, three special angels were made from the best core of nature, from the essence of the Trinity in the nature of God, and in such authority and power as the Trinity has within the seven spirits of God.

73. For the Trinity of God rises up within the seven spirits of God, and is in turn the life and heart of all seven spirits: so also have the three angelic kings <note>original: "englische Könige," which in this context means "angelic kings" (from Engel) rather than kings of the nation of England</note> each risen up in the nature of his own host or place, and each is a natural Lord of his place over the government of the angels; however, the Trinity of the Godhead, which is unchangeable, retains the *locum* <note>Latin: place or space</note> for itself, while the king retains the government of the angels.

74. Now, just as the Trinity of the Godhead is a single essence in all parts throughout the whole Father, and is connected together like the members in a human body, where all places are as one place—even if one place has a different office than another, just as with human limbs, yet it is still the one Body of God—so also are the three angelic kingdoms connected with one another, and not each one separately divided. No angelic king may say: "This is my kingdom, no other king may enter into it."

75. Although it is indeed his original natural hereditary kingdom, and remains his own, yet all other kings and angels are his true natural brothers, born of one Father, and they all inherit their Father’s kingdom together.

76. Just as the source-spirits <term>Quellgeister: Böhme’s term for the seven fundamental properties or "fountain-springs" of divine nature that generate all existence</term> of God each have their own natural seat of birth and keep their natural *locum* <note>Latin: place</note> for themselves, yet with the other spirits are the one God—for if the others did not exist, he would not exist either, and likewise one rises up within the other—so it is also with the primacy of the holy angels; it has no other form than that which is in God.

For their agility is as fast as the divine power itself, yet one is swifter than another, all according to which quality they belong to.

82. In that same seventh spirit of nature, the heavenly fruit and colors also arise, and everything that is tangible; it is exactly like a form <note>meaning: a visible, structured reality</note>, as if the angels were to dwell in the depth between heaven and earth, where they might climb up and down; and wherever they were, there their foot would rest, as if it stood upon the earth.

# Dawn in the Ascent. Chap. 12.

91. Just as the Trinity <note>original: "Dreyheit"</note> of God rules over the infinite being, and over the figures and various forms in the Godhead, and changes and forms them: So also are the three angelic kings lords over their angels, reaching into their very hearts and deepest depths. Although they cannot change themselves corporeally, like God himself who created them, they nevertheless rule them corporeally, and are obligated and bound to them, just as body and soul are bound to one another.

92. For the king is their head, and they are the king's members, and the <term>Source-princes: "Quellfürsten," high-ranking angels who serve as the primary conduits for the seven qualities of divine nature</term>, these angels are the king's counselors or agents, just as in a human the five senses, or the hands and feet, or the mouth, nose, eyes, and ears, are the means by which the king carries out his business.

93. Now, just as all angels are bound to the king, so also the king is bound to God his Creator, like body and soul. The body signifies God, and the soul the angelic king, who exists within the body of God, and has also become a creature <note>Böhme uses "Creatur" to emphasize that even the highest angel is a "created thing" rather than the uncreated Creator</note> within the body of God, and remains eternally in the body of God, like a soul in its nest; therefore God has also glorified him as highly as his own property, just as the soul is glorified within the body.

94. Thus the king or Grand Prince Michael stands equal to God the Father in his glorification or clarity <note>original: "Klarheit," referring to divine radiance or transparency</note>, and is a king and prince of God upon the mountain of God, and holds his office in the Deep, within which he was created.

95. That same circle or space, in which he and his angels were created, is his kingdom, and he is a beloved son of God the Father in nature, a creaturely son, in whom the Father takes his joy.

96. You must not compare him to the Heart or Light of God, which exists throughout the entirety of the Father, and which has neither beginning nor end, just like God the Father himself.

97. For this prince is a creature, and has a beginning, but he exists within God the Father, and is bound with Him in His love as His dear son, whom He has created out of Himself.

### Aurora: The Day-Spring. Chapter 12.

...I could not grasp it without God's enlightenment, much less believe it. For I would always be in doubt whether it had been a good angel at the command of God, since the Devil can also disguise himself in the form of an angel <note>The original cites 2 Cor. 11:24, but the reference to the Devil disguising himself as an angel of light is found in 2 Corinthians 11:14.</note> to lead people astray.

118. But because it is born in the **Center** or circle of life, as a brightly shining light, similar to the heavenly birth or the rising of the Holy Spirit, with a fiery impulse of the spirit, I cannot resist it, let the world mock me as it will.

119. The Spirit testifies that it is but a very short time until the <term>Flash<note>German: *Plitz* (modern *Blitz*). For Böhme, this is the sudden, transformative moment of divine revelation or "lightning" that ignites the soul and moves it from darkness to light.</note></term> shall rise in the whole circle of this world, in which this Spirit is a messenger or proclaimer of the day. Whichever person is not found in the birth of the Holy Spirit at that time, in that person this birth shall also never rise eternally; rather, they remain in the source-fountain of darkness, like a dead, hard flint-stone, in which the source of <term>wrath<note>German: *Grimmigkeit*. A central concept for Böhme, referring to the harsh, consuming, and "grim" quality of the first principle of nature when it is not illuminated by the second principle (Divine Light/Love).</note></term> and perdition rises eternally. There, such a person will mock eternally in the birth of hellish abomination; for whatever the quality of the tree is, such also is its fruit.

# 135 Day-Spring in the Ascent. Chap. 12.

### Now observe the form of heaven.

**123. When** you look upon this world, you have a prototype of heaven: the stars represent the angels; for just as the stars must remain unchanged until the end of this time, so the angels must remain eternally unchanging in the eternal time of heaven.

**124.** The elements represent the wondrous proportion and transformation of the heavenly form; for just as the Deep <note>The vast expanse or "abyss" of space</note> between the stars and the earth is always changing in its appearance—sometimes it is beautifully bright, sometimes cloudy, sometimes wind, sometimes rain, sometimes snow, sometimes the Deep is blue, sometimes greenish, sometimes whitish, sometimes dark.

**125.** In the same way, the transformation of heaven occurs in many colors and forms, though not in the same manner as in this world. Instead, everything happens according to the rising up of the spirits of God, and the light of the Son of God shines eternally within it; yet one "rising up" in the birth is greater than another; therefore, the wondrous wisdom of God is incomprehensible.

**126.** The earth represents the heavenly nature or the 7th <term>Nature-spirit</term> <note>Böhme describes seven "Source-Spirits" or qualities; the seventh is the "Essentiality" or the body in which the others manifest</note>, in which formations, shapes, and colors arise. The birds, fish, and animals represent the various shapes of the figures in heaven.

**127.** You should know that the Spirit in the "flash" <note>The moment of divine illumination or the sudden movement of the spirit</note> testifies that all kinds of figures arise in heaven, similar to the animals, birds, and fish of this world, but in a heavenly form, clarity, and manner, as well as all kinds of trees, shrubs, and flowers. But just as they arise, so they pass away again; for they are not incorporated <note>given a fixed, permanent physical body</note> in the same way as the angels. Rather, they take shape in the birth of the rising qualities within the <term>Nature-spirit</term>.

**128.** When a figure is formed in one spirit so that it exists, and then another spirit wrestles with it and prevails, it is separated again or changed—all according to the nature of the qualities. And this is in God like a holy play.

**129.** For this reason, the creatures—such as animals, birds, fish, and worms in this world—were not created for an eternal essence, but for a transitory one, just as the figures of heaven also pass away. I place this here only as a guide; you will find it described in more detail during the account of the Creation of this world.

### The 13th Chapter.
## Of the terrible, lamentable, and miserable Fall of the Kingdom of Lucifer.

1. Before this mirror I wish to summon all proud, greedy, envious, and wrathful people; there they shall see the origin of their pride, greed, envy, and wrath, as well as the outcome and final reward.

2. The learned ones have brought forth many and various strange theories <note>original: "monstra", literally monsters or omens, but here referring to monstrous or strange ideas/arguments</note> concerning the beginning of sins and the origin of the devil, and have scratched themselves with it; everyone thought he had the axe by the handle <note>A German idiom meaning to have mastered a matter or found the core solution</note>, yet it remained entirely hidden from them until this day <note>original: "bis auf dato"</note>.

3. But because it now wishes to reveal itself completely, as if in a clear mirror, it is well to be presumed that the great day of God's revelation is now at hand, when the fierceness <note>In Böhme’s system, "Grimmigkeit" or fierceness refers to the harsh, dark quality of nature when separated from God's light</note> and the kindled fire shall separate from the light.

4. 48. Now the Heart of God should have been in-qualified with the heart of the angel, and that could not be, for it was hard against soft, and sour against sweet, and dark against God, and fire against a lovely warmth, and harsh pounding against a lovely song.

The entire Godhead, in its innermost or primary birth at the core, has a very sharp, terrifying sharpness, in which the <term>astringent quality</term> <note>German: *herbe qualität*; the first of Böhme’s seven source-spirits, representing contraction, cold, and the "drawing together" that creates form</note> is a terrifying, harsh, hard, dark, and cold contraction, just like winter when it is fiercely cold, so that ice is formed from water, and it is altogether unbearable.

56. Consider if, in winter, when it is so cold, the sun were to be taken away; what kind of cold and altogether raw and hard darkness would result, where no life could endure.

57. In such a way is the astringent quality in the innermost core within itself, and for itself alone apart from the other qualities in God; for this severity creates the contraction and the holding of a <note>original: *Corpus*</note> body, and the hardness dries it so that it may exist as a <term>creature</term> <note>German: *creatürlich*; meaning having the physical or finite form of a created being</note>.

58. And the <term>bitter quality</term> <note>German: *bittere qualität*; the second source-spirit, representing movement, friction, and the impulse to expand or break out of the harsh contraction</note> is a tearing, penetrating, and cutting bitter source. For it divides and disperses the hard and astringent quality, and creates mobility. And between these two qualities, heat is born from their hard and fierce-bitter rubbing, tearing, and raging; this heat rises up in the bitter and astringent quality as a fierce ignition, and passes through as a hard <term>fire-resonance</term> <note>German: *Feurklang*; a unique term of Böhme's suggesting that light, heat, and sound are unified at this fundamental level of creation</note>. From this the hard tone arises, and in such an ascent, or such rising, it becomes enclosed and fortified within the astringent quality, so that it is a body that endures.

59. Now, if there were no further quality in this body that could quench the fieriness of these four qualities, there would indeed be a constant enmity within it; for the bitter would be against the astringent, in the way it storms and tears within it, shattering the astringent.

60. So too the astringent would be against the bitter, in the way it draws the bitter together and holds it captive, so that it could not have its own path.

61. And the heat would be against them both, in the way it makes everything hot and raging with its fierce ignition and rising, and is entirely against the cold.

35. **N**o; for if **God** had known it before the time of the creation of the angels, it would have been an eternal, intentional will, and there would be no enmity against **God**, but **God** would surely have created him as a devil from the start.

36. 54. The first spirit is the astringent quality, which in **GOD** is a fine, lovely contracting, drying, and cooling; it is used for the formation of things. Although it is somewhat sharp in its depth, it tempers itself with the sweet water so that it is entirely gentle, lovely, and full of joy.

And if it pleases him, he feeds from it and infects <note>In Böhme’s vocabulary, "to infect" (inficiren) often means a spiritual merging or influence rather than disease</note> himself with the thing, and wrestles with it, and creates a temperament <term>Temperanz: a state of balance or harmony between conflicting qualities</term>, regardless of how far away that thing might be. As far as his original or initial kingdom in God reaches, so far can the spirit rule instantly, and it is held back by nothing.

91. For he is and understands the power just as God the Holy Spirit does, and in this regard there is no difference between God the Holy Spirit and the spirit of the body, except this: that the Holy Spirit of God is the entire fullness, while the spirit of the body is only a part which penetrates through the whole fullness; and wherever it goes, it merges with that place, and rules there in that same location <note>Latin: "Loco"</note> together with God.

92. For he is from God and in God, and cannot be held back, except only by the seven nature-spirits of the body, which give birth to the animal spirit <gloss>the spirit of the soul</gloss>; they hold the reins in hand and can give birth to him however they wish.

# Chap. 14. The Rising Dawn.

So you say: He is present in many things with His wrath, because it is so hard and evil, and not like the Godhead.

99. Yes, dear man, it is all true; in silver, gold, stones, fields, clothing, animals, and humans—whatever is tangible—the wrath of God is certainly everywhere, otherwise it would not be so hard and tangible. <note>Böhme argues that the "hardness" of physical matter is a result of the "contraction" caused by God's wrath or sternness.</note>

100. But you should know that the core of love also stays hidden in everything in the hidden <term>center</term> <note>original: "Centro," referring to the inner spiritual origin of a thing</note>, unless it is entirely too evil—which does not please man either.
->(God possesses everything, but only according to nature; He is not the <term>essence</term> <note>original: "Essenz," meaning the fundamental substance or being</note>, He possesses Himself.)<-
Or do you think that you do right by bathing yourself in God's wrath? See to it that it does not set your body and soul on fire, and you burn in it eternally, like Lucifer.

101. But when God brings forth the hidden things at the end of this time, then you will see clearly where God's love or wrath has been; therefore watch and beware, and turn your eyes from evil, or you will ruin yourself.

102. I take heaven and earth as witnesses that I have here performed what God has revealed to me as His will.

103. Thus King Lucifer, in his <term>body</term> <note>original: "Corpus"</note>, transformed the sweet water into a sour sharpness, intending thereby to rule over the whole Godhead in his arrogance. He has also brought it so far that in this world, with that same sharpness, he seizes the hearts of all creatures—both in leaves and grass, and in everything—as a king and prince of this world.

104. Now, if the divine love were not still in the whole nature of this world, and we poor humans and creatures did not have the **Hero in the strife** <note>German: "Held im Streit." This is a title Böhme frequently gives to Christ as the champion who fights the spiritual battle against darkness.</note> with us, then we would all have to perish in an instant in that hellish horror.

## Chapter 15.
### Concerning the third <term>species</term> <note>original Latin: "species," here meaning a specific type, form, or quality.</note> or quality of the beginning of sin in Lucifer.

->1.<-

The third spirit in **God** is the bitter spirit, which arises in the flash of life; for the flash of life arises in the sweet water through the friction of the harsh and hot quality: the <term>body</term> <note>original: "Corpus"</note> of the flash, however, remains in the sweet water as a light or heart, standing fine and gentle; and the flash is entirely trembling, and from the terror and fire and water and harsh spirit it becomes bitter through the origin of the water in which it arises.

2. That same flash or raging terror or bitter spirit is caught in the harsh quality, and in the clear light within the harsh spirit it becomes glorified and highly joyful: that is now the mobility or the root of life, which forms the word in the harsh quality or makes it distinct, so that a thought or will arises in the <term>body</term> <note>original: "Corpus"</note>.

3. Now that same highly triumphant and joyful spirit is used most laudably and well for formation in the divine <term>salitter</term> <note>Böhme's term for the fundamental "divine soil" or spiritual matter of heaven.</note>, for it wells up primarily in sound and in love, and is closest to the heart of **God** in its birth, and joined with Him in joy; it is itself the source of joys or the rising up in the heart of **God**.

Of the 4th Species or Form of the Beginning of Sin in Lucifer.

34. Against this now raged and stormed the cold fire of the deep quality against the knee, and against the bitter power like a great uproar, and was now soon in the deep body raging nothing but murdering, robbing, burning and patching, a completely terrible hellish fire.

35. This fire-power and true fire-spirit now also raised itself in the center of the heart, and wanted, through the animal spirit (to champion with this) to rule the spirit of the will from the center, which arises from the begetter, as from the 7 source-spirits, which is the image of God, in the entire divine power, and to ignite the entire Salitter of God, as a new and mighty God. The forms and heavenly formations were to give up in terrible fire-quality, and let themselves be formed according to this power.

36. Now when I always write of the animal spirit, you must also know quite properly what it is or how it is, otherwise you will read this birth in vain, and it will go for you like the far-off heathens, who climb up to God's face, and could not live before it.

37. The spirit of power is far more subtle and incomprehensible than the body or the 7 source-spirits, which hold and form the body, for it proceeds from the 7 spirits, just as God the Holy Spirit from the Father and Son.

38. The 7 source-spirits have their jointly incorporated body from nature, that is, from the deep spirit of nature in the divine power, which I in deep books call the Salitter of God or the comprehensibility, wherein the heavenly figures arise. That is one spirit, like all 7 spirits, alone the other 6 and an incomprehensible being therein, for the divine power begets itself in the comprehensibility of the deep spirit of nature as if hidden, incomprehensible to explanations.

39. But the animal or power-spirit begets itself in the heart from the 7 source-spirits in the manner that the Son of God is born, and keeps its mind in the heart, and proceeds from the same mind into the divine power, as the Holy Spirit from the Father and Son, for it also has such a substance as God the Holy Spirit, and is of one quality with God the Holy Spirit.

40. When the animal spirit arises from the body, it should be one thing with the hidden Godhead, and is involved in the formation of a thing in nature, as God the Holy Spirit fashions. Of this you have an example: when a carpenter wants to build an artful house, or any other craftsman to make an artful work, the hands, which signify nature, cannot make it beforehand. Rather, the 7 spirits are the first builders of it, and the animal spirit shows the form to the 7 spirits. Then the 7 spirits form it and make it comprehensible, and only then do the hands work according to the image, for you must first bring a work into your mind if you want to make it.

41. For the soul comprehends the highest mind, she sees what God her Father makes, and works along in the heavenly formation, therefore she raises up for the nature-spirit a model of how they should form a thing. And according to this quality of the soul all things in this world are made, for the corrupted soul always works, that it might form heavenly forms, but it cannot, for it has for its work and labor only an erroneous, corrupted Salitter, which is a soon-dead nature, wherein it cannot form heavenly figures.

42. From this deep battle you may understand what great power the spirits of the perished angels have had in the heavenly nature, and what a substance the corruption may be, how they have corrupted and devastated nature in heaven in their place with their gruesome kindling, from which the terrible wrath that reigns in this world has arisen.

--- Page 215 ---
<meta>This page continues the discussion of the "animal spirit" (soul-spirit) from paragraph 38 on the previous page. It explores how the human soul mirrors the creative process of the Trinity and how the Fall of the angels corrupted the material world.</meta>

### ->Chapter 15. The Rising of the Dawn. 183<-

God's housing <note>original: 'heisse', likely meaning a vessel or container</note> or tangibility, in which the heavenly figures arise. This is a spirit just like all seven spirits, only the other six are an incomprehensible essence within it; for the divine power is born within the tangibility of the seventh spirit of nature as if hidden, incomprehensible to the creatures.

39. But the animal or soul-spirit <note>The 'animal' spirit refers to the Latin 'anima' (soul), the life-force that moves the body.</note> is born in the heart out of the seven source-spirits, in the same way and manner as the Son of God is born. It keeps its seat in the heart and goes out from that same seat into the divine power, just as the Holy Spirit goes out from the Father and the Son; for it also has such a subtlety as God the Holy Spirit, and works in harmony <term>inqualiret: a term used by Böhme to describe how different forces or spirits blend their qualities to act as one</term> with God the Holy Spirit.

40. When the animal spirit goes out from the body <note>original: 'Corpus'</note>, it is one thing with the hidden Godhead, and is part of the formation of things in nature, just like God the Holy Spirit Himself. You have an example of this: when a carpenter wants to build an artistic house, or another craftsman wants to make an artistic work, the hands—which represent nature—cannot do it first. Instead, the seven spirits are the primary builders, and the animal spirit shows the seven spirits the form. Then the seven spirits shape it and make it tangible; only then do the hands work according to that image, for you must first bring a work into your mind if you wish to make it.

41. For the soul grasps the highest meaning; she sees what God her Father does and works along with Him in the heavenly forming. Therefore, she circles a model before the spirits of nature, showing them how they should form a thing. And according to this pre-forming by the soul, all things in this world are made. For the corrupted soul works constantly to try and form heavenly shapes, but she cannot, because she has only earthly, corrupted Salitter <term>Salitter: Böhme’s term for the divine "sap" or constitutional matter of the universe, which can be either "sweet" (heavenly) or "bitter/scorched" (earthly/hellish)</term>—even a half-dead nature—for her work, in which she cannot form heavenly figures.

42. By this you can understand what great power the spirits of the cast-out <note>original: 'verstoffenen', likely 'verstossenen'</note> angels once had in heavenly nature, and what a substance the corruption must be, seeing how they corrupted and devastated nature in their place in heaven with their horrible ignition. From this, the terrible wrath <note>Böhme uses 'Grimm' to describe the harsh, punishing aspect of nature and God's judgment.</note> which rules in this world has arisen.

->43. For<-

<summary>Böhme explains the soul-spirit as a creative force that mirrors the Holy Spirit, using the metaphor of a carpenter to show how the mind directs the forces of nature. He concludes by linking the world's corruption and "wrath" to the fall of the angels who misused this creative power.</summary>
<keywords>soul-spirit, seven spirits, Trinity, animal spirit, Salitter, creation, fallen angels, wrath of nature</keywords>

# The Rising of the Dawn. Chap. 15.

43. Then the kindled nature still burns, which on the last day and this kindled fire-source is an eternal enmity against (God.). But whether this kindled fire-griffin, fiddle, bath, and that (God.) has unfortunately kindled it, from which the sun-fire has arisen, the (special) masters must also answer for and prove in nature, if not, then this fire-griffin shall also be condemned.

# Of the 5th Woodpecker or Form of Sin's Beginning in Lucifer and his Angels.

44. The 5th duel-spirit in the divine power is the blissful-stiff love, which in the right glance of gentleness and humility is also born in the flash of life. What the flash as a swift beam brings through, whereby joy unfolds, so the stock of the kindled love remains in the felled (water), and penetrates its gentleness after the flash through the fire into the harsh quality, and catches the fire, and makes the harsh quality gentle and soft, which is also a birth of the water.

45. But when the fire tastes the gentle, felled and soft taste, it catches itself and forms itself into a gentle warmth, very loving, and gives rise to a friendly life in the fire, and with this dear gentle warmth penetrates the harsh quality, and seizes the cold fire, and makes the hard soft, and the thick geese, and the darkness dear.

46. But when the bitter flash, traveling with the harsh and fire-spirit, kills this gentleness, then all is for naught but mere heavy desiring and fulfilling, a very gentle and lovely life, wrestling, thrusting and love-birth. For all the duel-spirits' severe births become in this penetrator quite gentle, lovely, humble, and friendly, and herein rightly reveals the Godhead.

47. For in the first 4 duel-spirits is the divine birth, therefore they must also be quite severe, although they also have their gentle mother, the water, under them: and in the fifth is the blissful-stiff love, and in the sixth the joy, and in the seventh the formation or comprehensibility.

48. Now then, Lucifer, with your love, how have you sustained yourself, is your love also such a duel-well? We want to now also enliven it, what a dear angel you have become.

# Cap. 15. The Rising of the Dawn. Cap. 16.

# Mark.

49. If Lucifer had not raised and kindled himself, his duel-well of love would be nothing other than in (God.). For there was no other Galitter in him than in (God.).

50. But when he raised himself up, intending with his animal spirit to rule the entire Godhead, the stock and sort of the light, which is the core of love in the felled (water), was a grim and striving-after salt-spring, from which a trembling, burning regimen and birth was perceived in the entire body.

51. Now when the animal spirit is born in this severe and harsh fire-birth, it pressed quite grimly out of the body into the nature or Galitter (God.), and dissolved the blissful-stiff love in the Galitter. For it pressed quite grimly and fiery like a storm-wight through everything, and thought it alone was (God.), it wanted to rule with sharpness.

52. From this has now arisen the great contradiction and eternal enmity between (God.) and Lucifer, for the power (God.) rules quite gently, lovely and friendly, so that one cannot even comprehend its birth, and then Lucifer's (side) wants and tears, ruling quite harshly, fiery and swiftly.

53. Of this you have an (example in the kindled Galitter of the stars, which from this kindled wrath must with vanity so swiftly revolve until the last day, then the wrathfulness will be separated from them, and given to King Lucifer as an eternal abode.

54. That this is a great contradiction in (God.), needs no remark, but a man may think, if such a grim fire-source arose in him in love, what contradiction and displeasure would arise, and how very often the whole body would become wrathful.

55. Which certainly happens to those who take the reins to the inn, but because he is (sated), he lies full like one sluggish, but when he becomes (enraged), he storms the head, as he would do to the love (God.).

56. Therefore, the sun-fire (God.) is now still in the love (God.) of this world until the end, and many an expectation will be swallowed in the sun-fire, of which much could be written, but it belongs in its proper place.

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the fall of Lucifer and how his rebellion transformed the divine substance into a source of wrath. It follows the description of the seven "source-spirits" from the previous page.</meta>

### Chapter 15. The Morning Redness in the Rising. 185

-> **Note.** <-

49. **I**f Lucifer had not exalted himself and kindled <note>meaning he ignited his own inner fire through pride</note> his own fire, his fountain-spring of love would have been nothing other than what is in GOD; for there was no other <term>Salitter<note>original: "Salitter"; Böhme's term for the divine "saltpeter" or the fundamental substance of the heavenly world.</note></term> in him than there was in GOD.

50. But when he lifted himself up, intending to rule the whole Godhead with his <term>vital spirit<note>original: "animalischen Geiste"; referring to the "anima" or the animating soul-force.</note></term>, the source and heart of the light—which is the core of love within the sweet water—became a fierce and piercing fire-source. From this, a trembling, burning dominion and "birth" <note>the process of coming into being</note> arose throughout his whole <term>Body<note>original: "Corpus"</note></term>.

51. When the vital spirit was born in this severe and harsh birth of fire, it pressed fiercely out of the Body into the nature or divine substance of GOD, and destroyed the delightful love within that substance. It surged through everything like a <term>furious tyrant<note>original: "Wüterich"</note></term>, thinking it was GOD alone and wishing to rule through harshness.

52. From this has now arisen the great conflict and eternal enmity between GOD and Lucifer; for the power of GOD wells up very gently, lovely, and friendly, so that its origin cannot even be grasped, while the spirits of Lucifer surge and tear with harsh, fiery, and rapid movements.

53. You see an example of this in the kindled substance of the stars, which, because of this ignited <term>wrath<note>original: "Grimme"</note></term>, must roll about so quickly in vanity <note>meaning the fleeting, material world</note> until the Last Day. Then, the fierceness will be separated from them and given to King Lucifer as an eternal dwelling.

54. That this causes a great conflict in GOD requires no proof. Instead, a person may consider this: if such a fierce fire-source arose within their own body, what conflict and displeasure would it cause, and how often would the entire body be driven to rage?

55. This is precisely what happens to those who take the devil in as a guest. While he is only a guest, he lies still like a tame little dog; but when he becomes the master of the house, he storms the building, just as he did to the Body of GOD.

56. Therefore, the <term>wrath-fire<note>original: "Zornfeur"</note></term> of GOD remains within the "Body of GOD" of this world <note>referring to the physical universe as a corrupted extension of the divine</note> until the end. Many a creature is swallowed up in this wrath-fire, about which much could be written, but it belongs in its proper place.

-> 57. Whether <-

<summary>Böhme explains how Lucifer’s pride transformed his inner divine essence into a raging fire, creating an eternal enmity with God’s gentle nature and introducing "wrath" into the physical world.</summary>
<keywords>Lucifer, Salitter, vital spirit, wrath-fire, divine nature, stars, spiritual fall, Jakob Böhme</keywords>

# The Rising of the Dawn in the 21st Year. 187

57. Whether now **God** himself thus fashioned and kindled this enmity and raging fire-source in Lucifer, the masters of works and grace must answer for and prove in nature: **If not, then this corrupt fire-source, which stands in place of love, shall also be condemned.**

# 58. The beautiful source-spirit in the divine power is Mercurius or the Sound, wherein the distinction and the heavenly joys arise. This spirit takes its origin in the fire-flash, that is, in the bitter quality, and ascends in the flash through the substantial water, wherein he softens himself, that he becomes bright, and in the harsh quality he is captured, there he stirs all spirits, from this morning the Sound arises, in the flash stands his ascending source, and in the substantial water in the love his body or root.

59. Now this Sound is the divine realm of joy, the **Triumphing, wherein the divine and gentle play of love in God arises, thereto the forms, formations and all kinds of figures.**

60. But you should know all this, that this quality penetrates quite gently and lovely with its power through all spirits, in such place and manner, as in a human heart a lovely and gentle fire of joy arises, wherein the animal (soulish) spirit triumphs, as if it were in heaven.

61. Now this spirit is not born for the formation of the Corpus, but for distinction and for mobility, especially for joy and for distinction in the formation.

62. When the animal spirit is born in the Center of the heart in the midst of the seven source-spirits, so that the will of the seven spirits is incorporated together, then the Sound carries it out to the Corpus, and is its chariot, upon which the spirit rides, and executes that which was decided in the council of the 7 spirits.

63. For the Sound travels through the animal spirit into the Nature of **God** or into the Galitter of the seventh source-spirit in the divine power, which is its initial mother, and inquales with the same in the order, and also in the distinction of the formation.**

64. Therefore had King Lucifer his haughty striving in the Sound.

# - **Morgenröte im 21. Jahrgang. 187**: The title. "Morgenröte" translates to "Dawn". The previous translation established "The Rising of the Dawn". "im 21. Jahrgang" translates to "in the 21st Year". "187" is a number, likely a page or section number, which should be kept.
- **57. Ob nun ...**: This paragraph discusses whether God created the enmity in Lucifer. It uses archaic language ("grimmenden Feuerquell", "geschäften", "berweifen") and some obscure, likely misspelled terms ("Werfebung", "Genadenmäbler").
- **58. Der schöne Quellgeist ...**: This paragraph introduces the next "source-spirit" ("Quellgeist"), which is "Marcurius oder Lhon" (Mercurius or the Sound). It describes its origin and nature using alchemical and mystical terms ("Feurplift", "bittern qualität", "fülle Wasser", "herben qualität").
- **59. Nun dieser Lhon ...**: This continues the description of "Lhon" (the Sound), identifying it with joy ("Freudenreich") and "Triumphiren" (Triumphing).
- **60. Du sollst aber ...**: This is an address to the reader ("Du"), explaining the quality of this spirit using the analogy of joy in a human heart. It contains more archaic/corrupted terms ("alt sie wissen", "Mügen", "feelische").
- **61. Nun dieser Geist ...**: Explains the function of this spirit: not for forming the body ("Corpus"), but for distinction ("Unterschieb") and mobility ("Beweglichkeit").
- **62. Wenn der animalische Geist ...**: Describes a process involving the "animal spirit", the "seven source-spirits", and "Lhon" acting as a chariot ("Wagen") to execute ("erequiert") what was decided. Contains Latinisms ("Centro", "corporiert", "erequiert").
- **63. Dann der Lhon ...**: Explains the movement of the "Lhon" through the "animal spirit" into God's Nature or "Galitter". Introduces the specific term "inqualiert". It contains a likely typo ("fiebenden" for "siebenden").
- **64. Darum da König Rucifer ...**: A short, grammatically incomplete sentence connecting King Lucifer to the "Lhon". Contains likely misspellings ("buchmütiges", "Mögles") and archaic syntax.
- **# 187**: A series of repeated numbers, which must be preserved exactly as they are.

This seems to be a consistent process. I have solutions for the tricky parts and I will make sure to adhere strictly to all formatting rules. The translation is ready.

6. This seventh spirit has a color and kind like all spirits, for he is the body of all spirits, wherein they are born, as in a Corpus: also from this spirit all figures and forms are fashioned, from which the angels are also created, and it establishes all naturalness therein.

11. Where one always sees aright the form of all 7 wheels, and the single wheel in the midst of all 7 wheels, and yet cannot understand how the wheel is made, but one wonders always at the wheel, as it shows itself ever more wondrously with its rising, and yet also remains only in its place.

12. In such a manner the Godhead is ever born, and yet also never perishes, and in such a manner life in angels and men is also ever born.

13.
