## ->Now behold.<-

32. **W**hen King Lucifer was created so glorious, beautiful, and godly, as a cherub <note>original: "Jerubin"</note> and king in God, he allowed his beautiful form to deceive him, as he saw what a noble, beautiful, and glorious spirit rose up within him. Then his seven source-spirits <term>Quellgeister; the seven fundamental active qualities or forces that Böhme believes constitute both God and nature</term> thought they would raise themselves up and ignite themselves; they believed they would then be as beautiful, glorious, and powerful as the vital spirit <term>animalische Geist; from the Latin 'anima' (soul), referring here to the subtle 'breath of life' or soul-spirit rather than 'animalistic' in the modern sense</term>. With this, they intended to rule in the whole territory with their own strength and power as a new God.

33. They saw clearly that the vital spirit was co-operating <term>inqualirete; Böhme’s term for the way different qualities or forces interact and work within one another</term> with the heart of God; therefore, it was their resolution that they would raise themselves and ignite themselves, in the hope of being as clear, deep, and almighty as the deepest ground in the center of the heart of God.

34. For they intended to raise the natural body—which was incorporated together out of the nature-spirit of God—into the hidden birth of God, so that their seven source-spirits might be as high and as all-comprehending as the vital spirit. And the vital spirit was meant to triumph over the center of the heart of God, and the heart of God was to be subject to it, and the seven spirits of God were to build and form everything with their vital spirit.

35. And this pride and self-will was entirely against the birth of God, for the body of the angel was to remain in its station <note>original: "Sede," from the Latin 'sedes' for seat or position</note>, and be a nature, and hold still like a humble mother, and not possess the omniscience and its own rational comprehensibility of the heart or the deepest birth of the Holy Trinity; instead, the seven spirits were to be born in their natural body just as they are in God.

->I 2<- 36. And

<summary>This page describes the theological mechanics of Lucifer's fall, explaining how his internal "source-spirits" attempted to seize the power of the "vital spirit" to become equal to God's heart. It emphasizes that pride arose from a refusal to remain in a humble, natural station.</summary>

<keywords>Lucifer, Fall of Heaven, Seven Source-Spirits, Vital Spirit, Adam, Pride, In-qualifying, Holy Trinity, Theosophy</keywords>

# 196 The Rising of the Dawn. Chap. 16.

36. And their comprehensibility was not to be in the hidden core, or in the innermost birth (of God), but the animal spirit, which they birthed in their Center of the heart, was to be inqualified with the innermost birth (of God), and help to form and fashion all figures according to the 7 spirits' (pleasure and will, so that in the divine womb everything would be one heart and will).

37. For so is the birth (of God) also, the 7th nature-spirit, spiritual and spiritual in its being, which it births, but holds as a suffering, as a spirit, as a spirit, and lets the Father's will, which is the other 6 spirits, form and fashion in itself, as they will.

38. Also no spirit reaches particularly with its corporative being for the heart (of God), but it channels its will with the others into the Center for the birth of the heart, so that the heart and the 7 spirits (of God) are one will.

39. For that is the comprehensibility's (Sefene), that it does not elevate itself into the incomprehensibility, for the power, which is corporified together in the Center or in Witten out of all 7 spirits, is incomprehensible and inscrutable, but not harmless, for it is not one spirit's power alone, but of all seven.

40. So now one spirit in its own corpus, outside of its instanding birth, cannot grasp into the whole heart (of God), and approve and fathom everything, for outside of its instanding birth it comprehends only its own birth in the heart (of God), but all 7 spirits together comprehend the whole heart (of God).

[Trait in man, but refine according to the wildness, nut (of God), as in the soul-spirit, not in the fiery essence of the souls, but in the light's (essence), therein (God's) image of the "bet.]

41. But in the instanding birth of the spirits, where one always births the other, there each spirit comprehends all 7 spirits, but only in the rising knowledge of life.

42. The heart, however, is now a particular When it is birthed, is one, a particular person, and yet not separated from the spirits.

separated, but the spirits cannot transform themselves into the others in their first birth.

43. And so the second cannot transform itself into the third, which is the going-out of the spirit, but each birth remains in its Sode, and all births together are yet only the one Sote.

44. But because the body of Lucifer was created out of nature and the outmost birth, it was quite wrong that he elevated himself into the inmost and deepest, which he could not do in divine right, but he had to elevate himself, and kindle himself, so that the Luciferin the sharpest bringing-through and infecting were prepared.

45. I think so, you beautiful nigromanticus, you have once transformed yourself, you may well also teach men your art, whether they might perhaps also become such mighty gods, as you have become.

46. You blind and arrogant necromantic Gauß, herein lies your art, you transform the elements of your body through your Conjurationes and Instrumenta of the Eucilita, which you use for it, and I think, you are right in this, but is it not against the birth (of God), so prove that.

47. How do you presume that you can transform yourselves into another shape? You let the devil make a fool of you thus and yet are blind in the art, and even if you had learned it ever so well, you still do not know the purpose in it; for the heart therein is the transformation of the Lucifer, as Lord Lucifer did, when he wanted to be (God).

# Now you say, how can that be?

48. Behold, when the corporic Lucifer-nature directs its working into magic, then the animal spirit, which it birthed, and which is established in the quality of the stars and elements in the hidden and deepest Center, is already a magician, and has transformed itself into magic.

49. The animal body, however, cannot do so soon after, but must be cleansed through characters and conjurations, and several instruments useful therein, so that the animal spirit makes the animal body unjudgeable, and transforms it into the shape, as was Lucifer's initial will.

50. The animal flesh cannot at all transform itself or be in another birth, but it becomes a lesser

43. Likewise, the second cannot transform into the third, which is the outgoing of the spirit; rather, every birth remains in its seat <note>original: "Sede"</note>, and yet all births together are but the one God.

44. But because Lucifer’s body was created out of nature and the outermost birth, it was quite wrong for him to elevate himself into the innermost and deepest birth, which he could not do by divine right; instead, he had to elevate and ignite himself, so that the source-spirits <term>source-spirits (Quellgeister): Böhme’s term for the seven fundamental forces of nature and divinity that "well up" to create reality</term> were set to penetrate and infect with the greatest sharpness.

45. I suppose, you fine necromancer <note>original: "Nigromanticus"</note>, you have certainly transformed yourself; you may as well teach men your art, to see if they might also become such powerful gods as you have become.

46. You blind and haughty necromantic charlatans <note>original: "Gauckler"</note>, your art lies in this: you transform the elements of your body through your conjurations <note>original: "Conjurationes"</note> and the instruments <note>original: "Instrumenta"</note> of qualities that you use for that purpose, and you think you are in the right; but if this is not against the birth of God, then prove it.

47. How do you suppose you can transform yourselves into another shape? You let the devil make fools of you and are yet blind in your art; even if you had learned it ever so well, you still do not know its purpose; for the heart within it is the transformation of the source-spirits, just as Lord Lucifer did when he wanted to be God.

## ->Do you ask now: how can this be?<-

48. **B**ehold, when the bodily source-spirits set their will upon sorcery <note>original: "Zauberey"</note>, then the animal spirit <note>Böhme uses "animal" (animalische) to refer to the soul-spirit or "anima," the animating force of a living being</note> which they birth, and which rules in the quality of the stars and elements in the hidden and deepest center <note>original: "Centro"</note>, is already a sorcerer and has transformed itself into sorcery.

49. The animal body, however, cannot follow immediately, but must be enchanted through characters <note>magical symbols or sigils</note> and conjurations, and various instruments serving that purpose, so that the animal spirit makes the animal body invisible and transforms it into the shape that was the initial will of the source-spirits.

50. The animal flesh cannot easily transform itself or place itself into another birth, but it becomes into a lowly and

and brought into a thin form, like a cloth or wood and the like, that has its fine body qualifying in the elements.

1. But the overfilled spirits can transform themselves into another shape, but also only as long as the birth of nature drives over their pulse. For when they externalize themselves with their inner turning and penetrating, so that a source-spirit becomes Primus, then their art lies vanquished, and their divinity in the first source-spirit, in which they began their art, has an end.

2. If it is to last longer now, it must be made anew according to the reigning source-spirit, or the devil must be with his animal spirit in the feeling spirits of the Corpus, who transforms him differently, otherwise his art has an end here. For nature does not let itself be juggled with every hour as the spirits wish, but everything must happen according to the spirit, which is Primus at the time.

3. The same spirit of God, which is Primus in nature, does not perform the jugglery, but it is made in the fierceness of the Salitter, which has kindled Lucifer with its elevation, which is its eternal kingdom.

4. But when the power of the same spirit subsides, the kindled fire can no longer serve the juggler. For the wrath-fire in nature is not in this present time the devil's own house of power, since love lies hidden in the Center of the wrath-fire, and Lucifer with his angels lies captured in the outward wrath-fire until the judgment of God, where he will receive the wrath-fire separate from love as an eternal possession, and will without doubt yield his head along with his juggler.

5. This I write only as a warning to those who have sorcery as their foundation, not in such a way that I would want to write of demonstrable sorcery, I have not learned it either, but the animal spirit sees their juggleries, which I do not understand in the body.

6. Because it leads completely and utterly astray from the love and wholeness of the birth of God, and is a contradiction in the love of God, bringing man without it to do pernicious things to the great world, so the spirit wants to have the juggler and changer of God's order defiled with the wrath-commandment of nature for an eternal participation, there they may prove their new divinity within.

<meta>This page continues the discussion from page 198 regarding the fall of Lucifer and the mechanics of spiritual corruption. Having previously described how spirits can manipulate their forms, Böhme now turns to the specific moment when Lucifer's rebellion "kindled" the wrath of God within the natural realm.</meta>

Chap. 16. ->The Rising of the Dawn.<- 199

### ->On the Kindling of the Wrath-Fire.<-

57. **W**hen King Lucifer, along with all his angels, kindled himself <note>Böhme uses "kindled" to describe the transition from a state of cold, peaceful light to one of fiery, ego-driven pride</note>, the wrath-fire immediately rose up in the body, and the lovely light in the <term>animal spirit<gloss>original: "animalischen Geiste"; derived from the Latin "anima" (soul), this refers to the animating or soul-spirit that gives life and movement to a creature, rather than "animalistic" in a modern sense</gloss></term> was extinguished, and he became a fierce devilish spirit, all according to the kindling and the will of the <term>source-spirits<gloss>the seven fundamental qualities or "fountain-spirits" that Böhme believes constitute the nature of both God and the universe</gloss></term>.

58. Now, this animal spirit was connected with the Godhead in nature and could <term>inter-qualify<gloss>original: "inqualiren"; to work together or share the same essential qualities and operations</gloss></term> with the same, as if it were one thing. It then struck out from the bodies of the devils into the nature of God like a murderer and a thief who desired to murder and rob everything and bring it under his power; and he kindled all seven spirits in nature, so that there was nothing but a harsh, bitter, fiery, and cracking, burning tearing and raging.

59. You must not think that the devil thus powerfully overcame the Godhead: No, but he kindled the wrath of God, which would have rested in secret for all eternity, and he made a pit of murder out of the <term>Salitter<gloss>Böhme's term for the divine "soil" or essential substance of the heavenly kingdom, likely derived from "saltpeter"</gloss></term> of God; for when one puts fire into straw, it burns. God did not become a devil because of this.

60. Furthermore, the wrath-fire of God in nature does not reach into the innermost core of the Heart, which is the Son of God, much less into the hidden holiness of the Spirit, but only as far as the birth of the six source-spirits in the <term>place<gloss>original Latin: "Locum"</gloss></term> where the striving <note>original: "stebende," likely an archaic variant of "strebende" (striving/ascending)</note> is born.

61. For in that place, or in this birth, Lord Lucifer became a creature, and he did not extend his dominion any deeper. However, if he had remained in love, his animal spirit would have reached into the <term>Center<gloss>original Latin: "Centrum"</gloss></term> of the Heart of God, for love penetrates through the entire Godhead.

62. But when his love was extinguished, the animal spirit could no longer enter the Heart of God, and his undertaking was in vain; instead, he raged and fumed in nature—that is, in the seventh source-spirit of God.

63. Because the power of all seven spirits stood in this one, all seven were also infected with wrath, but now only in the external and perceptible qualification. For the devil could not touch the Heart, nor could he touch the innermost birth of the source-spirits, because the glory of his seven spirits had already died in the first flash of the kindling.
->J 4<- ->died,<- <note>These are signature marks and a catchword for the printer to ensure the pages are bound in the correct order.</note>

<summary>Böhme explains how Lucifer’s pride "kindled" God's latent wrath, transforming his own soul into a "murderous" fire that corrupted the outer layers of nature while remaining unable to penetrate the divine heart of love.</summary>
<keywords>Lucifer, wrath-fire, animal spirit, source-spirits, Salitter, divine nature, corruption of light, Seven Spirits of God</keywords>

# The Rising of the Dawn on the 2nd Day

Him, and immediately on the first 2nd day of the animal hostage, hold captive.

64. In this hour, King Lucifer prepared for him more firmly the division and eternal perdition, which is now firmer in the outermost source-spirit of the nature of God, or in the outermost birth of this world.

65. But when nature ignited itself so terribly, the baptism of joys became a house of tribulation, for the harsh duality was ignited in its own baptism, which was now a completely arid, cold, and dark essence, like the cold and hard winter, which now drew the Salitter together, and dried it up, so that it became quite rough, cold, and sharp, like the stones, therein the Light was captured and sucked up with it, and formed into a hard, cold, dark essence.

66. When this happened, the light in nature in the outermost birth also went out, and everything became quite dark and corrupted, the water became quite cold and thick, and some remained in the clefts, which is the origin of the elemental water on Earth.

67. For before the times of the world, the water was very thin like the air, and life was born therein, which is now so deadly and corrupted, and thus it rolls and flows.

68. From the gracious love, which begins in the flash of life, became a fierce and bitter poison, a true pit of damnation, a sting of death: from the raging became a hard substance of stones, a house of misery.

69. In summary, it was all a completely dark and miserable essence in the whole domain, in the outermost birth of King Lucifer's kingdom.

70. But you must not think that nature was thus corrupted and ignited down to its innermost ground, but only the outermost birth; the inner one, however, in which the 7 source-spirits are born, reserves its right for itself, into which the ignited devil could not reach.

71. Now, however, the inner birth holds the winnowing fan in its hand, and will one day sweep its threshing floor, and give the chaff to the kingdom of Lucifer for eternal food. For if the devil could have reached into the innermost birth, the entire domain of his kingdom would have immediately become the kindled, burning division.

# Day 16. The Rising of the Dawn on the 2nd Day

72. But thus he must lie captive as a prisoner in the outermost birth until the Last Day, which is now at hand, and to be awaited very soon.

73. Lucifer, however, has ignited his source-spirits even into the innermost birth, and his source-spirits now give birth to a singular devil-spirit, who is an eternal enemy of God.

74. For when God manifested Himself in His outermost birth in nature, it was not His intentional will that He should ignite Himself, nor did He do so, but He sucked up the Salitter, and for the devil an eternal perdition is prepared.

75. For he cannot be cast out of God into another kingdom of the angels, but a Locus must remain for him as a domain. Thus He would not give him the ignited Salitter at once for an eternal domain, for the inner birth of the spirits is still hidden therein, for God had something else in mind to do, and King Lucifer was to remain a prisoner, until another angelic host from the same Salitter would take his place, which is mankind.

76. Now then, you jurists of Lucifer, call a king to account, whether he was right to have ignited the sun's essence in nature: if not, then he shall burn in it forever, and your followers must suffer the truth with him.

77. These, then, are the 7 aspects or forms of sin's beginning and of the sole enmity against God.

78. Now to speak briefly of the 4 new births of Lucifer, which he has begotten in himself in his corporeal government, for which he was cast out of his Locus, and became the most horrible devil.

# Of Pride, the first Son

Now the question is:

What then moved Lucifer to want to be above God?

79. Hereby you should know that he had no drive at all outside himself for his pride, but his beauty deceived him: when he saw that he was the most beautiful prince in heaven, he despised the friendly extinguishing and begetting of the Godhead, and thought he would with his princely power in

It introduces the concept of humans as replacements for the fallen angels.</meta>

Chapter 16. ->Morning Glow at the Sunrise.<- 201

72. But thus he must lie captive as a prisoner in the **outermost birth** <note>In Böhme’s thought, the "outermost birth" refers to our physical, corrupted world of matter, which acts as a veil or prison for fallen spirits.</note> until the **final day** <note>Judgment Day</note>, which is even now at hand and to be expected very soon.

73. Lucifer, however, has ignited his **source-spirits** <note>The seven fundamental qualities or "fountains" that constitute divine and natural life.</note> even into the innermost birth, and his source-spirits now give birth to an **animalistic devilish spirit**, which is an eternal enemy of God.

74. For when God became "angry" in His outermost birth within nature, it was not His intentional will that He wanted to ignite Himself, nor did He do it; rather, He contracted the **Salitter** <term>Salitter: A term Böhme uses for the divine substance or "sap" of the universe, the spiritual earth or salt of heaven</term>, and thereby prepared an eternal lodging for the devil.

75. For he cannot be cast out of God into another kingdom of angels, but a **Place** <note>original: "Locus"</note> must remain for him as a dwelling. Thus He did not want to give him the ignited Salitter immediately as an eternal dwelling, for the inner birth of the spirits still stood hidden within it. For God had something else in mind to do with this, and King Lucifer was to remain a prisoner until another angelic host from the same Salitter would take his place—which are **human beings**.

76. Now then, come forth, you **lawyers of Lucifer** <note>A jab at scholars or theologians who use logic to justify sin or defend the devil's influence</note>, and answer here for your king: whether he was in the right to ignite the fire of wrath in nature. If not, then he shall burn in it eternally, and your lies against the truth shall burn with him.

77. These, then, are the 7 **forms** <note>original: "Species," referring here to the seven qualities of nature or the seven ways sin manifests</note> or shapes of the beginning of sin and eternal enmity against God.

78. Now follows, in brief, an account of the 4 new "little sons" of Lucifer, which he gave birth to within himself during his bodily reign, because of which he was cast out of his **Place** <note>original: "Loco"</note> and became the most abominable devil.

### ->Concerning Pride, the First Son.<-

->Now the question arises:<-

> **What then moved Lucifer to want to be above God?**

79. **H**ere you should know that he had no impulse toward his pride from outside himself; rather, his own beauty deceived him. ## 81. ## 83. This son is the true gout of the present world, for he takes his origin in the flash of pride and of the spirit, and sits upon the root of life, like a thorny and bitter gall.

## 85. This son is the true burning hellish fire, and also takes its origin from pride, for when he could not satisfy his pride and spirit with his hostile drive, he kindled the fire of wrath in himself, and roared with it into the nature of God like a grim lion, from which the wrath of God then arose and sifted everything.

99. This birth of the flesh is now not the soul's dwelling-place, but it enters therein in battle with its light in divine power, and fights against the murder of the devil. 100. 101. 102. ### In the beginning God created heaven and earth, etc.
### Genesis 1.

48. **T**hese words must be properly considered for what they truly are; for the word **Am** <note>original: "Am," the first part of "Am Anfang" (In the beginning). Böhme is performing a mystical analysis of the physical sounds of the German words.</note> forms itself in the heart and travels to the lips, where it is caught, and goes sounding back again to the place from which it departed.

49. This signifies that the sound went out from the heart of God and encompassed the entire location <note>original: "Locum"</note> of this world; but when it was found to be evil, the sound stepped back into its own place.

50. The word **An** <note>The first syllable of "Anfang" (Beginning).</note> thrusts out from the heart to the mouth and has a long emphasis; but when it is pronounced, it closes in the middle of its seat against the upper palate, being half outside and half inside.

51. This signifies that the heart of God felt a loathing for the corruption and thrust the corrupted essence away from itself, but still grasped and held it in the middle, near the heart.

52. 57. The word **Created** <note>original: "Schuf"</note> forms itself above and below the tongue, bringing the teeth together in both jaws, compressing itself; and once it is formed and spoken, it opens the mouth again as quickly as a flash of lightning.

58. 61. This signifies that when God created heaven and earth, as well as all creatures, He nevertheless remained in His divine, eternal, almighty seat and never departed from it, and that He alone is everything. # Aurora Rising. Chapter 18.

### -> This is a Great Mystery. <-

71. **T**he word **Er** <note>original: "Er"; Böhme is analyzing the syllables of "Erden" (Earth). "Er" represents the harsh, initial sound of the material world</note> signifies the kindled, harsh, and bitter quality, the earnest wrath of God, which trembles in the back of the palate; the tongue is afraid of it, and huddles in the lower palate, fleeing as if from an enemy.

72. The word **Den** <note>The second syllable of "Erden"</note> catches itself again upon the tongue, and the spirit generates the power out of the word, and travels another way with it out through the nose; it also travels upward into the brain before the royal throne.

73. This signifies that the outermost **Salitter** <term>Salitter: Böhme’s term for the divine-material substance or "sap" of the earth, which contains both heavenly and earthly qualities</term> of the Earth is eternally rejected by God’s light and holiness.

74. But that the spirit catches the power of the word and travels another way through the nose into the brain before the throne of the senses, signifies that God wants to draw the heart of the Earth out from the wrath of wickedness and use it for His eternal, royal praise.

### -> Observe. <-

75. **H**e wants to draw the kernel and the best, or the good spirit, out of the Earth, and give it a new birth for His honor and glory.

76. Here, O Man, consider what kind of seed you will sow into the Earth; such a seed will also sprout and eternally bloom and bear fruit, either in love or in wrath.

77. But when the good is separated from the evil, then you will live in your portion acquired here, whether it be in heaven or in the hellish fire: wherever you now labor toward, there your soul will travel when you die.

78. ### -> Concerning the Creation of Light in this World. <-

81. **A**t this point, close the eyes of your flesh a little, for they are of no use to you here, since they are blind and dead; and open the eyes of your spirit, and I will rightly show you the creation of God.

### -> Observe. <-

82. **N**ow, when God drove together the corrupted **Salitter** <term>Salitter: Böhme’s term for the divine-material substance or "sap" of the earth, which contains both heavenly and earthly qualities</term> of the earth and stones—which had been generated in the outermost birth through the kindling—into a single lump, the second birth in nature in the deep above the earth was not pure and bright, because the wrath of God still burned within it.

83. And even though the innermost birth was light and bright, the outermost birth, which stood in the wrath-fire, could not comprehend it; rather, it was entirely dark.

84. For Moses writes: *And it was dark upon the deep*, etc. Genesis 1. The word **Upon** signifies the outermost birth, and the **In** signifies the innermost birth.

85. However, if the innermost birth had been dark, then the wrath of God would have rested eternally in this world, and it would never have become light; but in this way, the wrath did not touch the Heart of God.

86. Therefore, He remained a sweet, friendly, kind, gentle, pure, and merciful God according to His Heart in the innermost birth in the place <note>original: "Loco"</note> of this world, and His gentle love penetrates from His Heart into the outermost birth of wrath and extinguishes it. Therefore He said: *Let there be light.*

92. Now look, you child of man, what a gate of heaven, of hell, and of the earth, as well as the entire Godhead, the Spirit unlocks for you!

93. You should not think that God spoke at that time in a human manner, or that it was merely a powerless word, like that of a human. A human’s word also takes shape in such form, proportion, quality, and skill, but the half-dead human <note>Böhme refers to "half-dead" humanity as the state of being spiritually dull or fallen from original divine clarity.</note> does not understand it; and this understanding is quite noble and precious, for it is born only in the knowledge of the Holy Spirit.

94. But God’s Word, which He spoke in power at that time, encompassed heaven and earth, and the heaven of all heavens—indeed, the entire Godhead.

95. For it is written: **And it was dark upon the deep, and the Spirit of God moved upon the waters.**

96. The deep signifies the innermost birth, and the darkness signifies the outermost corrupted birth in which the <term>wrath: the contractive, harsh, or "dark" quality of nature that exists when not tempered by divine light</term> burned; the water signifies the softening of the Spirit.

97. That the Spirit hisses through the teeth signifies that the Spirit has passed from the heart of God through the wrath; but that the teeth remain closed while the Spirit hisses, and do not open, signifies that the wrath has not <term>comprehended: or "contained" (begriffen)</term> the Holy Spirit.

98. 99. For He goes through all closed chambers and births, and requires no unlocking, just as the teeth cannot hold Him back from passing through them.

113. Since the outermost birth in nature is twofold—that is, both evil and good—there is a constant tormenting, squeezing, lamenting, and howling; all creatures in this life must indeed suffer torment, and this evil world is rightly called a murder-pit of the devil.

116. 118. The tongue, however, signifies the soul; it is born from the seven spirits of nature and is their son. When the seven spirits so desire, the tongue must move according to their pleasure and must demand their concerns.

### 230 ->Aurora: The Day-Spring.<- Chap. 19.

The light that rose in the seven spirits of nature <note>The "seven spirits" or "fountain-spirits" (Quellgeister) are Böhme’s fundamental forces of divine and natural existence</note> had no specific seat or location but shone everywhere, though not as brightly as the sun. ## ->The 19th Chapter.<-

->Concerning the Heaven.<-

1. **T**he true heaven—which is our own human heaven where the soul goes when it departs from the body, and where Christ our King has entered, and from where he came from his Father and was born, becoming a man in the body of the Virgin Mary—has until now been almost hidden from the children of men, who have held many different opinions about it.
2. The scholars have also scratched at one another over it with many strange writings, and have fallen into each other's hair with insults and shaming. By this, the holy name of **God** has been profaned, his members wounded, his temple destroyed, and the holy heaven desecrated with this blasphemy and hostility.
3. People have always and in every way imagined that heaven was many hundreds or many thousands of miles away from this earth, and that **God** dwelt alone in that same heaven. Certain physicists <note>original: "Phisici" — in this era, the term referred to natural philosophers who studied the physical world and its laws</note> have even ventured to measure that height and brought forth very strange things.
4. Indeed, before I received this knowledge and revelation from **God**, I myself held it to be so: that the true heaven was only that which closes itself with a round circle, entirely light blue, high above the stars, believing that **God** had his special being only within it, and ruled this world only through the power of his Holy Spirit.
5. But as this gave me many a hard blow—doubtless from the Spirit who took pleasure in me—I have...

5. I finally fell into a hard melancholy and sadness as I looked upon the great deep of this world, as well as the sun and stars, the clouds, rain, and snow, and considered in my spirit the whole creation of this world.
6. Therein I found in all things both evil and good, love and wrath—in the irrational creatures, such as in wood, stones, earth, and the elements, as well as in humans and animals.
7. Furthermore, I considered the little spark <note>original: "Fünklein" — Böhme uses this term to refer to the *scintilla animae*, the tiny, divine fragment of light remaining in the human soul.</note> of man: what he might be esteemed for before **God** in comparison to this great work of heaven and earth.
8. Because I found that there was evil and good in all things, in the elements as well as in the creatures, and that in this world things went as well for the godless as for the pious; also that the barbarous nations possessed the best lands, and that fortune favored them even more than the pious.
9. I became, for that reason, entirely melancholy and highly distressed; no Scripture could comfort me, though I was quite well acquainted with it. In this, the devil certainly would not have been idle, for he often instilled "heathen thoughts" <note>This refers to doubts about divine providence or the suspicion that the world is ruled by chance rather than a just God.</note> into me, which I will here remain silent about.
10. But when, in such tribulation, I earnestly raised my spirit (though I understood little or nothing of what it was) into **God** as in a great storm, and enclosed my whole heart and mind, along with all other thoughts and will, within it—wrestling without ceasing with the love and mercy of **God**, and not letting go until he blessed me (that is, until he enlightened me with his Holy Spirit so that I might understand his will and be rid of my sadness)—then the spirit broke through.
11. But as I, in my determined zeal, thus stormed so hard against **God** and all the gates of hell <note>original: "Höllen Porten"</note> as if all my strength were still present, being willing to risk my life upon it (which certainly would not have been in my power without the assistance of **God's** Spirit), suddenly, after several hard storms, my spirit broke through the gates of hell into the innermost birth of the Godhead <note>original: "Gottheit"</note> and was there embraced with love, just as a bridegroom embraces his dear bride.

12. But what kind of triumph there was in the Spirit, I cannot write or speak; it cannot be compared to anything, except perhaps to that moment where Life is born in the midst of Death, and it is like the resurrection from the dead.

It happened as it does with a young tree planted in the earth: at first, it is young and tender and pleasant to look at, especially when it begins to grow well. However, it does not bear fruit immediately; even if it blossoms, the flowers fall off. Many a cold wind, frost, and snow pass over it before it matures and bears fruit.

15. So it was with this spirit; the first fire was only a seed, not a permanent, persistent light. Since that time, many a cold wind has passed over it, but the will was never extinguished.

16. This tree also often tried to see if it could bear fruit and showed itself with blossoms; but the blossoms were knocked off the tree until this very day, when it stands in its first fruit during its growth.

17. From this light I now have my knowledge, as well as my will and drive, and I wish to write this knowledge according to my gifts and let **God** rule. For I am far too weak to recognize His purpose; although the spirit allows some future things to be recognized in the light, I am—as far as the outer man is concerned—far too weak to comprehend such things.

There is no need for that at all; rather, the soul is placed into the innermost birth. There it is with **God** and in **God** and with all the holy angels, and can quickly be above and just as quickly below; it is held back by nothing.

50. For in the innermost birth, the Upper and Lower Deity are One body, One open portal: The holy angels walk just as much in the innermost birth of this world with our King **Jesus Christ**, as they do in the upper realm <note>original: "Revier", meaning district or territory</note>.

51. And where would the soul of man then wish to be, if not with its King and Savior **Jesus Christ**? For in **God**, far and near are as one thing, one comprehensibility—everywhere Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.

52. The portal of the **Deity** in the upper heaven is nothing else, and no brighter, than in this world. And where could there be greater joy than in the place where every hour beautiful, dear, newborn children and angels come to **Christ**, having pressed through death into life? They will undoubtedly know how to tell of many struggles. And where could there be greater joy than where, in the midst of death, life is continually being born without ceasing?

53. For every soul brings a new triumph with it, and there is nothing but pure, friendly welcoming and greeting <note>original: "beneveniren", a Germanization of the Latin *bene venire*</note>. Think of when the souls of children come to the parents who bore them in their bodies—might there not be heaven in that place? Or do you think I write too earthily? If you come to this window, you will not say it is earthly; though I must use an earthly tongue, there is nevertheless a true heavenly understanding beneath it, which I can neither write nor speak of in my outermost birth <note>Böhme refers to the "outermost birth" as the physical, material state of existence</note>.

54. I know well that the word of the three births will not be able to be grasped in every heart, especially where the heart is too drowned in the flesh and bolted shut with the outermost birth. But I cannot provide it any other way, for it is so; and even if I write pure spirit—as indeed in truth it is nothing else—the heart still perceives only flesh, so far as I can see.

->**On the Form of the Earth.**<-

55. **M**any writers have indeed written that heaven and earth were created out of nothing; however, I wonder that among such excellent men not one has been found who could describe the true ground, since the very same **God** who exists now has existed from eternity.

56. Now, where there is nothing, nothing comes to be; every thing must have a root, otherwise nothing grows. Had the seven spirits of nature <note>Böhme’s "seven spirits" are the foundational qualities of all existence: the sour, sweet, bitter, heat, love, sound, and corpus.</note> not existed from eternity, there would have been no angel, nor any heaven, nor any earth.

57. But the earth came from the corrupted <term>Salitter</term> <note>Salitter: Böhme’s term for the divine "soil" or the chemical-spiritual essence of the heavenly kingdom. It is a play on the word "saltpeter."</note> of the outermost birth; you cannot deny this. When you look upon the earth and stones, you must indeed say that a life is within them; otherwise, neither gold nor silver, nor herbs nor grass, would grow within them.

->Now one might ask:<-

->**Are all three births within it then?**<-

58. **Y**es, life presses through death; the outermost birth is death, the second is life, which stands in the wrath-fire and in the love, and the third is the holy life. <note>In Böhme’s theology, "births" (*Geburten*) refer to different dimensions of reality or stages of divine manifestation.</note>

->**Instruction.**<-

59. **T**he external earth is a bitter stench and is dead; every person understands this. But the <term>Salitter</term> has been murdered by the Wrath; you cannot deny that God’s wrath is in the earth, otherwise it would not be so harsh, bitter, sour, and poisonous, nor would it bring forth such poisonous, evil worms. But if you were to say that **God** created it so by His own purpose, you would be saying that **God** Himself is wickedness.

60. Please tell me, why was the devil cast out? You will certainly say, for the sake of his pride, because he wanted to be above **God**. Take a guess, friend <note>original: "Rath Fritz", a colloquial idiomatic address to the reader, similar to "Guess what, buddy."</note>, with what? What power did he have? If you know something here, speak; if you know nothing, then be silent and listen.

61. He sat in the <term>Salitter</term> of the earth before the times of creation, when it was still thin and stood in heavenly holy birth, and he was in the entire kingdom of this world. There it was not earth and stones, but a heavenly...

<summary>Böhme argues that the Earth was not created from "nothing" but from a corrupted divine substance (Salitter) affected by God's wrath, following the fall of Lucifer.</summary>

80. For "Evening" and "Morning" did not exist before the time of the sun and stars, which were only certainly and truly created on the fourth day—which I intend to prove from certain grounds when I reach the creation of the sun and stars.

You also see how the wrath of God lies hidden and at rest in the outermost birth of nature, and it cannot be awakened unless people awaken it themselves—those who, with their fleshly birth, <term>interact <note>original: "inqualiren" – a word Böhme coined to describe how different qualities or forces (Qualitäten) merge, influence, or work together within a being.</note></term> with the wrath in the outermost birth of nature.
107. Therefore, if someone were condemned to hell, he must not say that God did it, or that He willed it; rather, the human awakens the fire of wrath within himself. When this fire becomes burning, it then interacts as one thing with God’s wrath and the hellish fire.
108. When your light is extinguished, you see in the darkness; and in the darkness, the wrath of God is hidden. If you awaken it, it burns within you.
109. In a stone there is also fire, but if one does not strike it, the fire remains hidden; but if one strikes it, the fire leaps out. If something is then present that is capable of catching the fire, it burns and becomes a great fire. So it is also with man when he kindles the resting fire of wrath.

## -> Concerning the Night. <-

110. **T**he word *Night* <note>Böhme believed that the very sound and formation of words in the mouth revealed the spiritual nature of the thing described.</note> is first formed in the heart, and the spirit grumbles with the harsh quality—though the harsh quality does not fully grasp it—afterward it is formed on the tongue. Because it grumbles in the heart, the tongue meanwhile keeps the mouth shut until the spirit comes and is formed on the tongue; then she opens the mouth quickly and lets the spirit out.

111. The fact that the Word first takes hold in the heart and murmurs <note>original: "grunzet" (literally "grunts"). Böhme uses visceral, often animal-like sounds to describe the raw, vibrational movements of the divine forces before they become articulate speech.</note> with the harsh quality, signifies that the Holy Spirit took hold in the darkness over the heart of God in the <term>sidereal birth</term> <note>sidereal: relating to the stars or the astral plane; Böhme uses this to describe the natural world governed by planetary influences.</note> of the seven <term>source-spirits</term> <note>source-spirits: the seven fundamental properties or "qualities" that Böhme believes constitute both God and the universe.</note>. But the fact that He murmurs with the harsh quality signifies that the darkness was a resistance against the Holy Spirit, a resistance in which the Spirit found no pleasure.

112. However, the fact that He nevertheless goes through the dark street signifies that the Spirit also passes through the darkness—which is still in quiet rest—and births it into the light, provided it remains still and does not ignite the fire.

113. Here, the judging world—which seeks to condemn a person even in the mother’s womb—should rightly take notice. For such a world does not know whether the fire of wrath from the parents has been fully ignited within the fruit <note>i.e., the unborn child</note> or not. The Spirit of God also wanders in the darkness that still stands in rest, and He can certainly birth that darkness into the light. To this end, a person's hour of birth is very beneficial to them, and to many also very harmful, yet it is not a matter of compulsion <note>Böhme argues against hard predestination; while the stars (astrology) influence a person, they do not force the soul’s ultimate fate.</note>.

114. The fact that the mouth also closes when the Spirit takes hold over the heart, and the harsh quality murmurs against and with Him, signifies that the entire region or the entire place <note>original: "Locus"</note> of this world was completely dark in the sidereal and also in the outermost birth, and became light only through the powerful outflowing of the Spirit.

115. But the fact that the bitter spirit does not awaken while the Spirit passes through its place signifies the dark night in the outermost birth of this world; it has never grasped the light, and will never grasp it in all eternity.

116. From this, it follows that creatures see the sidereal light only with their eyes. Otherwise, if darkness were not still present in the outermost birth, the sidereal spirit could see through wood and stones, as well as through the entire earth, and would be hindered by nothing, just as it is in heaven.

117. But now the darkness is separated from the light and remains in the outermost birth. Within it rests the wrath of God until the Last Judgment; then the wrath will be ignited, and the darkness will be the house of eternal perdition. There, Lord Lucifer, along with all godless people who have sown in the field of wrath <note>original: "Zornacker"</note>, shall have their eternal dwelling.

                   ->The Portals of the Deity.<-

Here now, observe the hidden mystery of God.

49. When you look at the depth above the earth, you must not say, "the portal of God is not here," where God dwells in His holiness. No, no, do not think so; rather, the entire holy Trinity—God the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit—dwells in the <term>Center</term> <note>The "Center" in Böhme's thought is the inner point of divine manifestation</note> beneath the firmament of heaven, and that very firmament cannot contain Him.

50. It is indeed all one <term>Body</term> <note>original: *Corpus*</note>, the outermost birth as well as the innermost, together with the firmament of heaven, as well as the <term>sidereal birth</term> <note>The astral or "starry" influence that governs the middle realm of existence</note> within it, in which the wrath of God also operates; but these are positioned against one another, much like the governance within a human being.

51. The flesh signifies 1. the outermost birth, which is the house of death; the 2nd birth in man is the sidereal, in which life resides, and where love and wrath strive with one another.

52. And this is as far as man knows himself; for the sidereal birth generates life within the outermost birth—that is, within the dead flesh.

53. The 3rd birth is born between the sidereal and the outermost, and this is called the <term>animal</term> <note>From the Latin *anima*, meaning soul; this refers to the "soulish" or living breath of man</note> birth or the Soul, and it is as large as the whole man. And the external man does not know or comprehend this birth, nor does the sidereal man comprehend it; rather, each <term>source-spirit</term> <note>original: *Quellgeist*; the fundamental powers or qualities that flow from the divine source</note> only comprehends its own inherent root, which signifies heaven.

54. And this same animal man must press through the firmament of heaven to God and live with God; otherwise, the whole man cannot come to God in heaven.

55. For every person who wishes to be saved must be, within their inherent births, as the whole Godhead is with all three births in this world.

56. Man cannot be entirely pure, without wrath and sins, for the births in the depth of this world are also not entirely pure before the heart of God (Job 15:15); rather, love and wrath always wrestle with one another, because of which God calls Himself an angry, jealous God (Exodus 20:5, Deuteronomy 5:9).

57. Now, just as man is in the governance of his births, so also is the entire Body of God in this world; in the water, however,

...but the gentle life remains. Firstly, in the external Body of God in this world, there is the congealed, harsh, bitter, and heated death, in which the tangible water is also congealed and dead.

58. And within it is the darkness, where King Lucifer with his angels—as well as all fleshly, ungodly people who are still held captive in their living bodies, and the departed spirits of the damned—remain.

59. The Heart of God can neither see, hear, feel, smell, nor comprehend this birth; it is a folly which King Lucifer has fashioned in his <term>pride</term> <note>original: *Hoffart*; Böhme uses this to describe Lucifer's arrogant attempt to rise above God</note>.

<margin>7</margin> 60. The second birth is the <term>sidereal</term> <note>The astral or "starry" influence that governs the middle realm of existence, connecting the physical and spiritual</note> birth—you must understand this as the life of the <term>source-spirits</term> <note>original: *Quellgeister*; these are the fundamental spiritual "fountains" or forces of nature</note>. Within this birth, love and wrath stand against one another; and within it stands the "upper water," which is a Spirit of Life; and within it, or in between, is the firmament of heaven, which is made from the midst of the water.

61. This birth now pierces through the external, congealed death and generates the sidereal life within death—that is, in the congealed earth, water, and the flesh of animals and men, as well as birds, fish, and worms.

62. And the Devil can reach halfway into this birth, as far as the wrath can grasp, but no deeper; and that far is his dwelling. He can reach no deeper, and therefore the Devil cannot know how the other part of this birth has a root.

63. And man has come this far in his knowledge of the world since his Fall: the other root, which is called Heaven, the Spirit has kept hidden from man until now, so that the Devil would not learn of it from man and sprinkle poison into it before man's eyes.

64. This other part of the sidereal birth, which stands in love within the sweet water, is the firmament of heaven, which holds the ignited wrath along with all the devils captive. For they cannot enter into it; and in this Heaven dwells the Holy Spirit, who proceeds from the Heart of God and fights against the <term>fierceness</term> <note>original: *Grimmigkeit*; the quality of God's wrath or the harshness of nature</note>, and builds Himself a temple in the midst of the fierceness of God’s wrath.

65. And in this Heaven dwells the man who fears God, even while still in a living body; for that same Heaven is within man just as much as it is in the "depths" above the earth. And just as the depth is above the earth, so also is man in both love and wrath, until the soul departs; at which point, when the soul separates from the body, it remains alone either in the Heaven of Love or the Heaven of Wrath.

67. And in this heaven, the holy angels dwell with us, and in the other part dwell the devils; and in this heaven, man lives between heaven and hell, and must suffer many a hard blow, temptation, and persecution from the <term>Wrath</term> <note>German: *Grimm*; Böhme uses this to describe the harsh, fiery, and structural foundation of nature that exists without the light of love</note>, and must sometimes allow himself to be tortured and squeezed.

68. The Wrath is called the Cross, and the beloved heaven is called Patience; and the spirit rising within it is called Hope and Faith, which <term>co-qualifies</term> <note>original: *inqualiret*; Böhme’s term for different spiritual qualities blending or working together as one</note> with God and wrestles with the Wrath until it triumphs and overcomes, according to 1 John 5:4.

69. And within this lies the entire Christian teaching; whoever teaches otherwise does not know what they teach, for their teaching has no foot or foundation, and their heart is always flickering and lamenting, and does not know what it should do.

70. For such a spirit always seeks rest and finds it not; then it is impatient and always seeks something new, and when it finds it, it tickles itself therein as if it had found a new treasure, and yet there is no constancy in it, but it constantly seeks <term>withdrawal</term> <note>original: *abstinenz*; here implying a restless avoidance or lack of commitment to a spiritual path</note>.

71. You theologians, the Spirit opens door and gate to you here; if you will not see now, and instead of leading your little sheep to green pastures, you lead them to dry heaths, then you shall answer for that before the earnest and wrathful judgment of God; see to it.

72. I take heaven as my witness that I am performing here what I must do; for the Spirit drives me to it, so that I am also completely captured by it and cannot resist it, regardless of whatever might happen to me hereafter.

76. You must not think, as <note>Johannes Calvin (1509–1564), the French reformer. Böhme frequently clashed with Calvinist views on the Eucharist and the nature of Christ’s presence</note> Johannes Calvus or Calvinus thought, that the body of Christ is an un-almighty being, and comprises no more than the Space within itself.

77. No, you child of man, you err and do not rightly understand the divine power; for every human being comprises in their sidereal source-spirits the entire Space or body of this world, and the Space comprises the human; it is all one body, only different members.

78. How then would the source-spirits in the natural body of Christ not <term>co-qualify</term> <note>original: *inqualiren*; to blend or work together as one force</note> with the source-spirits of nature? For his body is also from the source-spirits of nature, and his heart is <term>Animal-like</term> <note>from the Latin *anima* (soul/breath); meaning a living, sentient being</note> from the third birth, which is the heart of God, which comprises all angels and the heaven of all heavens—yes, it comprises the whole Father.

79. 80. The body of Christ is no longer in hard material comprehensibility, but in the divine comprehensibility of nature, like the angels.

81. For our bodies also will not consist of such hard flesh and bones in the resurrection, but are like the angels; and although all form and power will be therein, also all dexterity even to the organs of birth <note>original: *Geburtsglieder*; reproductive organs</note>, which will stand in another form, as well as the entrails of the intestines, yet we will not have that hard tangibility.

82. For Christ says to Mary Magdalene in Joseph’s garden by the grave after his resurrection: *Touch me not, for I have not yet ascended to my God and to your God* (John 20:17). It was as if he wanted to say: I no longer have the animal body, and although I show myself to you in my old form, otherwise you could not see me in your animal body.

87. 88. Likewise, you see how, according to the Wrath, you are always in Hell among all the devils. If your eyes were only opened, you would see wonders; but you stand between Heaven and Hell and can see neither, walking upon a very narrow bridge.

89. ### 272 ->The Aurora in its Ascent.<- Chapter 21.

61. This is not to be understood as if I were powerful enough in these things, but rather as much as I can grasp. For the Being of God is like a wheel, where many wheels are made within one another crosswise, above one another and below one another, and they always turn together. <note>original: "Rad... quericht." This describes a gimbal-like or multidimensional motion where various aspects of reality intersect.</note> Though one sees the wheel and wonders greatly, yet all at once in its turning one cannot learn nor grasp it; but the more one looks at the wheel, the more one learns its form, and the more one learns, the greater delight one has in the wheel, for one always sees something more wonderful, and a person cannot see and learn enough.

62. So also I: what I do not describe sufficiently in one place concerning this great mystery <term>mystery: 'Geheimniß' – a hidden spiritual truth that is revealed to the seeker through divine grace</term>, you will find in another; and what I cannot describe in this book because of its length and my own inability to fully grasp it, you shall find in the others that follow.

63. For this book is the first growth of this little branch, which turns green within its mother, just like a child who is learning to walk and cannot yet run very well.

64. For even if the spirit sees the wheel and wants to grasp its form in every place, it cannot do so sufficiently because of the wheel's turning. But when it happens that the spirit sees its first-grasped form once again, it always learns something more, and becomes ever more favorable to the wheel, and loves it.

->Now take note.<-

65. **T**he earth has the very same qualities and source-spirits <term>source-spirits: 'Quellgeister' – Böhme’s term for the active, creative forces or energies that flow from the divine essence to form the natural world</term>, as the depth above the earth or as the heavens, and everything belongs together in one body, and the whole of God is that same single body. But that you do not see and know Him entirely is the result of sin, by which you lie enclosed in dead flesh within this great divine body; and the power of the Godhead is hidden from you, just as the marrow in the bones is hidden from the flesh. But if you break through in the spirit through the death of the flesh, then you see the hidden God. Just as the marrow in the bones breaks through and gives power and strength to the flesh, and yet the flesh cannot grasp the marrow, but only its power; so also you cannot see the hidden Godhead in the flesh, but you receive its power and understand through it that God dwells in you.

110. Now, I will prove to you that life lies hidden beneath and within the death of the earth, as well as within the children of the earth.

# Chapter 22. The Day-Spring in its Rising.

## The 22nd Chapter.
### Concerning the Birth of the Stars and the Creation of the 4th Day.

1. **H**ere we now begin to describe the <term>sidereal birth</term> <note>The "sidereal birth" refers to the origin and generation of the stars and the celestial influences they exert on the world.</note>, and it is well to note what the first title of this book means, which is: **The Day-Spring in its Rising** <note>original: "Morgenröte im Aufgang." This is the title of the work, often known by its Latin name, *Aurora*.</note>; for here even a very simple person will be able to see and comprehend the Essence of GOD.
2. Let the reader not strike himself blind through his own unbelief and sluggish comprehension, for I have here all of Nature with all its children as a witness and proof. If you are only rational, then look around you, and look at yourself and consider yourself rightly, and you will soon find from what kind of spirit I write.
3. I will indeed obediently carry out the command of the Spirit; you, for your part, see to it that you do not allow yourself to be shut out of an open door, for here the <term>Gate of Knowledge</term> stands open.
4. And although the Spirit will run contrary to certain <term>astrologers</term> <note>original: "Astrologos." Böhme frequently challenged the academic astrologers of his time, who he felt studied the stars' movements without understanding their spiritual source.</note>, it matters little to me; I must be more obedient to GOD than to men. They are blind in the spirit; if they do not wish to see, then they may remain blind.

-> Now take note. <-

5. **W**hen on the 3rd day the <term>fire-flash</term> <note>original: "Feuer-Blitz." In Böhme’s thought, this is the sudden ignition of light and consciousness within the "dark" or "harsh" qualities of nature.</note> rose up out of the Light, which became shining in the sweet water—which flash is the bitter quality that is born out of the ignited <term>shock</term> <note>original: "Schracke." This refers to a sudden, startling tension or "crack" within the elemental forces that initiates change.</note> of the fire in the water.
6. Thus all of Nature in this world was then <term>bubbling</term> <note>original: "quallend." This implies a state of active, surging, and teeming vitality.</note> and moving, in the earth as well as above the earth, and life began to be born again in all things.
7. From the earth rose up grass, herbs, and trees; and in the earth rose up silver, gold, and all kinds of ore; and in the deep above the earth rose up the wonderful formation of powers.
8. However, so that you might understand how there is one substance and occasion for all these things and births, I will [describe] everything one after another, each in its order—

...to write, so that you might rightly understand the foundation of these mysteries: and I will 1. begin with the Earth; thereafter 2. concerning the Deep above the Earth; and 3. concerning the joint corporization <note>original: *Corporirung*; Böhme uses this to describe how spiritual forces "body forth" or solidify into physical matter</note> of the bodies of the stars; 4. concerning the seven primary qualities of the planets, and of their Heart, which is the Sun; 5. concerning the four elements; 6. concerning the outward, comprehensible birth, which arises from this entire dominion <note>original: *Regiment*; the governing laws or system by which nature is managed</note>; and 7. concerning the wondrous proportion and skill of the entire Wheel of Nature.
9. Before this mirror I have now invited all lovers of the holy and highly-praised arts of philosophy, astrology, and theology <note>originals: *Philosophia, Astrologia, and Theologia*</note>; there I will reveal the root and the foundation to them.
10. And though I have not studied or learned their art, and do not know how to work with their circle-measuring <note>likely referring to the mathematical tools and geometry used by academic astronomers</note>, that causes me no concern; they shall nevertheless have so much to learn that many a man will not fathom or grasp it in his lifetime.
11. For I do not use their formula <note>original: *Formula*; the systematic methods or technical jargon of the universities</note> and manner, since I have not learned it from them, but I have another teacher, which is all of **N a t u r e**. From this same whole Nature, with its inherent birth, I have studied and learned my philosophy, astrology, and theology <note>originals: *Philosophiam, Astrologiam, and Theologiam*</note>, and not from men or through men.
12. But because men are gods, and have the knowledge of God the only Father, from whom they have come and in whom they live, I do not at all despise their formulas <note>original: *Formulam*</note> of philosophy, astrology, and theology. For I find that for the most part they stand upon the right foundation, and I will also strive to follow after their formula.
13. For I must indeed say that their formula is my master, and from their formula I have my beginning and first knowledge. I am also not of the mind to overturn or improve their formula, for I cannot do so, nor have I ever learned it, but I leave them sitting in their seat.
14. However, I also do not wish to build upon their foundation, but as a hardworking servant I will scrape the earth away from the root, so that the entire tree may be seen with the root, trunk, limbs, branches, and fruits; and thus my writing is nothing new, but rather their philosophy and mine...

18. Therefore, the Spirit of Nature says: because they will not wake up from sleep and open the door, I will do it myself.
19. 20. Then I would lie there and be trodden underfoot, whereas before I had been displayed upon the beautiful door; for what else is the bolt for, but for firewood?
21. Behold, I tell you a mystery: as soon as the door opens to its very hinge, all useless, firmly-wedged bolts will be cast away, for the door will henceforth...

24. **C**oncerning this, Moses writes: (Genesis chapter 1) And God said, Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and years: and let them be for lights in the firmament of the heaven to give light upon the earth.

And the evening and the morning were the fourth day. (Genesis 1:14, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19.)
26. And it is well to be presumed that the creation before the Flood <note>original: *Sündfluth*</note> was not described in writing, but as a dark word in memory, brought from one generation to another, until after the Flood, when the world began to live in an Epicurean <term>Epicurean: Böhme uses this to describe a materialistic lifestyle focused on worldly pleasure and physical senses, ignoring spiritual realities</term> manner again.

[...they] have Creation, and see therein that there is a God, and that this essence of the world has not stood thus from eternity; so that they might have a mirror in it, and fear that same hidden God.
28. This was also the chief instruction and teaching of the patriarchs <note>original: *Altväter*; refers to the biblical ancestors such as Noah or Abraham</note>, both after the Flood and also before it: that they directed people toward Creation, just as the entire Book of Job also urges.
29. After those patriarchs came the "wise heroes" <note>Böhme likely refers to the great philosophers of antiquity, such as the Greeks</note>; they reached somewhat deeper into the knowledge of nature, and I must say with the foundation of truth that in their philosophy and knowledge they came before God’s face, and yet they could neither see nor recognize Him.
30. For man is so thoroughly dead in death, and locked into the outermost birth in dead tangibility <note>original: *Begreiflichkeit*; refers to the physical, material world that can be grasped by the senses</note>, otherwise they would surely have thought that within this tangibility there must be a divine power hidden in the center <note>original: *Centro*</note>, which had thus created, maintained, supported, and governed this tangibility.
31. They did indeed honor and worship the sun and stars as gods, but they did not recognize how they were created or became, or out of what they were made.
32. For they might well have thought that they must have come from something, and that the thing which created them must be greater and older than the stars.
33. Furthermore, they had the earth and stones as examples, showing that they must have come from something, as well as humans and all creatures <note>original: *Creaturen*</note> on earth. All of this convicts them, showing that in these things a more mighty power is present, which created all of this in such a way.
34. Indeed, why should I write much of the heathens' blindness? Even our doctors <note>original: *Doctores*; here Böhme crititiques the university-trained theologians of his day</note> in their "crowned little hats" <note>a mocking reference to academic or clerical headwear, symbolizing pride in worldly learning</note> are just as blind: they know indeed that there is a God who created all this, but they do not know where that God is, or what He is like.
35. When they want to write of God, they seek Him outside of this world, in a heaven alone, as if He were an image to be compared to something. They admit, to be sure, that this God governs everything in this world by a Spirit, but His bodily presence <note>original: *corporlich Eigenthum*; refers to God's actual essence or being</note> they want to have situated strictly many thousand miles away in a heaven.
36. Well—

36. Come now, you **Doctors** <note>original: "Doctores," referring to university-trained theologians and scholars</note>, if you are in the right, then give the Spirit an answer; I wish to question you a little.

37. What do you suppose stood in the place of this world before the time of the world? Or from what do you suppose the earth and stars came to be? Or what do you suppose is in the deep above the earth, or from what did the deep come to be? Or how do you suppose that man is **God's image**, in which God dwells? Or what do you think the **wrath of God** is? Or what displeasure does God have with man that He should torment him, seeing as He created him? Why should He count sin against him and condemn him to eternal torment!

38. Why then did He create that which man offends against? Surely that must be even more evil? Why or from what did that come to be? Or what is the cause, or the beginning, or the birth of the **fierce wrath of God**, from which **Hell** and **Devil** have come to be? Or how does it happen that all **creatures** <note>original: "Creaturen"</note> in this world bite, thrust, and strike one another, and yet sin is reckoned to man alone?

39. Or from what did the poisonous and evil beasts and worms come to be, with all the vermin? Or from what were the **holy angels** made? And finally, what is the **soul** of man, and the great God Himself?

40. Give a correct and thorough answer to this, and prove it, and leave off your bickering over words. If you can prove from your previous writings that you know the true, only God—how He is in love and wrath, and what He is—and if you can prove that God is *not* in the stars, elements, earth, stones, humans, beasts, worms, in leaf, herb, and grass, in Heaven and earth, and that all this is not God Himself <note>Böhme is arguing for a panentheistic view where God's power sustains all things, rather than God being distant from creation</note>, and that my spirit is false, then I will be the first to burn my book in the fire, and I will recant and curse everything I have written, and I will allow myself to be obediently instructed.

41. However, I do not mean to say that I cannot err at all, for there are some things not sufficiently explained; they were described as if from a glimpse of the great God, where the **Wheel of Nature** <note>a central concept in Böhme’s thought, representing the dynamic, rotating forces of divine manifestation</note> turns too quickly, and man, with his half-dead and tough <note>original: "zehen," likely meaning "zäh" (tough or heavy), or possibly "tenfold" in a mystical sense</note> comprehension, cannot sufficiently grasp it.

61. For God requires no other service than that His creature, who exists within His body, should not move away from Him, but rather be holy as He is.

62. For this reason, God also gave the Jews the Law, so that they should apply themselves to gentle holiness and love, so that the whole world would have a mirror in them. But when they fell into pride and boasted of their [biological] birth over love, and turned the Law of love into a sharpness of wrath, then God pushed their lampstand <note>A biblical reference to God removing His grace or presence, as in Revelation 2:5.</note> away and moved to the heathens.

63. Secondly, this is the difference between Christians, Jews, Turks, and heathens: that the Christians know the Tree of Life, which is Christ. He is the Prince of our Heaven and of this world, and He reigns in all births <note>The various stages of manifestation or spiritual generations.</note> as a King in God His Father, and humanity are His members.

64. Now Christians know how they can—by the power of this Tree—penetrate from their death through His death to Him and into His life, and rule and live with Him. Thus, by their "penetrating through" and by their new birth out of this dead body, they are able to be with Him in Heaven.

65. And even though the dead [physical] body is in the midst of Hell among all the devils, the new man nevertheless reigns with God in Heaven; for them, the Tree of Life is a strong gate through which they enter into life.

98. When it is smelted for the sixth time, it becomes somewhat harder. 99. In this sixth smelting, I believe, lies the greatest danger for alchemists in their making of silver and gold. For a truly subtle fire is required here; the work can easily become burnt and "deaf" <note>Alchemical jargon for material that has lost its potency or failed to transform.</note>, or even too soft from a fire that is too cold. It must be a <term>median fire</term><note>A moderate, balanced heat.</note>, so that the spirit in the heart does not rise up in rebellion but seethes gently. Then it gains a fine, sweet, and soft ring, and rejoices continually, as if it were about to ignite once more in the light of GOD.

100. But if the fire in the fifth and sixth smeltings is too hot, the new life—which was born in love from the water through the power of the rising light—is once again infected by the grimness of the wrathful fire. The ore then becomes a burnt dross and <term>refuse</term><note>Original: "Aberaum," referring to debris or waste material.</note>, and the alchemist has filth instead of gold.

### The 23rd Chapter.
### Of the Depth above the Earth.

1. **W**hen man gazes at the depth above the Earth, he sees nothing but stars and watery clouds; then he thinks that there must be another place where the Godhead reveals itself with the heavenly and angelic dominion <term>dominion: original *Regiment*; refers to the governing forces, laws, or active powers of a realm</term>. He is inclined to distinguish the depth, along with its dominion, from the Godhead, for he sees nothing there but stars, and the dominion between them is fire, air, and water.
2. Then he thinks: God made that by His purpose out of Nothing; how could God be in that essence, or how could that be God Himself? He always imagines to himself that it is merely a house, in which God rules and dwells with His Spirit: that God could surely not be a God whose essence consists in the power of this dominion.
3. Many a man might well say: what kind of God would that be, whose body, essence, and power consisted of fire, air, water, and earth?
4. See, you uncomprehending <note>original: *unbegreiflicher*; here meaning one who is unable to grasp the truth or lacks spiritual insight</note> man, I will show you the right ground of the Godhead. If this whole essence is not God, then you are not God’s image; if there is some foreign God elsewhere, then you have no part in Him. For you are created out of this God, and you live in this same God, and this same God constantly gives you power, blessing, food, and drink from Himself; likewise, all your knowledge stands in this God, and when you die, you are buried in this God.
5. If there is now a foreign God who is outside of this one, who then will make you living again out of this God in whom you have decayed? How will the foreign God—out of whom you were not created and in whom you never lived—figure your body and spirit back together again?
6. If you are then a different matter than God Himself, how will you then be His child? Or how could the man and King Christ be God's bodily Son, whom He has born out of His heart?

### Concerning the Siderial Birth, and the Birth of GOD.

15. **B**efore the time of the created heavens, the stars, and the elements, and before the creation of the angels, there was no such wrath of God, nor any death, nor any devil, nor even earth or stones. Likewise, there were no stars; instead, the Deity was born in a gentle and lovely manner, and shaped into images <note>original: "Bildnisse"; refers to the archetypal forms or ideas within the divine mind.</note>, which were embodied through the <term>source-spirits (Quellgeister): Böhme’s term for the seven fundamental forces or qualities that "spring" or "well up" to create all reality.</term> with their birthing, wrestling, and rising. 16. But take careful note here: the earnest and severe birth, from which the wrath of God, hell, and death originated, has indeed been in God from eternity, but it was not ignited or raised up. For the whole of God exists in 7 species, or a sevenfold form or birthing; and if these births did not exist, there would be no God, no life, no angel, and no creature at all.
17. And these same births have no beginning, but have born themselves thus from eternity. Within this <term>depth (Tiefe): The unfathomable abyss of God's being.</term>, God Himself does not know what He is. For He knows no beginning, and nothing like Himself, and also no end.
18. Of these seven births in total, none is the first, nor the second, third, or last; rather, all seven are each the first, second, third, fourth, and last. Yet, according to the manner and way of a creature <note>Böhme means that because humans are finite "creatures," we can only understand things one step at a time, even though they happen simultaneously in God.</note>, I must set them down one after the other, otherwise you would not understand it. ...understand his will in this very well.
