Just watch out: if you blind yourself, there is no more counsel, and you must not say you did not know it. Arise, the day is dawning!

69. The third distinction, or the 3rd Person in the Essence of God, is the surging Spirit <note>original: "wallende Geist"; this suggests a boiling, bubbling, or actively moving flow like a spring</note>, which arises from the rising up in the terror-flash <note>original: "Schracke"; Böhme's term for the sudden ignition of life and light out of the dark tensions of nature</note> where life is born. It now surges in all powers and is the Spirit of Life; the powers cannot seize or grasp it again, but rather it ignites the powers and, through its surging, makes figures and images, and forms them according to the manner in which the wrestling birth <note>the process of divine generation</note> stands in every place.

70. And if you do not wish to be blind, you should know that the air is that same Spirit; however, in the space <note>original: "Loco"; Latin for place or location</note> of this world, nature within it is quite substantially ignited in the wrath-fire, which Lord Lucifer has done; and the Holy Spirit, which is the Spirit of Gentleness <note>original: "Sanftmuth"</note>, lies hidden therein within its heaven.

71. You need not ask: "Where is this heaven?" It is in your heart; only unlock it—here the key is shown to you.

72. Thus there is one God, and 3 distinct Persons in one another, and none can grasp or restrain the other, or fathom the origin of the others; but the Father begets the Son, and the Son is the Father’s heart, and his love and his light, and is an origin of joys and the beginning of all life.

73. And the Holy Spirit is the Spirit of Life, and a former and creator of all things, and a performer of the will in God; it has formed and created out of the body and in the body of the Father all angels and creatures, and still daily sustains and forms everything, and is the sharpness <note>the keen, penetrating quality</note> and the living Spirit of God. As the Father speaks the Word out of his powers, so the Spirit forms it.

## -> Of the Great Simplicity of God. <-

74. **W**ell then, Master Jack <note>original: "Junker Hanß"; a satirical name Böhme uses to mock proud, worldly scholars or mockers who think they are noble but lack spiritual insight</note> on the brown horse, you who ride from heaven into hell, and from hell even into death, wherein the sting of the devil lies, behold
-> Yourself <-

### 310 -> Aurora: The Day-Spring. <- Chapter 23.

you here, you world-wise man, you who are filled with wicked cleverness.

75. Take note, you world-wise lawyers <note>original: "Juristen"</note>, if you will not seek this mirror, this bright and clear face of God, and behold yourselves therein, then the Spirit offers you birth in the innermost bitter circle <note>the "bitter quality" is one of Böhme's seven source-spirits of nature, associated here with the root of harshness</note> where cleverness is born, where the sharpness of God’s anxious birth dwells; for it is there that your cleverness and deep understanding are born.

76. If you wish to be gods and not devils, then make use of the holy and gentle Law of God; if not, you shall forever and eternally give birth within the strict and earnest birth of God. The Spirit speaks this as a word of God, and not my dead flesh.

77. You should know that I do not suck this knowledge out of dead reason; rather, my spirit inter-works <term>inqualiret: a word Böhme coined from Latin to describe how the spirit acts in harmony and co-operates with the "qualities" of God</term> with God, and approves of the Godhead as it is, with all its birth, taste, and smell. I find, therefore, that the Godhead is an entirely simple, gentle, lovely, and quiet Being; that the birth of the Trinity of God generates itself quite gently, amiably, tangibly, and in unity; and the sharpness of the innermost birth can never raise itself into the gentleness of the Trinity, but remains hidden in the depths.

78. And this sharpness in the hiddenness is called God’s Wrath; and the essence of gentleness in the Trinity is called God. In that gentleness, nothing issues from the sharpness that might destroy or kindle the wrath; rather, the spirits play gently within one another like small children when they rejoice together, where each has his task, playing with and caressing one another.

79. The holy angels also engage in such work, and within the Trinity of God there is an entirely gentle, lovely, and sweet Being, where the Spirit always rises in the tone <note>original: "Thone," referring here to divine sound or harmony</note>, and one power moves the other as if lovely songs or the playing of stringed instruments were rising there.

80. And as the rising of the spirits is in every place, so also the tone forms itself—but quite gently, incomprehensible to the bodies of the angels, yet quite comprehensible to the animal birth <note>original: "animalischen Geburt," referring to the "soul-life" or vital spirit (from Latin *anima*) rather than a beast-like nature</note> of the angels. And as the Godhead reveals itself in every place, so too do the angels reveal themselves. For the angels are created out of this essence, and they have their princes of the source-spirits of God among them, just as they exist within the birth of God.

### Chapter 23. -> Aurora: The Day-Spring. <- 311

81. Therefore, just as the Being of God reveals itself in its birth <note>original: "Geburt"; Böhme uses this term to describe the eternal process by which God’s qualities manifest and interact</note>, so too do the angels. Whichever power in the birth of God becomes the *Primus* <note>Latin: "the first" or "chief"</note> at any given time, it rejoices from the Heart of God in the Holy Spirit; the Prince of Power of that angel also begins his song of praise before all others, and rejoices with his host. Now it is one, then the other, for the birth of God is like a wheel.

82. But when the Heart of God reveals itself with its special clarity, then the entire host of all three kingdoms of the holy angels rises up. And in this rising of the Heart of God, the man Jesus Christ is King and *Primus*; He leads the royal dance <note>original: "Reigen"; a traditional circle dance, here symbolizing the harmonious movement of souls in heaven</note> with all the holy souls of men until the Last Day. Then holy people will become perfect angels, and the godless will become perfect devils, and that for all eternity. Here, look at yourself in the mirror, you clever world, and see where your cleverness comes from.

#### -> Now you will say: <-

83. **Y**ou seek a much deeper cleverness than we do; you wish to climb into the hiddenness of God, which is not fitting for any man. We seek only human cleverness, but you wish to be like God and know everything, just as God is—and that in all things, both in heaven and hell, in devils, angels, and men. Therefore, it is surely not wrong for us to seek subtle, sharp schemes, for it brings honor, power, and wealth.

## -> The Reply. <-

84. **I**f you follow me up this ladder upon which I climb into the depths of God, you will have climbed well. I did not come to this understanding, or into this work and knowledge, through my own reason or my own intentional will. I did not seek this science <note>original: "Wissenschaft"; here meaning spiritual knowledge or a structured understanding of divine mysteries</note>, nor did I know anything about it; I sought only the Heart of God, to hide myself therein from the storm-winds of the devil.

85. But when I reached that place, this great and difficult labor was laid upon me: to reveal and announce to the world the great Day of the Lord. And because the world so hungrily lusts after the root of the tree, I must reveal to them what the whole tree is, thereby announcing that it is the Day-Spring <note>original: "Morgenröte"; the dawn or first light of the morning</note> of the day which God has long ago decreed in His counsel. Amen.
-> 86. Thus <-

### 312 -> Dawn of the Ascent. <- Ch. 23.

86. So you see now what God is, and how his love and wrath have been from eternity, and also how his "birth" <note>The "birth" of God refers to the eternal process by which God's nature manifests and generates itself.</note> occurs. You must not say that you do not live and exist in God, or that God is something foreign to which you cannot come; rather, wherever you are, there is the <term>Gate of God<note>original: "Porten Gottes"; Böhme emphasizes that the divine is omnipresent and accessible through one's own inner state rather than a physical location.</note></term>. If you are holy, then according to your soul you are with God in heaven; but if you are godless, then according to your soul you are in the fire of hell.

#### -> Now observe further. <-

87. **W**hen God created all the angels, they were created out of this "birthing" of God; their bodies were formed together out of nature, and within them their spirit and light were born, just as the Godhead was born. And just as the <term>source-spirits<note>original: "Quellgeister"; Böhme’s term for the fundamental forces or qualities of divine nature that flow like springs (Quellen) to animate all existence.</note></term> of God always took their power and strength from the "body" of nature, so also the angels; they always took their power and strength from the nature of God.

88. And just as the Holy Spirit formed and shaped everything in nature, so also did the angelic spirit <term>in-qualify<note>original: "inqualiren"; a technical term meaning to harmoniously interact or co-operate with the essential qualities of another being or of God.</note></term> within the Holy Spirit, and helped to form and shape everything, so that everything would be one heart and will, and pure delight and joy.

89. For the angels are children of the great God, whom he has born in his body of nature for the increase of divine joy.

90. Here you should know, however, that the bodies of the angels cannot grasp the "birth" of God; their body does not understand it either. Only their spirit understands it. The body, however, stays still, just like nature in God, and lets the spirit work and <term>play in love<note>original: "liebespielen"; describes the effortless, joyous communion between the spirit and the divine, likened to the spontaneous play of children.</note></term> with God. For the angels play before God and in God, just like little children before their parents; by this, the divine joy is increased.

91. But when the great and mighty prince and king Lucifer was created, he would not do this, but rose up and wanted to be God alone, and ignited the <term>fire of wrath<note>original: "Zornfeuer"; the "dark" or harsh aspect of God's power which becomes destructive when separated from light and love.</note></term> within himself; and so did all his angels.

92. But when this happened, he roared with his ignited fire-spirit into the nature of God; then the whole body in the nature of God, as far as his dominion reached, was ignited. But because his light was immediately extinguished, he could no longer "in-qualify" with his spirit in the two births of the Son of God and the Holy Spirit of God, but remained stuck in the harsh birth of God.

### Ch. 23. -> Dawn of the Ascent. <- 313

93. For the Light of God and the Spirit of God cannot be grasped by the **harsh birthing** <note>The "harsh birthing" (scharfe Gebärung) refers to the qualities of tension, contraction, and friction in nature that exist without the softening influence of divine Love.</note>; therefore, they are also two distinct entities. For this reason, Lord Lucifer, with his stern, cold, and hard fire-birth, could no longer touch or see the Heart and Holy Spirit of God, nor taste or feel them; instead, he was spat out with his fire-spirit into the outermost nature, in which he had ignited the <term>wrath-fire<note>original: "Zornfeuer"; the destructive, consuming aspect of the divine fire when separated from light and love.</note></term>.

94. This same nature is indeed the Body of God, in which the Godhead is born; however, the devils cannot grasp the gentle birth of God which rises up in the Light. For their body has died away in the Light and lives in the outermost and stern birth of God, where the Light shall never again be ignited.

95. For their **fat** <note>original: "Fettes"; in Böhme’s alchemical language, this refers to the combustible "oil" or essence of the soul that serves as the fuel for either the light of love or the fire of wrath.</note> within the sweet water is burnt up, and from that same water a sour stench has formed, in which the Light of God can no longer ignite itself, and the Light of God can no longer walk therein.

96. Thus the <term>source-spirits<note>original: "Quellgeister"; the fundamental active forces of Böhme's cosmos.</note></term> within the devils are locked in hard wrath; their bodies are a hard death, and their spirits are a fierce sting of the wrath of God, and their source-spirits are always born in the innermost sharpness according to the right of the harsh Godhead.

97. For they cannot be born otherwise, nor can they die or pass away; rather, they stand in the most anxious birthing, and there is nothing but vain fierceness, wrath, and malice within them. The ignited fire-source rises up from eternity to eternity, and they can eternally no longer touch, see, nor comprehend the sweet and light birth of God.

## -> Concerning the Ignited Nature. <-

# ->Chapter 24.<-
## ->On the Incorporation and Formation of the Stars.<-

### 1.
**W**hen the whole body of Nature within the vastness of this world was frozen, as if in a hard death, and yet life was hidden within it, **God** moved the whole body of Nature of this world on the fourth day, and from Nature, out of the light that had risen, He brought forth the stars. For the wheel of **God’s** birth moved again, just as it had done from eternity.

2. It did indeed move on the first day, and the birth began in the body of corrupted Nature; for on the first day, life distinguished itself from death, and on the second day, a <term>firmament</term> <note>The "Feste" or firmament acts as a boundary or "partition" between the spiritual world and the material world.</note> was created in between, and on the third day, life broke through death. For then the light broke through the darkness and made the dead body of Nature greening and mobile.

3. For on the third day, the body of Nature was in such great <term>anguish</term> <note>original: "geängstet." In Böhme's thought, "Angst" refers to the literal "narrowing" or compression of forces that creates the tension necessary for life to erupt.</note> until the fire of love was kindled within death. Then the light of life broke through the frozen body of death and grew green out of death; yet on the third day, it stood only in the <term>terror of fire</term> <note>original: "Feuerschrecke." This refers to the sudden, transformative flash or "crack" when the dark, harsh qualities of nature are ignited into light.</note>, from which mobility arose.

4. But on the fourth day, the light rose and made its seat in the house of death, which death, however, cannot comprehend. Just as the <term>stern birth</term> <note>original: "strenge Geburt." The foundational, harsh qualities of God's power—bitterness, heat, and hardness—that form the "core" of existence.</note> of **God**, which stands in the innermost core and from which life arises, cannot seize or contain gentleness, nor the light of gentleness along with the Spirit in gentleness—so also the dead darkness of this world cannot seize the light of Nature, nor can any devil.

5. Rather, the light shines through death and has made for itself its royal seat in the midst of the house of death and the wrath of **God**; and it brings forth for Him a new body of **God** out of the house of wrath, which exists eternally in the love of **God**, incomprehensible to the old, kindled state in the <term>outermost birth</term> <note>The physical, material world we perceive with our senses.</note>.

->Now<-

He emphasizes that the light of life exists within the "house of death" (the material world) but remains separate and incomprehensible to darkness and evil.</summary>

->**Now you ask:**<-
### ->**How shall I understand this?**<-

6. **I** cannot write this into your heart, for it is not within everyone's understanding and grasp—especially where the spirit stands in the house of wrath and does not <term>work in union</term> <note>original: "inqualiret." A Böhmean term meaning to operate together with the same qualities or essence.</note> with the light of **God**. But I will show you in earthly parables, so that you might come a little into deep thought.

7. Look at a tree: it has on its outside a hard, coarse bark, which is dead and numb; yet it is not entirely in death, but rather in a state of <term>faintness</term> <note>original: "Ohnmacht." Implies a lack of active power or consciousness.</note>, and there is a difference between it and the body that grows beneath the bark. The body, however, has its living power and breaks through the withered bark, and brings forth many beautiful young bodies, which all nonetheless stand in the old body.

8. But the bark is like a dead thing and cannot grasp the life of the tree; rather, it only hangs upon it and is a covering for the tree, in which the worms nest and thereby eventually destroy the tree as well.

9. So too is the whole house of this world: the outer darkness is the house of **God's** wrath, where the devils dwell, and it is truly the house of death, for the holy light of **God** has died out within it. <insert>Understand: it has entered into its own <term>principle</term> <note>original: "Principium." Böhme uses this to describe distinct realms of existence—here, the dark realm of wrath.</note>, and this outermost essence is to be regarded as almost dead toward **God**, even though it lives in **God**, but in a different source.</insert>

10. But the body of this great house, which lies hidden beneath the bark of darkness—incomprehensible to the darkness—that is the house of life, where love and wrath wrestle with one another.

11. Now love always breaks through the house of death and brings forth holy, heavenly branches in the great tree, which stand in the light. For they turn green through the bark of darkness, just as the branch does through the bark of the tree, and they are one life with **God**.

12. And wrath also grows green in the house of darkness, and through its infection, it keeps many a noble branch captive in death within the house of <term>fierceness</term> <note>original: "Grimmigkeit." A key term for Böhme describing the harsh, stinging, and wrathful quality of the material world's foundation.</note>.

13. This then is the <term>sum</term> <note>original: "Summa." The summary or core essence.</note> or the substance of the <term>sidereal birth</term> <note>original: "siderischen Geburt." The birth of the stars and the astral influences that govern the material world.</note> about which I wish to write here.

->**Now the question is:**<-
### ->**What are the stars? or from what did they become?**<-

14. **T**hey are the power of the seven <term>Source-Spirits<note>Original: Quellgeister. In Böhme's system, these are the seven fundamental "fountain spirits" or active qualities that flow from God to create and sustain all reality.</note></term> of **God**. For when the wrath of **God** was ignited by the devils in this world, the entire house of this world—in its nature or its outermost birth—became frozen as if in death; from this come the earth and the stones. When that same hard <term>residue<note>Original: Abraum. Usually refers to mining waste or overburden; here Böhme uses it to describe the material "dregs" that solidified when the divine light withdrew.</note></term> was driven together into a lump, the deep became clearer, but entirely dark, for the light within it had died away in the wrath.

15. But now, the body of **God** <note>Böhme often refers to the physical universe as the "body" of God in its manifested form.</note> in this world could not remain in death; instead, **God** moved Himself toward birth with His seven Source-Spirits.

->**But you must understand this high matter correctly.**<-

16. **T**he Light of **God**, which is the Son of **God**, as well as the Holy Spirit, had not died. Instead, the Light—which from eternity has gone forth from the heart of **God** and has illuminated the nature born from the seven spirits—withdrew from that harshly corrupted nature. Because of this, the nature of this world, with its <term>tangibility<note>Original: Begreiflichkeit. Refers to the material, "graspable" quality of the physical world compared to the spiritual.</note></term>, remained in death and cannot grasp the Light of **God**, but is instead a dark house for the devil.

17. After this, on the fourth day of creation, **God** reborn the entire house of this world with its qualities, and placed the Source-Spirits into the house of darkness, so that He might bear from it a new body again for His praise and honor.

18. For His intention was to create another angelic host out of this house, which was to be done in this way: He wished to create an angel, who was Adam; he was to bear from himself creatures of his own kind who would possess the house of the new birth. And in the middle of time, their King was to be born from the body of a human being and possess the newborn kingdom as a King of these creatures, in the place of the corrupted and cast-out Lucifer.

19. During the fulfillment of this time, **God** wished to adorn this house with its qualities as a royal government, and to grant the entire house to those same Source-Spirits,

...so that in the house of darkness and death they might once again bring forth creatures and images, as they had done from eternity, until the entire host of newly created angels—which were human beings—should be completed. At that point, **God** intended to lock the Devil into the house of darkness in a narrow cave and ignite the whole house again in His light, except for the cave of the Devil.

->**Now the question arises:**<-
### ->**Why did God not lock him up immediately, so that he would not have caused so much misery?**<-

20. **B**ehold, this was **God’s** purpose, and it had to stand: that He intended to build Himself an <term>angelic host<note>Original: "englisch Heer." In this context, Böhme uses the word "englisch" to mean "angel-like" or "pertaining to angels," rather than the English nationality.</note></term> once again out of the corrupted nature of the earth; understand this as a new body that would exist in **God** eternally.

21. It was by no means **God’s** intention to give the entire earth to the Devil as an eternal dwelling; rather, He gave him only the death and the <term>wrath<note>Original: "Grimmigkeit." A key term for Böhme referring to the harsh, bitter, and fierce quality of nature when it is separated from God's light.</note></term> of the earth, which the Devil himself had brought into it.

22. For how had the <term>Salitter<note>Original: "Salitter." A term Böhme adapted from "saltpeter." To him, it represents the divine "sap" or the fundamental chemical-spiritual substance from which all things are built.</note></term> of the earth sinned before **God**, that it should stand entirely and utterly in eternal shame? It had done nothing; it was merely a body that had to remain still while the Devil rose up within it.

23. If He had granted the Devil an eternal dwelling place immediately, then no new body could have been built out of that same <note>original: "Loco" (Latin: place/location)</note> space. How had that same space sinned in **God**, that it should remain in eternal shame? Not at all; it would have been an injustice.

24. But now, **God's** undertaking was that He wanted to make a beautiful angelic host out of the earth, along with all kinds of formations. For within it and upon it, everything was meant to turn green and be <term>reborn<note>Original: "neugebären." Literally "newly born." Böhme sees the natural world as a cycle of constant spiritual rebirth striving to return to its divine origin.</note></term>, as one can see in ore, stones, trees, herbs, and grass, and all kinds of animals according to the heavenly likeness.

25. And even though these same formations were perishable—because they were not pure before **God**—nevertheless, at the end of this time, **God** intended to pull the heart and the kernel out of this new rebirth and separate it from death and wrath. This new rebirth was then meant to flourish eternally in **God** outside of this space and bear heavenly fruit once again.

->D 3 | 26. The<-

27. 28. But the reason there are so many stars with such diverse effects is the infinity which <note>original: "inficiret," meaning to permeate or influence through contact</note> permeates itself within the seven spirits of **GOD** and gives birth infinitely.

29. That the birth, or the body of the stars, does not change in its position—as they have done from eternity—signifies that it is to be a constant birth. Through this, the frozen body of the earth would be continually ignited again in the same operation (which nevertheless stands in infinity) and be born anew. This applies also to the house of deep darkness above the earth, so that the new body might always be born out of death until the time and the entire newborn body were completed.

> How then do the stars exist in love and wrath?

41. For until the third day from the time of the kindling of God's wrath in this world, nature was a dark valley in its anguish and stood in death; but on the third day, life broke through death, and the new birth began.
42. This was done so that this time might become one with eternal time again, and that no day of death might remain between them. It ensures that the eternal love, and the newborn love from the new body of nature, might be one eternal love, and that there be no distinction between the eternal love and the newborn love, but that the newborn love should reach into the very essence that has been from eternity, and also for itself into eternity.
43. Thus, the newborn love—which has arisen in the stars and in the whole body of this world out of the water of life in the light—is so completely united with the eternal, unbeginning love, that it is one heart and one spirit, which carries and sustains everything.
44. In this kindling of the light in the stars and elements, the birth of nature did not, however, transform itself entirely into holy gentleness, as it was before the time of the wrath, so that the birth of nature would now be entirely holy and pure. No; rather, it stands in its sharpest, strictest, and most anxious birth, where the wrath of God flourishes <note>original: "grünet"; literally "greens," but used by Böhme to mean "grows vigorously."</note> without ceasing like hellish fire.

**10.** And I have chosen for myself the gates of the knowledge of light, and will pursue the Spirit’s impulse and knowledge. For then he would take what is mine with interest and take it away from me entirely, giving it to another who had traded much with his talent. Thus I will sow; He may water it, and I will let Him rule.

# ->The Rising Aurora.<- Chapter 25.

Even though it seems as if the other stars also shine brightly, it is actually nothing of the sort; instead, they all receive their brilliance from the sun, as shall follow shortly hereafter.

## ->The true birth and origin of the sun and<-
## ->planets is constituted as follows:<-

68. **W**hen Heaven was made to create a distinction between the Light of God and the ignited corruption of the body of this world, the body of this world was a dark valley. It possessed no light that could have shone in the external realm outside of Heaven; there, all powers stood imprisoned as if in death, and they were in such great agony until they heated themselves in the center of the body.
69. But when it happened that this anxious birth stood so severely in the heat, the Love in the Light of God broke through the <term>Heaven of distinction<note>The 'firmament' or boundary Böhme believes separates the divine realm from the material world.</note></term> and ignited the heat. Then, within the heat, in the water or in the <term>fatness of the water<note>original: "Fetten des Waſſers"—refers to the oily, combustible essence or "unctuosity" that Böhme believes allows light to take hold in matter.</note></term>, the shining light arose and the heart of the water was ignited; and this happened in a single moment.
70. For as soon as the light truly took hold of the <term>corpus<note>original: "Corpus"—Latin for "body," referring here to the material substance of the sun.</note></term>, the body was captured in the light, and the heat was captured and transformed into a considerable gentleness, and it could no longer remain in such anguish.
71. Because the heat was "startled" by the light, its cruel fire-source subsided and could no longer ignite itself further. Also, the breakthrough of Love in the Light of God through the Heaven did not extend any further at that time, according to God's purpose; for that reason, the sun did not become any larger.

## ->Concerning the Planet Mars.<-

72. **B**ut when the sun ignited, the cruel <term>fire-terror<note>original: "Feuerſchrack"—a sudden, violent eruption or shock of fire energy.</note></term> rushed upward out of the location of the sun, like a cruel, tempestuous lightning bolt. In its bodily essence, it took along the <term>fierceness<note>original: "Grimmigkeit"—the wrathful or harsh quality of nature.</note></term> of the fire, from which the water became entirely bitter; and this water is the kernel or the core of the terror.
73. Now the <term>astrologers<note>original: "Aſtrologi"</note></term> write that the planet Mars stands high above the sun at a distance of 15,750 miles, which I will let stand, as I do not work with the compass. The swift fire-terror traveled that far from its own location until the light also took hold of it; there, it was also captured by the light, and it stood still and occupied that location.

## ->About the Planet Jupiter.<-

76. **W**hen the bitter <term>fire-fright<note>original: "Feuerſchrack"—the sudden, terrifying burst of energy or "scare" that characterizes the planet Mars in Böhme's system.</note></term> was captured by the light, the light pressed even higher into the deep by its own power, until it reached into the hard and cold seat of nature. There, the power of the first rising from the Sun could go no higher, and it remained sitting there bodily, and took that same location for its dwelling.
->But you must understand this thing correctly.<-
77. **I**t was the power of the light that remained standing in this place; it is a completely gentle, friendly, gracious, and sweet essence. Concerning this planet, the <term>astrologers<note>original: "Aſtro-logi"—Böhme frequently references contemporary astrological calculations to ground his spiritual visions.</note></term> write that he stands 7,875 miles high above Mars; but he is the <term>soother<note>original: "Sänftiger"—one who calms or moderates something.</note></term> of the destroyer and raging Mars, and an origin of gentleness in all life, as well as an origin of the water from which life is born, as I will report hereafter.
78. Thus far the power of life from the Sun has reached, and no higher; however, the luster or shine—which also has its own power—reaches unto the stars and through the entire body of this world.
->But you must properly understand how<-
->these two planets came to be.<-
79. **W**hen the power of the Heart of God pressed out of the eternal, <term>un-extinguished<note>original: "unerſtorbenen"—literally "un-died," referring to a source that is perpetually living and never stagnant.</note></term> well-spring of the Water of Life through the <term>Heaven of Distinction<note>The 'firmament' or boundary Böhme believes separates the divine realm from the material world.</note></term>, and ignited the water in the location of the Sun, then the lightning—understand, the <term>fire-flash<note>original: "Feuer-Bliz"</note></term>—shot out of the water; it was altogether terrifying and bitter, and from that, Mars was formed.
80. Immediately after that same flash, the power of light followed swiftly, like a gentle, elevating life, and it overtook the fire-fright and soothed it, so that he became somewhat faint and could no longer break through the deep or go further, but remained standing there, trembling.

81. 82. From that same power, the planet Jupiter came to be—and not from the same place where he now stands; rather, he always ignites that same place with his power. He is like a houseguest in that place, who must always wander about in his <term>rented house<note>original: "Lehnhaus"; Böhme uses the legal metaphor of a "fief" or "leasehold" to describe the astrological "houses" through which a planet travels. 83. If one wishes to rightly investigate the birth or beginning of the stars, then one must properly know the birth of life—how life is born in a body—for it is all one and the same birth.

84. He who does not know and understand this also does not know the birth of the stars, for everything together is one body. Every creature, once life is born within it, has its subsequent birth standing in its body just like the birth of the natural body of this world; for all life must be born rightly according to the Godhead, just as the Godhead always bears itself.

85. When one rightly considers and ponders this—which cannot happen without the special enlightenment of the holy God—one finds initially the <term>harsh, cold, and severe birth<note>In Böhme's system, this represents the "First Principle": the dark, contracting force of desire that creates "mass" or "substance" out of nothingness.</note></term>, which is the cause of physical nature or the formation of a thing.

86. If this severe and cold, sharp contracting power did not exist, there would be no natural or physical being; likewise, the birth of God would not subsist, and everything would be unsearchable.

87. But in this hard, severe, and cold power stands the physical being or the body, wherein the spirit of life is born; and from that same spirit come the light and the understanding, through which the senses and the <term>approval<note>original: "Approbirung"; here meaning the testing, proving, or active manifestation of the various spiritual forces.</note></term> of all powers arise.

88. For when the light is born, it is born in the middle of the body as a heart or spirit from all the powers; and there it also stands still in its initial place and passes through all the powers.

89. For just as it is born out of all the powers and possesses the wellspring of all the powers, so it also brings with its

### ->Chapter 25. Rising Dawn.<-

Let the source-spring <note>original: "Quellbrun"; Böhme’s term for the living, flowing fountain-heads of divine energy.</note> of all powers shine into every power, from which taste and smell, as well as sight, feeling, and hearing arise, along with reason and understanding.

90. Now, just as the record and beginning of life is in a creature, so also is the first rebirth of the nature of the new life in the corrupted body of this world.

91. And whoever denies this has neither right understanding nor any knowledge of nature; furthermore, his knowledge is not born in **God**, but he is a mocker of **God**.

92. For see, you cannot deny that life in a creature arises in the heat of the heart, and in that same life stands also the light of the <term>animal birth<note>original: "animalische Geburt"; from the Latin "anima" (soul/life). Böhme refers to the biological manifestation of life in a physical body.</note></term>.

93. Now the heart signifies the Sun, which is also the beginning of life in the external body of this world: now you certainly cannot say that the animal birth deviates from the heart, because the body stands in mobility.

94. Thus the Sun also does not deviate from its seat, but keeps its own <term>place<note>original: "Locum"; Latin for place or position.</note></term> as a heart for itself, and shines as a light, or as a spirit of the entire body of this world, into all powers of the body.

95. For its birth is also originally from all powers; therefore, with its light and heat, it is also once again a spirit and heart in the whole body of this world.

96. Furthermore, you also cannot deny that the gall <note>original: "Galle"; in Böhme’s theosophy, the gall or bile represents the bitter, stirring, and aggressive quality of life that provides movement.</note> in a creature did not arise from the heart; for it has a vein to the heart and is the heart’s mobility, from which the heat arises.

97. It has its first origin from the flash of life, when life is born in the heart, and when the light rises in the water, then the <term>fire-shock<note>original: "Feuerschreck"; the sudden, terrifying eruption of energy that occurs when the dark, astringent forces of nature are ignited by light.</note></term> goes before it, which rises out of the anguish of the water in the heat.

98. So that when the heat in the cold in the bitter quality is thus in anguish, and the light is ignited through the hidden heaven of the heart in the physicality, then the anxious death in the wrath of **God** is startled, and retreats as a shock or flash from the light, and rises quite terribly, trembling and fearful above itself; and the heart’s light hurries after it and <term>infects<note>original: "inficiret"; here used in the archaic sense of "permeating" or "tempering" one quality with another.</note></term> it, and then it remains seated.

99. And that is and signifies the planet *Mars*, for that is how he also came to be, and his own quality is nothing else than a—

## Chapter 26.

### Concerning the Planet Saturn.

1. Saturn, the cold, sharp, and stern, harsh ruler, takes his beginning and origin not from the Sun; for he has in his power the chamber of death, and is a drier-up of all powers, from which physicality arises.

2. Just as the Sun is the heart of life, and an origin of all spirits in the body of this world, so Saturn is a beginner of all physicality and tangibility; and in the power of these two planets <note>Sun and Saturn represent the two poles of Böhme's cosmos: expansive life/light and contractive matter/darkness.</note> stands the whole body of this world, and no creature or formation, nor any mobility, can come to be in the natural body of this world outside the power of these two.

3. His origin, however, is the earnest, harsh, and stern anxiety <note>original: "Aengstlichkeit"; Böhme uses this term to describe a state of intense spiritual pressure or contraction that precedes the birth of matter.</note> of the whole body of this world; for when at the time of the kindling of the wrath, the light in the outermost birth of this world went out—which birth is naturalness or tangibility, or the rising up of the birth of all source-spirits <note>original: "Quellsgeister"; the fundamental qualities or forces of nature</note>—the harsh quality then stood in its sharpest and sternest birth, and contracted the workings of all source-spirits quite harshly and sternly. From this, then, the earth and stones have come to be, and it was truly the house of death, or the enclosure of life, wherein King Lucifer was then imprisoned.

For he has his own bodily property for himself, like a child when it is born from its mother.

### Chapter 26. The Dawn in the Rising.

Following this, secondly, the light became shining within the fat <note>In Böhme’s alchemy, "fat" or "oil" of the water refers to the combustible, life-giving essence that allows the spiritual light to burn</note> of the water within the heat; this is now the **Sun**.

28. 29. Thus, one first sees the glow, and from the glow the fire-crack, and after the fire-crack the power of the ignited body; then the light, along with the power of the body, suddenly raises itself above the crack and rules much higher, deeper, and more powerfully than the fire-crack itself.

30. Furthermore, the power of the ignited body—in the power that has gone out beyond the fire—acts gently, lovely, and intelligently; in this, one rightly understands the divine being. This is also the form and manner of the becoming of the Sun and the two planets **Mars** and **Jupiter**.

56. Now, however, in this dark valley <note>A common metaphor in Böhme’s work for the material, fallen world or the mortal condition of man</note>, there are the seven Spirits of God, which also have neither beginning nor end; for none is the first, and none is the second, third, or last.

57. The seven spirits also each give birth to the others from eternity to eternity.

58. The first regime stands in the body <note>original: "Corpus"</note> of all things—that is, in the entire Depth or the essence of all essences. In every end and place, it possesses the seven spirits within itself, essentially or characteristically, inseparably or immovably as its own property.

59. Now, if the seven spirits do not wrestle triumphantly <note>Böhme’s concept of "Ringen" (wrestling) refers to the dynamic, creative friction and interaction between the spiritual forces that generates life and light</note> in any given place, then there is no movement in that place, but rather a deep darkness. 60. Yet, the root of the seven spirits is at all ends; but outside of the "wrestling," it stands still, and no movement is perceived.

61. Such a house is the entire Depth outside, within, and above all heavens—which house is called Eternity. And such a house is also the house of flesh in humans and all creatures.

62. I mean this, however, in the house of the deep of this world, although the house of flesh and the deep all work together <note>original: *inqualiret* — Böhme's term for how different qualities or forces interact and penetrate one another</note> as one body, and it is indeed one body, only consisting of different parts or members.

### ->**The Deep in the Center.**<-

97. Behold, when the seed is now born, it stands in the middle of the body in the heart, for there the Mother of the Trinity begins.
98. First, the astringent <note>original: *herbe* — meaning harsh, sharp, or contracting</note> spirit begins; it draws a mass together out of the sweet water—that is, out of the fatness of the heart’s blood, or its sap, or the oil of the heart. This same oil already contains the root of the Trinity within it, just as the whole human being does; for it is just as if one threw tinder-fire into straw.

### ->**Now the question arises: How does this happen?**<-

99. Here is now the true ground of the human being; now mark this well, for it is the mirror of the Great Mystery <note>original: *Mysterium Magnum* — the hidden source of all existence</note>, the deep hiddenness of humanity. For this door, all the scholars of the world have danced and sought, yet they have not found it:
100. Now I must once again announce that it is the day-spring <note>original: *Morgenröte* — the dawn or the first light of wisdom</note> of the day, just as the gatekeeper desires it to be.

### ->**Now observe.**<-

109. In exactly this way, the first mass came to be. For the Spirit of Love in the Heart of God looked into the Water of Life within the body of the ignited, angry Father—from which and out of which love had risen in the lightning-flash of fire before the time of wrath.

In this vision, one spirit captured the other; the oil or water in the wrath received the love-spirit in the heart of God, and <term>inter-qualified</term> <note>original: "inqualiret"; Böhme's signature term for how different forces or qualities work within and through one another</note> with it, and the harsh spirit pulled the <term>mass</term> <note>original: "Massam"; the material substance from which the first human was formed</note> together. For at that very hour when Lucifer rose up, the Father became wrathful in the <term>source-spirits</term> <note>original: "Quellgeister"; the seven active qualities that animate all of nature</note> against the legions of Lucifer, and the Heart of God hid itself in the firmament of heaven; at that point, the <term>Salitter</term> <note>original: "Salitter"; a term Böhme uses for the divine mineral substance or "soil" of heaven</note> or the "working" of the physical body was already burning—for outside of the light is the dark chamber of death.

125. That was the seed of love; for one love received the other. According to this Son, man is the image of God.

134. 135. 136. Thus, in the comprehensibility of my present source-spirits, or also in the circle of life, I can recognize nothing other than that the day is dawning. 137. --- Page 400 ---
<meta>Continuing from the title page of Jacob Böhme’s "De Regeneratione" (1779 edition), this page provides a mystical explanation of the frontispiece illustration, setting the theological stage for the treatise on the "New Birth."</meta>

-> ### Explanation of the Frontispiece Regarding the New Birth. <-

**The** Cross <note>original: "+", a symbol Böhme uses to represent both Christ and the intersection of the divine and earthly planes</note> is the birth of all things, and the Cross is also the rebirth; yet to Reason <note>Böhme uses "Vernunft" (Reason) to describe human logic, which he believes is blind to spiritual truths</note> it is a folly and a strange, wondrous speech. This is because Reason, being born only of the stars and friendly sunshine, neither sees nor knows the eternal death that lies at its very root. But whoever feels the sting of that death becomes aware of the great distress, so that he must sigh anxiously with David: *Out of the depths I cry to you, O Lord.* For he sees that his will is corrupted, inclined toward sin and malice, and has turned away from God; therefore he cries out for the rebirth of a new will.

But no one sees or feels this death who does not search their own soul, nor ground their mind and behold the form of their will—observing who shapes and moves it, whether good or evil works within it, and which of the two has the upper hand.

For here is the bond of eternity, here is the greatest power; here either God or distress must be made manifest. Here the light must shine in joy through godly virtues, or the fire must torment and crucify the soul in hellish vices, in darkness and eternal death. For two contrary things cannot exist together: God and Mammon; Christ and Belial; the Lamb with the seven eyes and the Dragon with the seven heads. The enmity must be ended through reconciliation in obedience, or through eternal separation.

Therefore, God has placed the Cross <note>the "+" symbol</note> as the power of the Trinity <term>Dreyzahl: the Threefoldness or Trinity of God's nature</term> in the crucified Christ for the rebirth of a new, godly will in the Light, and for the separation of the evil will into the Darkness. This is so that we may work virtues in Him from the new birth as good fruits of the Holy Spirit—rather than [remaining in] vice and sin from the fleshly birth and evil works which stay in death and darkness. For where there is no good will, there the power remains in the darkness within the fire, and the soul has become a monstrous birth <note>original: "Mißgeburt", referring to a spiritual deformity or "mis-birth"</note> that can perform no good works.

Therefore, see how the Rebirth is taught in this little book through divine revelation.

-> Fore= <- <note>This "Fore=" is a catchword, indicating the next page begins with the word "Foreword."</note>

<summary>This page explains the symbolic frontispiece, framing the "New Birth" as a necessary escape from the corrupted human will and the "eternal death" hidden within nature. It establishes the central conflict between the Light (God/Christ) and Darkness (Mammon/the Dragon) within the human soul.</summary>
<keywords>Jacob Böhme, Rebirth, The Cross, Trinity, Reason vs. Revelation, Will, Spiritual Alchemy, Inner Conflict</keywords>

<meta>Continuing from the explanation of the frontispiece, this page begins the author’s formal preface. # ->The Author’s Preface.<-

**A**lthough I have sufficiently explained this in my other very deep writings and presented it from the Ground <note>original: "Grunde." For Böhme, the "Ground" or *Ungrund* refers to the absolute, underlying source of all existence—the divine essence before manifestation.</note>, yet because not everyone has such books in hand, nor is it within everyone’s grasp to understand them: Therefore, for the service of the simple children of Christ, and at the request of good friends, I have written a brief summary of the new rebirth, to see if anyone might wish to learn to know themselves through it.

2. But whoever desires to search for the Ground from which this flows, and has the gift of understanding, let him read the *Book of the Threefold Life of Man*; also the *Three Books on the Incarnation and Birth of Jesus Christ*; likewise the *Book of Six Points*; the *Great Mystery* <note>original: "Mysterio Magno," Böhme’s massive commentary on Genesis</note>; the *Book of the Three Worlds*, explaining how they exist within one another as one, yet make up three Principles <term>Principia: Böhme’s term for the three fundamental modes of reality: the dark world of fire/will, the light world of divine love, and the outer world of nature.</term>, that is, three births or beginnings, etc. Also the book *On the Three Principles* <note>original: "de Tribus Principiis"</note>: there he will find whatever he may ask, as high as a human mind can soar, as well as in the *Forty Questions of the Soul*.

3. This I have now written for the hungry and thirsty hearts following Christ’s fountain, as my fellow members in the Spirit of Christ. To the mockers, however, I have written nothing; for they have their own book within themselves, with which they drive the children of Christ under the Cross, and they must—against their own will—be the servants of Christ's children, even if they do not understand this.

## ->Of the New Rebirth.<-

### ->The First Chapter.<-

**C**hrist spoke: Unless you turn back and become like children, you shall not see the kingdom of God. And again in John 3:5, he says to Nicodemus <note>Nicodemus was a Pharisee and member of the Sanhedrin who visited Jesus by night to discuss his teachings.</note>: Unless someone is born anew of water and spirit, he cannot enter the kingdom of God. For what is born of the flesh is flesh, and what is born of the spirit is spirit. Scripture clearly testifies that the carnal, natural man perceives nothing of the Spirit of God: it is foolishness to him, and he cannot understand it.

2. Since we all possess flesh and blood and are moreover mortal, as is evident before our eyes, and yet Scripture also says that we are temples of the Holy Spirit who dwells within us: and that the kingdom of God is within us, and that Christ must take shape in us, and that he wishes to give us his flesh for food and his blood for drink. And further it says: He who will not eat the flesh of the Son of Man has no life in him: So we must earnestly consider what kind of person resides within us that is similar to and capable <note>The original term "fåhig" implies both the capacity to understand and the ability to contain or receive the divine presence.</note> of receiving the Godhead.

3. For concerning the mortal flesh, which turns to earth and lives in the vanity <note>In this context, "vanity" (Eitelkeit) refers to the 17th-century concept of "vanitas"—the transient, empty, and fleeting nature of the material world.</note> of this world, and

And this is the dry rod of Aaron <note>A biblical reference to Numbers 17, where Aaron’s staff miraculously sprouted, symbolizing the resurrection and the life-giving power of Christ.</note>, which turned green and bore almonds, and is the true High Priest <term>High Priest: A title for Christ as the ultimate mediator between God and humanity.</term>; and it is precisely that humanity of which Christ spoke in John 3: [saying] that He had come from heaven and was in heaven, and no man could come into heaven except the Son of Man, who had come from heaven and who was in heaven. In saying that He had come from heaven, He understands the heavenly essence, the heavenly corporality; for the power of God needs no "coming," as it is entirely unmeasured and undivided everywhere; but the essence requires coming; the power only needs to move and reveal itself within the essence.

->On the New Rebirth.<-

I.
# **A**lhier <note>original: "Alhier", meaning "here" or "in this place"</note> we now rightly understand our New Rebirth: how we can be and remain Temples of God; yet during this time, according to our outward humanity, remain also sinful mortal men. Christ has burst open and unlocked the gate of our inner, heavenly humanity—which was shut in Adam—within the human essence. It now depends solely on this: that the soul leads its will out of the vanity <note>In this context, "vanity" refers to the empty, fleeting nature of the material world.</note> of the corrupted flesh, and introduces it into this open gate in the Spirit of Christ.

2. There must be a great and powerful earnestness; not merely a learning and knowing, but a hunger and great thirst for Christ’s Spirit. For knowing alone is not faith; rather, the hunger and thirst for that which I desire—so that I represent <term>einbilde; to "in-form" or "image" oneself into a state</term> it to myself and, through this representation <term>Einbildung</term>, take hold of it and grasp it as my own—that is faith.

3. The soul must no longer desire vanity, but only the love of God in Christ Jesus.

2. This is also how it is to be understood in our Christianity: The children of history <note>original: "Historien Kinder"; those who possess a purely intellectual or historical knowledge of scripture without an inner spiritual transformation</note> are not heirs of Christ’s goods, but rather the legitimate children who are born anew from Christ’s Spirit. 3. This was a prototype <term>prototype: a pre-figuration or symbolic model</term> of the future of Christendom. For the promise of Christendom was made to Abraham; therefore, the prototype was immediately presented in the two brothers, Isaac and Ishmael, showing how Christendom would conduct itself, and how two kinds of people would be found within it: true Christians and mouth-Christians <note>original: "Maul-Christen"; those who are Christian in name or speech only</note>. 4. 7. For the right spirit does what is right. But if the will to act is present and yet the action does not follow, then the true person is held captive in vain lust, which restrains the action. Such a person is only a hypocrite, an Ishmaelite; he speaks one way and acts another, testifying that his mouth is a liar. For that which he teaches, he does not do himself, and he serves only the animalistic man in vanity.

-># On the New Rebirth.<-

8. Then if someone says: "I have the will, and would gladly do good, but I have earthly flesh <note>original: *irdisch Fleisch*; refers to the fallen, physical nature of humanity that resists spiritual impulses</note> that holds me back so that I cannot; however, I shall be saved by grace for the sake of Christ’s merit; for I certainly comfort myself with His suffering and merit; He will accept me out of grace without any merit of my own and forgive my sin"—such a person acts exactly like one who knew of a good food for his health but did not eat it, eating instead a poisonous one in its place, from which he became sick and died.

9. What does it help the soul to know the way to God and yet not want to walk it, but instead walk the path of error and fail to reach God? What does it help the soul to comfort itself with the divine childship <term>childship: (*Kindschaft*) the spiritual status and legal right of being a child of God</term> of Christ, His suffering and death, and to flatter itself, if it does not wish to enter into the birth of a child? That is, to be born as a true child out of Christ’s Spirit, out of His suffering, death, and resurrection? Certainly and truly, this tickling and flattering oneself with Christ’s merit, apart from the true, in-born childship, is false and a lie, no matter who teaches it.

10. This comforting belongs to the penitent sinner who is in the struggle against sin and God’s wrath, when temptations come and the devil besets the soul; there, the soul should wrap itself entirely in the life and death of Christ and in His merit.

11. Christ has indeed earned it alone; but He did not earn it as a "merit" in the sense of a wage given for a task, so that He might give us childship from the outside as a gift of His merit and thus adopt us into childship. No, He Himself is the merit; He is the open gate through death, and we must enter through it. He does not, however, take animals <note>original: *Thiere*; a common mystical metaphor for people who live according to their unrefined, worldly instincts rather than the Spirit</note> into His merit, but rather those who turn back and become as children.

12. Those same children who come to Him are His earned reward. For He also spoke thus: "Father, the

"People were yours, and you have given them to me, and I give them eternal life." <note>A paraphrase of John 17:6 and 17:2.</note> Now, however, the life of Christ is given to no one unless he enters into it in the Spirit of Christ—into his humanity, suffering, and merit—and is born as a true child of merit within that merit. The child-like essence walks in heaven, and heaven is within the person. But if heaven is not open within the person, and he only stands before heaven acting the hypocrite, saying: "I am still outside, but Christ will take me in by grace; his merit is indeed mine"—such a person, according to the outer man, exists in vanity and sin, and with his soul in hell, as if in God's wrath.

14. Therefore, learn to understand rightly what Christ has taught and done for us. He is our heaven; he must take a shape within us if we are to be in heaven. Thus, the inner "soul-man" is in heaven with the holy body of Christ, as in the new birth, while the outer mortal man is in the world. Of this Christ says: "My sheep are in my hand, no one can snatch them out of it; the Father who gave them to me is greater than all." <note>John 10:28-29</note>

-># Of the New Rebirth.<-

...but from our little pearl <note>original: "Perlein," a favorite term of Böhme referring to the "pearl of great price" or the divine spark hidden within the soul</note>, from Christian essence and spiritual knowledge <term>knowledge: the original "Wissenschaft" here refers to an experiential, mystical understanding rather than academic study</term>, not from the husk <note>Böhme uses "husk" (Hülse) to describe the outward, formal shell of religion</note> and historical accounts, but from a childlike spirit, from the knowledge of Christ, as a branch on the vine of Christ, from the measure of that knowledge opened within us in God's counsel.

2. Now, we are tied to historical accounts, to stone churches, which would indeed be good in their value if one also brought the temple of Christ into them.

3. It is taught that their absolution <term>absolution: the formal release from guilt or sin by a priest</term> is a forgiveness of sins; likewise, that the Lord’s Supper takes away sins; likewise, that the Spirit of God is poured in through the office of preaching.

4. All of this would have its place if it were explained correctly, and if one did not merely cling to the husk. Many a person goes to church for 20 or 30 years, hears preaching, uses the sacrament, receives absolution, and is just as much a beast of the devil and of vanity as the next: A beast goes into the churches and to the Lord’s Supper, and a beast comes away from it again. How can he eat who has no mouth? How can he hear who has no hearing? Can someone enjoy a food that is locked away from his mouth? How can he drink who is far from the water? What does it help me that I go into the walled church and fill my ears with an empty breath? Or go to the Lord’s Supper and feed only the earthly mouth, which is mortal and perishable? I might as well give him a piece of bread at home so that he is full. How does that help the soul, which is an immortal life, if the animal-man <note>Böhme distinguishes between the "animal" or "soulish" man (the natural, unregenerate human) and the "new man" in Christ</note> keeps the outward form of Christ's usage, yet the soul cannot reach the jewel of that usage? For Saint Paul says of the Lord’s Supper: *Therefore, because you do not discern the Lord’s body, you receive it unto judgment.* <note>original: "Darum, daß ihr nicht unterscheidet den Leib des Herrn, empfahet ihrs zum Gerichte" — a reference to 1 Corinthians 11:29</note>

5. The covenant stands; it is proven in its use; Christ offers us His Spirit in His word, as in the preached word, and in the sacraments His body and blood, and in brotherly reconciliation His absolution.

-># The Sixth Chapter.<-

6. What good does it do, however, if a beast <note>original: "Thier"; Böhme uses this term to describe the carnal, earthly nature of man that lacks spiritual life</note> listens there, yet has no hearing for the inner living Word? Because the Word finds no place in their hearing where it might take hold.

7. He who says such a thing to a closed-off sinner is in error, and he who accepts it without God's voice within him also deceives himself.

8. No one can forgive sin except God alone; the preacher's mouth does not have forgiveness in its own power. The Spirit of Christ has it within the voice of the priest's mouth, provided that he is also a true Christian. But what did it benefit those who heard Christ teaching on earth, when He spoke: *Come to me, all you who are weary and burdened, and I will give you rest*? <note>A reference to Matthew 11:28</note> What did it benefit those who heard it, but were not weary? Where would the refreshment remain? Since they had dead ears and only heard the external Christ, but not the Word of divine power, they were not refreshed. Just as little benefit does a beast-like man receive from his hypocritical absolution; so also do the **sacraments** <note>original: "Sacramenta," referring to holy rituals like the Lord's Supper</note> benefit him.

9. In the sacraments it is now clear, as it is in the office of teaching. The covenant <term>covenant: the "Bund," or the spiritual agreement between God and humanity</term> is proclaimed; the soul’s partaking occurs, but in the same quality as the soul's "mouth" is. It receives the essence of the eternal world, but according to the quality of the dark world. As the mouth is, so also is the food that belongs in the mouth. 12. But if there is any stubble or straw in the sermon, he sucks vanity from it, and the soul sucks from it the false poison and the murder of the devil; with this, she tickles herself by hearing how she can judge other people. But if the preacher is also a "dead" man, and sows poison and shame out of his own passions <term>passions: the original "Affecten" refers to uncontrolled worldly emotions or biased impulses rather than spiritual inspiration</term>, then the devil teaches and the devil hears. This same teaching is caught in the godless heart and brings forth godless fruits, through which the world has become a murder-den of the devil; so that in both the teacher and the listener, there is nothing within but vain mocking, blaspheming, scorning, word-wrangling, and biting at the husk <note>To "bite at the husk" means to argue over external forms, literal meanings, or trivialities while missing the internal "kernel" of spiritual truth.</note>.

->### The Sixth Chapter.<-

13. But in the holy teacher, the Holy Spirit teaches, and in the holy listener, the Spirit of Christ hears through the soul and the divine housing of the divine treasure. The holy person has his church within himself, where he hears and teaches inwardly. But Babel <note>original: "Babel" - a reference to the Tower of Babel, used here to signify the confusion and hypocrisy of organized religious institutions that focus only on external forms.</note> has a heap of stones, where she goes in to practice hypocrisy and to shine; she lets herself be seen in beautiful clothes and pretends to be devout and pious; the stone church is her god, in which she puts her trust.

14. The holy person, however, has his church with him and in him at all places: For whether he stands or walks, lies down or sits, he is in his church; he is in the true Christian church, in the temple of Christ. The Holy Spirit preaches to him from all creatures; everything he looks upon, there he sees a preacher of God.

15. Here the scoffer will say that I despise the stone church where the congregation gathers. To that I say: No. Rather, I point to the hypocritical Babylonian Whore <note>A common Reformation-era metaphor for a corrupt church, derived from the "Whore of Babylon" in the Book of Revelation.</note>, who only practices harlotry with the stone church and calls herself a Christian, but is a brat of a whore <term>Hurenbalg: literally "whore's brat" or "bastard"; used here as a sharp insult for one who is a product of false, hypocritical faith rather than spiritual rebirth.</term>.

16. A true Christian brings his holy church with him into the congregation: His heart is the true church, where one should practice divine service. If I were to go to church for a thousand years, and to the sacrament <note>Refers to the Lord's Supper or Eucharist.</note> every week, and even if I let myself be absolved every day; if I do not have Christ within me, it is all false, and a useless trifle, a mere wood-carving in Babel, and there is no forgiveness of sins.

17. The holy person performs holy works from the holy power of his mind <term>Gemüthes: the "Gemüth" is a central concept in German mysticism, referring to the seat of the soul's disposition, will, and emotions—the deepest part of the inner self.</term>. The work is not the reconciliation itself; rather, it is the building that the true spirit builds within its essence <note>original: "Wesen" — referring to the fundamental nature or being of the soul.</note>. It is his dwelling-place, just as the false Christian’s fables are his dwelling-place, where his soul then goes to practice hypocrisy. External hearing goes into the external and works in the external; and internal hearing goes into the internal and works in the internal.

->I.<-

**A** true human being, who is reborn in the Spirit of Christ, exists in the simplicity of Christ and has no quarrel with anyone over religion. He has enough struggle within himself against his animal, evil flesh and blood; he considers himself always a great sinner and stands in awe before God, for his sins are laid bare and stand in judgment; for the <term>Turba</term><note>original: "Turba." 2. But for the godless, his sins rest in the sleep of death; they sprout up from the abyss and bring forth fruit in hell.

3. Christendom in Babylon quarrels over <term>knowledge</term><note>original: "Wissenschaft." And they poorly teach that whoever does not agree with them in every point of doctrine and opinion is no Christian, but a <term>heretic</term><note>original: "Ketzer."</note>.

# ->The 8th Chapter.<-

->**1.**<-

**T**he whole Christian religion consists in this: that we learn to recognize ourselves—what we are, from whence we have come, how we have entered from unity into disunity, wickedness, and injustice, and how we have awakened these things within ourselves. Secondly: where we were when we were in unity, when we were children of God. Thirdly: how we are now in disunity, in conflict and reluctance. Fourthly: where we are journeying to out of this fragile being: where we intend to go with the immortal part of us, and also with the mortal.

**2.** In these four points stands our whole religion—to learn to come out of disunity and vanity, and to enter again into the <term>One Tree</term> <note>A metaphor for the collective spiritual body of humanity restored to its original state.</note> from which we all came in <term>Adam</term>, which is Christ within us. We need not strive for anything, nor do we have any conflict; let each person only practice how he may enter again into the love of God and of his brother.

**3.** Christ’s testaments are absolutely nothing other than a brotherly covenant: that God binds Himself with us in Christ, and we in Him. All teaching should lead toward this, as well as all willing, living, and doing. Whatever teaches and does otherwise is <term>Babel</term> <note>original: "Babel". This refers to the Tower of Babel, symbolizing the confusion of sects and the "empty talk" of institutionalized religion that lacks spiritual power.</note> and a fable; it is merely a carving <note>original: "Schnizwerk". Refers to something artificial, human-made, or "hand-crafted" by the ego rather than grown by God.</note> of pride, a useless judgment, and a confusing <margin>of the</margin>

of the world, a hypocrisy of the devil, with which he blinds the simple-minded.

**4.** All that teaches outside of God’s Spirit, and lacks divine recognition <note>original: *Erkäntniß*; a deep, experiential knowledge rather than just facts</note>, yet sets itself up as a teacher in God’s kingdom and wishes to serve God with teaching, is false. Such a person serves only his idol-belly <note>A common Reformation-era term for someone motivated by physical appetite or greed rather than spiritual truth</note> and his proud, haughty mind, desiring to be honored and called holy. He holds an office chosen by the children of men, who merely flatter him and have appointed him for the sake of favor. Christ spoke: *He who does not enter by the door into the sheepfold is a thief and a murderer, and the sheep do not follow him, for they do not know his voice.*

**5.** He does not have the voice of the Spirit of God, but only the voice of his own art and his learning; he teaches, and not God’s Spirit. But Christ says: *Every plant which my heavenly Father has not planted shall be rooted out.* How then shall he plant heavenly plants who is godless, since he has no seed within himself in his own power? Christ says plainly: *The sheep do not hear his voice; they do not follow him.*

**6.** The written word is only a tool that the Spirit guides: the Word that seeks to teach must be alive within the literal word. The Spirit of God must be in the literal sound <note>original: *Halle*; meaning the resonance or echo of the spoken/written word</note>; otherwise, no one is a teacher of God, but only a teacher of letters, a knower of histories <note>meaning factual or chronological knowledge without spiritual life</note>, and not of the Spirit of God in Christ. Everything with which one wishes to serve God must happen in faith—that is, in the Spirit—which makes the work complete and acceptable before God. What a person begins and does in faith, he does in the Spirit of God, who works together in the deed; that is pleasing to God, for He has made it Himself, and His power is within it; it is holy.

**7.** But whatever is done in the selfhood <note>original: *Selbheit*; the state of being focused on one's own ego or self-will apart from God</note> without faith is only a figure or a shell of a true Christian work.

**8.** If you serve your brother and do it only out of hypocrisy, and give to him unwillingly, then you do not serve God. For your faith does not proceed out of love into the hope of your gift. You may indeed serve your brother, and he for his part thanks God and also for his part blesses you; but you do not bless him, for you give to him with a grud-
[[margin: ging]] <note>The word is split across the page: *mur-* on the main page and *-rischen* in the margin, meaning 'grudging' or 'muttering.'</note>

<summary>This page argues that true spiritual teaching and Christian works must come from the Holy Spirit and internal faith, rather than intellectual learning or ego. It warns that those who teach without divine inspiration are "thieves and murderers" who serve their own pride.</summary>

<keywords>Rebirth, Holy Spirit, False Teachers, Faith, Selfhood, Literal Word vs. Living Word, Hypocrisy</keywords>

Page 47 begins by applying this principle to the act of giving and the office of teaching.</meta>

## ->Chapter Eight.<-

[...earthly] spirit <note>The text likely begins with "earthly" (*irdischen*), completing a sentence from the previous page</note> into your gift, it does not enter into God’s Spirit or into the hope of faith; therefore, your gift is only half-given, and you have only half a reward for it.

**9.** This is also to be understood regarding receiving: If someone gives in faith and divine hope, he blesses his gifts through his faith. But he who receives them ungratefully and murmurs in his spirit, curses them in the enjoyment of them. Thus, to each remains his own; what he sows, that shall he also reap.

**10.** So it is also in the <term>teaching office</term> <note>original: *Lehramt*; referring to the official role of a minister or preacher</note>: What a person sows, that shall he also reap. If one sows good seed from the Spirit of Christ, it takes root in a good heart and bears good fruit. But in the godless, who are not capable of receiving it, the <term>wrath of God</term> is stirred up. If one sows strife, contempt, and misinterpretation, all godless people take that in; it also takes root and bears such fruit that people mock, deride, slander, and misinterpret one another.

**11.** From these things the great <term>Babel</term> <note>In this context, "Babel" represents the "City of Confusion"—the fragmented, worldly, and prideful state of institutional churches that fight over dogmas rather than living in the Spirit</note> is born and has grown up. Out of <term>pride</term> <note>original: *Hoffart*; a haughty or arrogant pride</note>, people quarrel over the "history" <note>original: *Historie*; referring to "historical faith," or believing the Bible as a mere list of facts rather than a living experience</note> and the justification of the poor <term>sinner</term> before God. They lead the simple-minded astray and make them blasphemous, so that one brother despises another for the sake of "history" and the exchange of letters, and gives him over to the devil.

**12.** Such <term>slanderous spirits</term> <note>original: *Lästerbälge*; literally "slander-bellows," implying they puff out insults like a bellows puffs air</note> do not serve God, but rather the great building of disunity. Because a corrupted lust still lies within the earthly flesh of all men, they awaken this abomination even in the simple children of God. They make God’s people, along with the children of wickedness, into blasphemers. They are merely master builders of the great Babel and the world, and are as useful as a fifth wheel on a wagon—except that they help erect the structure of hell.

**13.** Therefore, it is highly necessary for the children of God to pray earnestly and learn to recognize this false building. They must withdraw their minds from it and not help to build it up themselves, nor persecute the children of God, lest they be delayed and led astray regarding the Kingdom of God. As Christ spoke to the <term>Pharisees</term>: *Woe to you, Pharisees! You travel over land and sea to make a single <term>convert</term> <note>original: *Judengenossen*; a proselyte to Judaism</note>, and when he has become one, you make him twice as much a child of hell as yourselves.* This truly happens today among the current <term>factions and sects</term>, and among the loud-mouths and <term>quarrelsome teachers</term>.
<margin>14. Because</margin>

<summary>This page warns that religious actions and teachings performed without the Holy Spirit result in "Babel," a state of spiritual confusion and sectarian strife. It critiques those who prioritize "historical" facts and dogmatic arguments over brotherly love and spiritual rebirth.</summary>

<keywords>Babel, spiritual giving, teaching office, sowing and reaping, religious strife, Pharisees, sectarianism, justification, pride, historical faith</keywords>

--- Page 444 ---
<meta>Concluding the eighth chapter, continuing the discussion on avoiding religious discord (referred to as the "great Babel" on the previous page) and living a life of simple Christian love.</meta>

## ->Concerning the New Rebirth.<-

**14.** Therefore, all the children of God, who intend to be members of Christ <term>members of Christ: a biblical concept where believers are seen as individual parts of the spiritual body of Jesus</term>, have been faithfully warned through the gifts opened to me by God against such loathsome strife and bloody conflict <note>original: *Blutpaucken*—a term often used in this era to describe the "thumping" of war drums or the violent agitation of religious persecution</note>, to depart from the discord between brothers and to strive simply <note>original: *schlecht*, meaning plainly or simply in this context</note> for love and righteousness toward all people.

**15.** For if one is a good tree, then he shall also bear good fruit. Although he must sometimes suffer the swine <note>A common metaphor in the 17th century for those who do not value spiritual things</note> devouring his fruit, he should nonetheless remain a good tree and always desire to work alongside God, refusing to be overcome by any evil. Thus he stands in God’s field <term>God's field: a metaphor for the world or the community of believers where spiritual growth occurs</term> and bears fruit for God’s table, which he shall enjoy eternally. Amen.

->T H E  E N D.<-

<summary>This concluding section of the chapter exhorts believers to abandon religious infighting in favor of simple love and righteousness, using the metaphor of a good tree that continues to produce fruit despite external persecution.</summary>
